relevance_reason: Large genetic association study showing that copy number variation of complement C4A and C4B at the MHC locus drives SLE risk independently of HLA-DRB1*03:01, with stronger effects in men; this is susceptibility evidence for the SLE entry.

findings.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) built a multi-ancestry reference panel of 2,530 haplotypes from whole-genome sequencing of 1,265 individuals. They used it to impute C4A and C4B gene copy number into ImmunoChip data from 6,748 SLE cases and 11,516 controls of European ancestry. Across the 11 most common combinations of C4A and C4B copy number, relative risk of SLE varied 7-fold. Each copy of C4A was protective (OR 0.54), equivalent to 2.3 copies of C4B (OR 0.77).
quotes: Groups of research participants with the eleven most common combinations of C4A and C4B gene copy number exhibited 7-fold variation in their relative risk of SLE
Logistic-regression analysis estimated that the protection afforded by each copy of C4A (OR: 0.54; 95% CI: [0.51, 0.57]) was equivalent to that of 2.3 copies of C4B (OR: 0.77; 95% CI: [0.71,0.82]).
We then analyzed SNP data from the largest SLE genetic association study (ImmunoChip 6,748 SLE cases and 11,516 controls of European ancestry)

findings.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) analyzed SLE risk for individual C4 alleles and their flanking SNP haplotypes. They concluded that C4A gives strong protection and C4B more modest protection against SLE, and that the C4 genes themselves, rather than nearby variants, are the main drivers of risk. The C4-B(S) allele, which lacks any C4A gene, was the highest-risk C4 allele.
quotes: Analysis of SLE risk in relation to each of these C4 alleles and SNP haplotypes reinforced the conclusion that C4A contributes strong protection, and C4B more modest protection, from SLE, and that C4 genes (rather than nearby variants) are the principal drivers of this variation in risk levels
DRB1*03:01 is in strong LD (r2 = 0.71) with the common C4-B(S) allele, which lacks any C4A gene and is the highest-risk C4 allele in our analysis

findings.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) studied an African American cohort of 1,494 SLE cases and 5,908 controls, in which LD between C4-B(S) and HLA-DRB1*03:01 is low (r2 = 0.10). A joint association analysis implicated C4A (p < 10(-14)) and C4B (p < 10(-5)) but not DRB1*03:01 (p = 0.29). C4-B(S) alleles increased SLE risk regardless of DRB1*03:01 status. Each C4 allele had a similar effect size in Europeans and African Americans.
quotes: Among African Americans, we found that common C4 alleles exhibited far less LD with HLA alleles; in particular, the LD between C4-B(S) and DRB1*03:01 was low (r2 = 0.10)
Joint association analysis of C4A, C4B, and DRB1*0301 implicated C4A (p < 10−14) and C4B (p < 10−5) but not DRB1*0301 (p = 0.29)
C4-B(S) alleles consistently increased SLE risk regardless of DRB1*03:01 status, whereas DRB1*03:01 had no consistent effect when controlling for C4-B(S)

findings.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) jointly analyzed the European and African American SLE cohorts while accounting for C4 alleles. This identified a more modest genetic effect independent of C4, tagged by rs2105898 and rs9271513. It appeared to involve noncoding variation in the HLA class II XL9 region that is associated with expression levels of many HLA class II genes.
quotes: Accounting for C4 alleles in jointly analyzing the SLE association data from African American and European ancestry cohorts also enabled the mapping of an additional, more-modest genetic effect independent of C4; this effect (tagged by rs2105898 and rs9271513) appeared to involve noncoding variation in the HLA class II XL9 region

findings.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) found that C4 alleles had stronger effects on SLE risk in men than in women. A sex-by-C4 interaction term was significant (p = 0.002). Common combinations of C4A and C4B produced 14-fold variation in SLE risk among men versus 6-fold among women.
quotes: When a sex-by-C4 interaction term was included in association analyses, this term was significant for both SLE (p = 0.002) and schizophrenia (p = 0.0024), with larger C4 effects in men for both disorders.

common combinations of C4A and C4B generated 14-fold variation in risk for SLE, 31-fold variation in risk for Sjögren's syndrome, and 1.7-fold variation in schizophrenia risk among men (versus 6-fold, 15-fold and 1.26-fold variation in risk among women, respectively)

findings.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) measured complement in CSF from 589 adults. Per C4 gene copy, men had on average 27% more C4 protein than women, and C3 levels were 42% higher in men. Plasma data showed the sex difference was most pronounced at ages 20 to 50 years, which matches the ages of differential disease vulnerability. The authors suggested that sex differences in complement levels may help explain why women have a greater risk of SLE.
quotes: CSF from adult men contained on average 27% more C4 protein per C4 gene copy than CSF from women (meta-analysis p = 9.9 × 10−6, Fig. 3c).
CSF levels of C3 protein were also on average 42% higher among men than women (meta-analysis p = 7.5 × 10−7, Fig. 3d).

Sex differences in complement protein levels may help to explain the more potent effects of C4 alleles in men, women's greater risk of SLE and Sjögren's syndrome and men's greater vulnerability to schizophrenia.

findings.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) proposed that higher C4 protein levels may attenuate interactions between the adaptive immune system and ribonuclear self-antigens at sites of cell injury, because complement speeds clearance of debris from dead cells, and that this could pre-empt the development of autoimmunity. They noted that the same C4 alleles that increase vulnerability to schizophrenia appeared to protect strongly against SLE.
quotes: elevated levels of C4 protein likely attenuate interactions between the adaptive immune system and ribonuclear self-antigens at sites of cell injury, pre-empting the development of autoimmunity.
The same C4 alleles that increase vulnerability to schizophrenia appeared to protect strongly against SLE and SjS.

relevance_reason: Reports a rare MEF2D regulatory variant associated with SLE and a Raynaud/anti-RNP/anti-Sm sub-phenotype in Swedish cohorts, with functional studies; a susceptibility locus finding for the SLE entry.

findings.statement: Farias et al. (2019) performed targeted resequencing of coding and conserved regulatory regions in and around 215 candidate genes in pooled DNA from 140 SLE patients and 17 Swedish controls. They identified a rare variant, rs200395694:G>T (hg19 chr1:g.156450591G>T), in intron 4 of the MEF2D gene that was associated with SLE in Swedish cohorts. The combined cohorts had 12 heterozygotes among 504 patients and 6 among 839 controls (allele frequency 0.011 vs 0.003; p = 0.014). The allele frequency was 0.001 in 1000 Genomes and 0.002 in SweFreq, and no homozygotes were reported.
quotes: we identified a rare regulatory variant rs200395694:G > T located in intron 4 of the MEF2D gene encoding the myocyte-specific enhancer factor 2D transcription factor and associated with SLE in Swedish cohorts (504 SLE patients and 839 healthy controls, p = 0.014, CI = 1.1-10)
There were in total 12 heterozygotes out of 504 patients and 6 heterozygotes out of 839 controls giving an allele frequency of 0.011 and 0.003, respectively.
the allele frequency in 1000G project is 0.001

findings.statement: Among 140 Swedish SLE patients with clinical data, Farias et al. (2019) found that all 3 carriers of the MEF2D rs200395694 risk allele (2 females, 1 male) had anti-Sm antibodies, anti-RNP antibodies, and Raynaud phenomenon. This triad was present in 8.7% of all patients, and its association with the variant was significant (p = 0.00037). Associations with anti-Sm alone (p = 0.0058) and anti-RNP alone (p = 0.017) were nominally significant.
quotes: all three individuals carrying the MEF2D rs200395694-A allele were positive for these three phenotypes, as compared to 11 individuals (8.5%) of all the patients, with a significant association between this triad of disease manifestations and the rs200395694-A allele (p = 0.00037; Fisher’s exact test)
We observed a nominally significant association between the MEF2D rs200395694-A allele and presence of anti-Sm antibodies (p = 0.0058) and anti-RNP antibodies (p = 0.017) with Fisher’s exact test.

findings.statement: Farias et al. (2019) found that the MEF2D rs200395694 region carries marks of a cell type-specific enhancer that is active in T, B, NK cells, and monocytes. In EMSA, the alleles differed in protein binding in Jurkat and Daudi nuclear extracts. In luciferase assays, the alternative A allele increased expression in unstimulated Jurkat (1.3-fold) and K562 (1.8-fold) cells but suppressed expression in THP-1 cells. In minigene assays, the risk allele significantly repressed splicing of the alternative tissue-specific alpha-2 isoform in all cell lines tested without affecting the alpha-1 isoform. The authors suggested that this could change the set of target genes regulated by alpha-2, which includes DNASE1L3 and AIM2.
quotes: We observed differential protein-binding between the reference and the alternative allele in nuclear extracts from both cell lines
the alternative A allele induced expression in non-stimulated Jurkat (1.3-fold, p = 0.02) and K562 cells (1.8-fold, p = 0.0001) compared to the reference C allele
The alternative isoform α2 generated from the minigene with the rare A allele was significantly repressed in all tested cells.

relevance_reason: Mouse model and human postmortem study showing that type I IFN drives microglia-dependent synapse loss in CNS lupus; this adds to understanding of how SLE causes disease.

findings.statement: Bialas et al. (2017) reported behavioral phenotypes and synapse loss in lupus-prone mice. Blocking type I interferon (IFN) signaling prevented both. Type I IFN stimulated microglia to become reactive and to engulf neuronal and synaptic material in these mice.
quotes: Here we report behavioural phenotypes and synapse loss in lupus-prone mice that are prevented by blocking type I interferon (IFN) signalling.
we show that type I IFN stimulates microglia to become reactive and engulf neuronal and synaptic material in lupus-prone mice

findings.statement: Bialas et al. (2017) observed increased type I IFN signaling in postmortem hippocampal brain sections from patients with SLE. They suggested that IFN-driven, microglia-dependent synapse loss may explain the neurologic symptoms seen in some patients with SLE (CNS lupus).
quotes: our observation of increased type I IFN signalling in post-mortem hippocampal brain sections from patients with SLE

identification of IFN-driven microglia-dependent synapse loss, along with microglia transcriptome data, connects CNS lupus with other CNS diseases and provides an explanation for the neurological symptoms observed in some patients with SLE

findings.statement: Bialas et al. (2017) noted that up to 75% of patients with SLE have neuropsychiatric symptoms, collectively called CNS lupus. These range from anxiety, depression and cognitive impairment to seizures and, rarely, psychosis. CNS lupus typically presents at diagnosis or within the first year.
quotes: up to 75% of patients with SLE experience neuropsychiatric symptoms that range from anxiety, depression and cognitive impairment to seizures and, in rare cases, psychosis-collectively this is referred to as central nervous system (CNS) lupus
CNS lupus typically presents at lupus diagnosis or within the first year

relevance_reason: Identifies NCF1 p.Arg90His and NCF1 copy number variation as SLE susceptibility factors in multiple ancestries.

findings.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) genotyped SLE cases and controls of Chinese, European American, and African American ancestry with the Immunochip. In Chinese, the strongest association was at rs73366469 in the GTF2IRD1-GTF2I intergenic region on 7q11.23 (P = 3.8 x 10(-29), OR = 2.88). The association was confirmed at a modest level in European Americans but not in African Americans. A non-Immunochip SNP, rs117026326 in intron 9 of GTF2I, showed stronger association and accounted for the rs73366469 signal.
quotes: In Chinese, the strongest association signal was detected at rs73366469 (minor allele frequency of 28.7% in cases versus 12.6% in controls, P=3.8×10−29, OR=2.88) within the GTF2IRD1-GTF2I intergenic region at 7q11.23
This association was confirmed in European Americans at a modest significance level (P=7.5×10−3, OR=1.32), but not in African Americans
rs117026326, located in intron 9 of GTF2I, exhibited stronger association with SLE (Pmeta Chinese=4.4×10−40, OR=2.94; Pmeta EurAm=1.2×10−4, OR=2.83

findings.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) used NCF1-specific PCR and Sanger sequencing to resequence the 15.5-kb NCF1 region in 45 Chinese subjects, which was needed to distinguish NCF1 from its pseudogenes NCF1B and NCF1C. They identified a missense variant in NCF1 (g.74779296G>A; p.Arg90His, rs201802880) as the likely causal variant behind the 7q11.23 SLE association. The risk allele was associated with SLE in African Americans (15.7% vs 8.3%, OR = 2.02), in Asians (meta-analysis of Chinese and Korean datasets, P = 3.1 x 10(-104), OR = 3.47), and in European Americans (meta P = 1.9 x 10(-7), OR = 2.61). Conditioning on p.Arg90His eliminated the signals at p.Ser99Gly and in the GTF2IRD1-GTF2I region.
quotes: Here we report a missense variant (g.74779296G>A; p.Arg90His) in NCF1, encoding the p47phox subunit of the phagocyte NADPH oxidase (NOX2), as the putative underlying causal variant
Of the variants, only p.Arg90His was associated with SLE (15.7% versus 8.3%, P=2.9×10−5, OR=2.02, Table 1 and Supplementary Table 5).
findings.population: Chinese; Korean; European American; African American

findings.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) found that the NCF1 p.Arg90His risk allele was associated with earlier age of SLE onset in a dose-dependent manner in Korean and European American patients.
quotes: the allele encoding p.Arg90Hiswas dose dependently associated with early age of onset in Korean and European-American patients with SLE

findings.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) found that NCF1 p.Arg90His was also associated with primary Sjogren syndrome in Chinese (OR = 2.45) and European Americans (OR = 2.35). It was also associated with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis in Koreans (OR = 1.65), with a modest effect size.
quotes: p.Arg90His was associated with other autoimmune diseases, including primary Sjögren’s syndrome ([MIM 270150]) in Chinese (37.8% versus 18.3%, P=7.2×10−17, OR=2.45) and European Americans (4.8% versus 2.2%, P=9.7×10−4, OR=2.35)
seropositive rheumatoid arthritis ([MIM 180300]) in Koreans (26.6% versus 18.1%, P=2.5×10−8, OR=1.65, Table 1 and Supplementary Table 8) but with a modest effect size

findings.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) assessed NCF1 copy number variation using the deltaGT/GTGT ratio. Having one copy of NCF1 was associated with increased SLE risk in Koreans, Chinese, and European Americans (P = 5.9 x 10(-4), OR = 3.91). Having 3 or more copies was protective in Koreans, Chinese, European Americans, and African Americans. The authors concluded that this supports reduced ROS production as a risk factor for SLE.
quotes: One copy of NCF1 (5:1 ratio) was associated with increased risk of SLE in Koreans (P=0.032), Chinese (P=0.011) and European Americans (P=5.9×10−4, OR=3.91, Supplementary Table 9).

In contrast, having ≥3 copies of NCF1 (3:3 and 2:4 ratios) was protective against developing SLE in Koreans (P=3.7×10−5), Chinese (P=2.8×10−3, OR=0.28), European Americans (P=0.038, OR=0.85) and African Americans (P=0.018, OR=0.73).
findings.population: Korean; Chinese; European American; African American

findings.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) noted that Arg90 of p47phox lies in a phosphoinositide-binding pocket of the PX domain and is critical for p47phox membrane translocation and NOX2 activation. Prior in vitro mutation studies indicated that the Arg90His change reduces ROS production. The authors suggested that p.Arg90His confers SLE risk by reducing NOX2-derived ROS levels. However, the genotype was not associated with intracellular ROS levels in neutrophils from controls, and rs117026326 genotype was not associated with NCF1 transcript levels.
quotes: These data suggested that p.Arg90His might confer risk for SLE by reducing NOX2-derived ROS levels.
However, p.Arg90Hiswas not associated with intracellular ROS levels in neutrophils from controls (Supplementary Fig.5), probably because of the impact of mitochondrial ROS.

Arg90 of p47phox, located in a phosphoinositide-binding pocket of the PX domain, has a crucial role in the membrane translocation of cytosolic p47phox and resultant activation of NOX2 for ROS production.

relevance_reason: This mouse study identifies a promoter polymorphism in the NZB gene for EAT-2 (SH2D1B) as a lupus-susceptibility allele and shows how it works in dendritic cells. That makes it animal-model and functional evidence for SLE, not a report of human patients.

findings.statement: Talaei et al. (2015) studied C57BL/6 congenic mice carrying a homozygous NZB chromosome 1 interval from 70 to 100 cM. These mice develop high-titer antinuclear antibodies and severe glomerulonephritis. Using subcongenic mice, the authors found that a locus in the 88-96 cM region was associated with altered dendritic cell (DC) function. This locus synergized with T-cell defects to promote expansion of pathogenic proinflammatory T-cell subsets.
quotes: C57BL/6 congenic mice with an introgressed homozygous 70 cM (125.6 Mb) to 100 cM (179.8 Mb) interval on c1 from the lupus-prone New Zealand Black (NZB) mouse develop high titers of antinuclear Abs and severe glomerulonephritis

a genetic locus in the 88-96 cM region was associated with altered dendritic cell (DC) function and synergized with T cell functional defects to promote expansion of pathogenic proinflammatory T cell subsets

findings.statement: Talaei et al. (2015) found that the promoter region of the NZB gene encoding EWS-activated transcript 2 (EAT-2), an adapter in the SLAM signaling pathway, is polymorphic. This polymorphism reduced EAT-2 levels in dendritic cells by about 70%. Silencing EAT-2 in DCs lacking the polymorphism increased IL-12 production and enhanced Th1 differentiation in T cell-DC cocultures. This reproduced the phenotype of DCs from congenic mice carrying the NZB chromosome 1 70-100 cM interval.
quotes: the promoter region of the NZB gene encoding the SLAM signaling pathway adapter molecule EWS-activated transcript 2 (EAT-2) is polymorphic, which results in an ∼ 70% reduction in EAT-2 in DC
Silencing of the EAT-2 gene in DC that lacked this polymorphism led to increased production of IL-12 and enhanced differentiation of T cells to a Th1 phenotype in T cell-DC cocultures

findings.statement: Talaei et al. (2015) showed that SLAM signaling inhibited IL-12 production by CD40L-activated dendritic cells, and that EAT-2 knockdown increased IL-12 production by CD40-stimulated DCs. SLAM coengagement blocked CD40-induced activation of the p38 MAPK and JNK pathways. This block was reversed in DCs carrying the NZB EAT-2 allele. The authors concluded that EAT-2 negatively regulates DC cytokine production downstream of SLAM engagement and that a polymorphism disturbing this process promotes the development of lupus.
quotes: knockdown of EAT-2 resulted in increased production of IL-12 by CD40-stimulated DC
SLAM coengagement blocked activation of p38 MAPK and JNK signaling pathways in DC, which was reversed in DC with the NZB EAT-2 allele
We conclude that EAT-2 negatively regulates cytokine production in DC downstream of SLAM engagement and that a genetic polymorphism that disturbs this process promotes the development of lupus.

relevance_reason: Functional immunology study of Th17 cells in children with lupus nephritis; it adds to understanding of how SLE develops but contains no genetic findings.

findings.statement: Kshirsagar et al. (2014) found that effector T cells (CD4+CD45RA-Foxp3- and Foxp3-low) from children with lupus nephritis had enhanced Stat3 activity, which correlated with increased frequencies of IL-17-producing cells. PBMCs from these children had significantly higher RORC and IL-17 mRNA levels than controls. Inhibiting mTOR with rapamycin reduced both Stat3 activation and the frequency of IL-17-producing T cells.
quotes: enhanced activity of Stat3 in CD4(+)CD45RA(-)Foxp3(-) and Foxp3(low) effector T cells from children with LN correlates with increased frequencies of IL-17-producing cells within these T cell populations
The levels of retinoic acid-related orphan receptor c and IL-17 mRNA are significantly higher in PBMCs from children with LN than in those from controls.
Mammalian target of rapamycin inhibition by rapamycin reduces both Stat3 activation in effector T cells and the frequency of IL-17-producing T cells in lupus patients.

findings.statement: Kshirsagar et al. (2014) showed that Th17 cells from children with lupus nephritis had high Akt activity and an enhanced capacity to migrate, and that inhibiting the Akt pathway significantly reduced Th17 cell migration. Complement factor C5a slightly increased IL-17 expression and activated Akt in anti-CD3-activated lupus effector T cells. The authors suggested that modulating Akt activity therapeutically might inhibit Th17 cell trafficking to sites of inflammation.
quotes: Th17 cells from children with LN exhibit high Akt activity and enhanced migratory capacity. Inhibition of the Akt signaling pathway significantly decreases Th17 cell migration.
Complement factor C5a slightly increases the expression of IL-17 and induces activation of Akt in anti-CD3-activated lupus effector T cells.
suggest that therapeutic modulation of the Akt activity may inhibit Th17 cell trafficking to sites of inflammation

relevance_reason: Functional and genomic characterization of SLE-associated FCGR3B copy-number deletion, proposing a mechanism (chimeric FCGR2C/FCGR2B gene with ectopic FcγRIIb on NK cells) for SLE risk.

findings.statement: Mueller et al. (2013) mapped allelic and paralogous sequence variation across the FCGR2/FCGR3 locus on chromosome 1q23 using sequence from fosmid and BAC clones and sequence-captured DNA from FCGR3B-deleted genomes. They identified two highly paralogous 24.5-kb blocks within the FCGR2C/FCGR3B/FCGR2B locus, devoid of nonpolymorphic paralogous sequence variations, that define the limits of the regions in which nonallelic homologous recombination leads to FCGR2C/FCGR3B copy-number variation; reduced FCGR3B copy number is associated with increased SLE risk.
quotes: Reduced FCGR3B copy number is associated with increased risk of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

This analysis identified two highly paralogous 24.5 kb blocks within the FCGR2C/FCGR3B/FCGR2B locus that are devoid of nonpolymorphic paralogous sequence variations and that define the limits of the genomic regions in which nonallelic homologous recombination leads to FCGR2C/FCGR3B copy-number variation.

findings.statement: Mueller et al. (2013) found by flow cytometry, immunoblotting, and cDNA sequencing that individuals with FCGR3B-deleted alleles showed ectopic presence of FcγRIIb on natural killer (NK) cells. They concluded that FCGR3B deletion juxtaposes the 5-prime regulatory sequences of FCGR2C with the coding sequence of FCGR2B, creating a chimeric gene that results in ectopic FcγRIIb accumulation on NK cells, providing an explanation for SLE risk associated with reduced FCGR3B copy number.
quotes: individuals with FCGR3B-deleted alleles show ectopic presence of FcγRIIb on natural killer (NK) cells

We conclude that FCGR3B deletion juxtaposes the 5'-regulatory sequences of FCGR2C with the coding sequence of FCGR2B, creating a chimeric gene that results in an ectopic accumulation of FcγRIIb on NK cells and provides an explanation for SLE risk associated with reduced FCGR3B gene copy number.

findings.statement: Mueller et al. (2013) found evidence of swapping of haplotype blocks between the highly paralogous blocks of the FCGR2/FCGR3 locus, most likely arising from sequential ancestral recombination events across the region.
quotes: the data showed evidence of swapping of haplotype blocks between these highly paralogous blocks that most likely arose from sequential ancestral recombination events across the region.

relevance_reason: Identifies CSK regulatory SNP rs34933034 as an SLE susceptibility locus with functional B-cell studies.

findings.statement: Manjarrez-Orduño et al. (2012) found that SNPs tagging a CSK haplotype 'B' were nominally associated with SLE in a prior European GWAS (1,311 cases, 3,340 controls). Sequencing of CSK exons and conserved intronic regions in 24 European SLE patients homozygous for haplotype B identified the minor A allele of intronic SNP rs34933034 (G>A) on 34 of 48 B chromosomes. Genotyping of 3,769 SLE cases and 3,404 controls of European ancestry from 11 cohorts showed an association of the A allele with SLE (allelic OR 1.32, p = 1.04 x 10(-9)).
quotes: the minor allele (A) of the intronic variant rs34933034 (G > A) was present in 34 of the 48 chromosomes bearing the “B” haplotype
we genotyped 3769 SLE cases and 3404 controls of European ancestry derived from eleven cohorts
The results provide convincing evidence for an association between SLE and the A allele of the variant rs34933034: allelic O.R. 1.32, p-value 1.04 × 10−9.

findings.statement: Manjarrez-Orduño et al. (2012) showed that the rs34933034 A allele lies almost exclusively on the CSK B haplotype (D-prime = 0.95) but has low correlation (r2 < 0.5) with other haplotype-tagging SNPs; conditional analysis with 1000 Genomes imputation showed that association of B-haplotype tags such as rs8033381 (P = 9 x 10(-8)) was eliminated after conditioning on rs34933034 (P = 0.19). No genetic interaction was observed between rs34933034 and PTPN22 R620W (rs2476601).
quotes: Linkage disequilibrium analysis shows that the rs34933034 A allele nearly exclusively exists on the B haplotype (D′ = 0.95)
the rs8033381 marker tagging the common B haplotype shows an association (P-value: 9 × 10−8) that is eliminated after conditioning on rs34933034 (P-value: 0.19)
we did not observe evidence of genetic interaction between rs34933034 and rs2476601 (PTPN22, R620W).

findings.statement: Manjarrez-Orduño et al. (2012) found that CSK expression was highest in B cells and inversely correlated with B-cell maturity, and in naive B cells from 29 healthy B-haplotype homozygous donors the rs34933034 risk A allele was associated with higher CSK transcript levels. Naive B cells from risk allele carriers showed increased inhibitory Tyr508 phosphorylation of Lyn, enhanced calcium mobilization after BCR cross-linking, and carriers had higher plasma IgM.
quotes: higher levels of CSK transcripts in naïve B cells are significantly associated with the rs3493034 A allele
naïve B cells from subjects carrying the CSK risk allele exhibit higher Tyr508 phosphorylation of Lyn than non-risk allele carriers
naïve B cells homozygous for the A allele exhibit enhanced calcium mobilization triggered by BCR cross-linking

findings.statement: Manjarrez-Orduño et al. (2012) found in 27 umbilical cord blood samples that newborns homozygous for the CSK risk allele had double the frequency of transitional B cells, with an expansion of late transitional cells; the authors suggested this might reflect impaired tolerance checkpoint or enhanced positive selection, predicting more autoreactive B cells, and that the Lyp-Csk complex increases lupus susceptibility at multiple B-cell maturation and activation points.
quotes: newborn subjects homozygous for the CSK risk allele have double the frequency of transitional cells (CD38hi, CD10hi) compared to levels observed in the cord blood of non-risk subjects
This might reflect an impairment of a tolerance checkpoint or an enhanced positive selection of late transitional B cells.

relevance_reason: A large case-control study of C4 copy-number variation and SLE risk. It found that partial C4 deficiency is not an independent risk factor for SLE.

findings.statement: Boteva et al. (2012) genotyped 2,207 subjects of northern and southern European ancestry (1,028 SLE cases and 1,179 controls) from the UK and Spain. They measured total C4, C4A, and C4B gene copy numbers and the loss-of-function C4 exon 29 CT indel. Using multiple logistic regression with HLA-DRB1 and MHC region SNPs, they showed that genetically determined partial C4 deficiency states were not independent risk factors for SLE. The C4A exon 29 CT insertion was not associated with SLE in either cohort.
quotes: we genotyped 2,207 subjects of northern and southern European ancestry (1,028 SLE cases and 1,179 controls) for total C4, C4A, and C4B gene copy numbers, and the loss-of-function C4 exon 29 CT indel
We clearly demonstrate that genetically determined partial C4 deficiency states are not independent risk factors for SLE in UK and Spanish populations.
These results are further corroborated by the lack of association shown by the C4A exon 29 CT insertion in either cohort.
findings.population: UK and Spanish (northern and southern European)

findings.statement: Boteva et al. (2012) concluded that complete homozygous C4 deficiency is one of the strongest genetic risk factors for SLE. Partial C4 deficiency states, however, did not independently predispose to the disease. The authors suggested that earlier reported associations may reflect long-range linkage disequilibrium within the MHC.
quotes: Thus, although complete homozygous deficiency of complement C4 is one of the strongest genetic risk factors for SLE, partial C4 deficiency states do not independently predispose to the disease.
it has not been established whether this association is primarily causal or secondary to long-range linkage disequilibrium

relevance_reason: The paper is about NCF1 copy number variation and rheumatoid arthritis, not systemic lupus erythematosus. It is useful only as background on NCF1 genetic complexity and its function in the NADPH oxidase in autoimmunity.

findings.statement: Olsson et al. (2012) found that patients with rheumatoid arthritis were less likely than controls to carry an increased copy number of NCF1 (7.6% vs 11.6%; p = 0.037). They suggested that an increased NCF1 copy number may protect against developing RA.
quotes: We find that RA patients are less likely to have an increased copy number of NCF1, 7.6%, compared with 11.6% in controls; p=0.037.
These data suggest that an increased copy number of NCF1 can be protective against developing RA

findings.statement: Olsson et al. (2012) showed that the T allele of the NCF1-339 SNP (rs13447) is expressed from NCF1 and significantly reduces production of reactive oxygen species.
quotes: We also show that the T-allele of NCF1-339 (rs13447) is expressed in NCF1 and significantly reduces reactive oxygen species production.
