relevance_reason: Case-control association study: low FCGR3B copy number linked to SLE susceptibility in Caucasian and Chinese cohorts, plus FCGR2B I232T association and the linkage disequilibrium between the two.

findings.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) used a triple paralogue ratio test (PRT) assay to measure FCGR3B copy number in Caucasian SLE cohorts from the UK and Sweden and their controls. Combined by meta-analysis, the two cohorts showed a significant association between low FCGR3B copy number (0 or 1 copies) and SLE (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.08-2.27; P = 0.018). High copy number was not associated with SLE.
quotes: The association with low CN, but not high CN, was supported by Caucasian SLE cohorts from the UK and Sweden.
combined as a single cohort by meta-analysis (Fig. 3B) showed significant association of low CN with SLE [odds ratio (OR) 1.57, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.08–2.27; P = 0.018]

findings.statement: In a Hong Kong Chinese SLE case-control cohort, Niederer et al. (2010) found a strong association between low FCGR3B copy number and SLE (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.25-2.18; P = 4 x 10(-4)). The association was strongest in patients with lupus nephritis. Across all cohorts, the combined meta-analysis OR was 1.62 (95% CI 1.30-2.03). FCGR3A copy number did not differ between cases and controls.
quotes: found a strong association of low CN with SLE (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.25–2.18; P = 4 × 10−4) with a similar effect size to that in Caucasians

This association was the strongest in the sub-group of Chinese patients with lupus nephritis, and demonstrates for the first time the association of FCGR3B low CN with SLE in a non-Caucasian population.
The combined OR of this effect, by meta-analysis, was 1.62 (95% CI 1.30–2.03) (Fig. 3B).

findings.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) genotyped 2 new Caucasian SLE cohorts from the UK and Sweden and confirmed that homozygosity for the FcgammaRIIB-232T allele (I232T, rs1050501) is associated with SLE. A meta-analysis of all Caucasian studies gave an OR of 2.26 (95% CI 1.49-3.41). In the Hong Kong Chinese cohort, 232T homozygotes showed a nonsignificant trend toward increase in SLE.
quotes: We have added to this data by analysing two new Caucasian SLE cohorts from UK and Swedish populations, further demonstrating a significant association of FcγRIIB-232T allele homozygosity with SLE risk
When all studies involving Caucasian cohorts were analysed in a meta-analysis, there was a strong association with SLE (OR 2.26, 95% CI 1.49–3.41)
findings.population: UK and Swedish Caucasian; Hong Kong Chinese

findings.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) found weak-to-moderate linkage disequilibrium between FCGR3B copy number and FCGR2B I232T in Caucasian and Chinese controls. Low FCGR3B copy number was more common in carriers of the 232T allele. In logistic regression, however, FCGR3B copy number remained significant after adjusting for FCGR2B I232T in both populations (Chinese OR 1.67; Caucasian OR 1.55). The authors concluded that, despite the LD, the two variants have independent effects on SLE risk.
quotes: There was weak-to-moderate LD in the Caucasian and Chinese control cohorts, as measured by D′
Overall, this indicated that, despite the presence of LD between the loci, FCGR2B-I232T and FCGR3B CNV have independent effects on the risk of developing SLE.

findings.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) found that homozygosity for FcgammaRIIA-131R was more frequent in the SLE cohorts (OR 1.3 in both Chinese and Caucasians), but the association was not significant. FcgammaRIIIA V176F was not significantly associated with SLE.
quotes: The proportion of FcγRIIA-131R homozygotes was increased in the SLE cohorts, although the association was not significant, perhaps due to relatively small numbers
FcγRIIIA-V176F did not show a significant association with SLE.

findings.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) suggested that the strong association between low FCGR3B copy number and SLE points to a role for neutrophils in protection from SLE. Their proposed mechanism is that reduced FcgammaRIIIB expression lowers immune complex uptake by neutrophils, leading to more immune complex deposition and inflammatory damage.
quotes: The strong association of low CN of FCGR3B with SLE suggests a hitherto un-emphasized role of neutrophils in protection from SLE.
Reduced FcγRIIIB expression could thus lead to increased IC deposition and resulting inflammatory damage and disease.

findings.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) found significant ethnic differences in FCGR3B copy number. Low copy number was least common in Caucasians (7.4%), intermediate in Chinese and Vietnamese, and most common in Kenyans. High copy number was most common in Chinese and Vietnamese. FCGR3B copy number showed no association with ANCA-associated vasculitis, severe malaria, or bacterial sepsis.
quotes: Low FCGR3B CN (0 or 1 copies) was least common in Caucasians, intermediate in Chinese and Vietnamese populations and highest in the Kenyan population.
There was no association of FCGR3B CNV with vasculitis, nor with malarial or bacterial infection.
findings.population: Caucasian, Hong Kong Chinese, Vietnamese Kinh, Kenyan

relevance_reason: This association study links a FCGR2B SNP that abolishes receptor function to SLE susceptibility in Caucasian and Southeast Asian populations, and to protection against severe malaria in an African population.

findings.statement: Willcocks et al. (2010) found that an FCGR2B SNP that abrogates the function of the inhibitory receptor FcgammaRIIb was strongly associated with susceptibility to SLE in both Caucasians and Southeast Asians.
quotes: We show that a SNP in human FCGR2B that abrogates receptor function is strongly associated with susceptibility to SLE in both Caucasians and Southeast Asians.

findings.statement: Willcocks et al. (2010) found that the minor allele of the defunctioning FCGR2B SNP was more common in Southeast Asians and Africans, who live in areas where malaria is endemic, than in Caucasians. In an East African population, homozygosity for the minor allele was associated with substantial protection against severe malaria (odds ratio = 0.56; P = 7.1 x 10(-5)). The authors suggested that this protection may contribute to the higher frequency of the SNP, and therefore of SLE, in Africans and Southeast Asians.
quotes: The minor allele of this SNP is more common in Southeast Asians and Africans, populations from areas where malaria is endemic, than in Caucasians.
We show that homozygosity for the minor allele is associated with substantial protection against severe malaria in an East African population (odds ratio = 0.56; P = 7.1 x 10(-5)).
This protective effect against malaria may contribute to the higher frequency of this SNP and hence, SLE in Africans and Southeast Asians.

relevance_reason: Case-control association study identifying EGR2 regulatory SNPs as SLE susceptibility factors (Japanese cohorts implied but not stated in abstract).

findings.statement: Myouzen et al. (2010) genotyped 14 tag SNPs in the EGR2 gene region in 3 sets of SLE case-control cohorts and found a peak of association with SLE susceptibility for rs10761670, located in the 5-prime flanking region of EGR2 (pooled OR = 1.23, 95% CI 1.10-1.37, P = 0.00023). The same SNP was also associated with rheumatoid arthritis (OR = 1.15, P = 0.0019), suggesting that EGR2 is a common risk factor for SLE and RA.
quotes: We then performed a case-control association study using three sets of SLE cohorts by genotyping 14 tag SNPs in the EGR2 gene region. A peak of association with SLE susceptibility was observed for rs10761670 [Pooled: OR = 1.23 (95% CI 1.10-1.37), P=0.00023).
This SNP was also associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) [OR = 1.15 (95% CI 1.05-1.26), P = 0.0019), suggesting that EGR2 is a common risk factor for SLE and RA.

findings.statement: Myouzen et al. (2010) found that rs10761670 in the 5-prime flanking region of EGR2 was significantly positively correlated with EGR2 expression (R = 0.23, P = 0.00072). Among SNPs in complete linkage disequilibrium with rs10761670, rs1412554 and rs1509957 affected transcription factor binding and transcriptional activity in vitro, suggesting they may be causal regulatory variants; the authors concluded that increased EGR2 expression may contribute to SLE pathogenesis.
quotes: a significant positive correlation with expression was identified in an SNP located at the 5' flanking region of EGR2 (rs10761670, R=0.23, P=0.00072)

two SNPs (rs1412554 and rs1509957) affected the binding of transcription factors and transcriptional activity in vitro, suggesting that they may be candidates of causal regulatory variants in this region
EGR2 is a genetic risk factor for SLE, in which increased gene expression may contribute to SLE pathogenesis.

relevance_reason: A large GWAS replication study that identified five new SLE susceptibility loci (TNIP1, PRDM1, JAZF1, UHRF1BP1, IL10), confirmed previously reported loci and proposed further candidate loci.

findings.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) selected SNPs from 2,466 regions that showed nominal association with SLE (P < 0.05) in a genome-wide scan of 1,310 cases and 7,859 controls. They genotyped these SNPs with a custom array in independent case-control samples from the United States (1,129 cases, 2,991 controls) and Sweden (834 cases, 1,338 controls). The study identified five new SLE susceptibility loci at genome-wide significance (P < 5 x 10(-8)): TNIP1 (OR = 1.27), PRDM1 (OR = 1.20), JAZF1 (OR = 1.20), UHRF1BP1 (OR = 1.17) and IL10 (OR = 1.19).
quotes: To confirm additional risk loci, we selected SNPs from 2,466 regions that showed nominal evidence of association to SLE (P < 0.05) in a genome-wide study and genotyped them in an independent sample of 1,963 cases and 4,329 controls.
This replication effort identified five new SLE susceptibility loci (P < 5 x 10(-8)): TNIP1 (odds ratio (OR) = 1.27), PRDM1 (OR = 1.20), JAZF1 (OR = 1.20), UHRF1BP1 (OR = 1.17) and IL10 (OR = 1.19).
genotyped two independent SLE case and control populations from the United States (1,129 SLE cases and 2,991 controls) and Sweden (834 SLE cases and 1,338 controls)

findings.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) found that a SNP on 5q33.1 (rs7708392), located within an intron of TNIP1, was significantly associated with SLE in all three cohorts (combined P = 3.8 x 10(-13); OR 1.27). This SLE signal was 21 kb from, and appeared distinct from (r2 = 0.001), the psoriasis risk variants near TNIP1. The authors noted that TNIP1 interacts with TNFAIP3.
quotes: A variant (rs7708392) on 5q33.1 that resides within an intron of TNIP1 (encoding TNF-α-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3)-interacting protein 1) was significantly associated with SLE in all three cohorts and had a combined P = 3.8 × 10−13 (Fig. 2).
the SLE and psoriasis risk variants are separated by 21 kb and appear to have distinct genetic signals (r2 = 0.001)

findings.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) identified an SLE risk variant (rs6568431; P = 7.12 x 10(-10)) in the intergenic region between PRDM1 (BLIMP1) and ATG5. This signal appeared distinct from the previously reported ATG5 risk allele rs2245214 (r2 < 0.1). rs2245214 remained significantly associated with SLE after conditioning on rs6568431.
quotes: A second confirmed risk variant (rs6568431, P = 7.12 × 10−10) was identified in an intergenic region between PRDM1 (PR domain containing 1, with ZNF domain, also known as BLIMP1) and ATG5 (APG5 autophagy 5-like).
rs6568431 has an r2 < 0.1 with rs2245214, and rs2245214 remains significantly associated with SLE (P < 1 × 10−5) after conditional logistic regression incorporating rs6568431

findings.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) identified the JAZF1 promoter region as an SLE susceptibility locus (rs849142; P = 1.54 x 10(-9)). The same variant had previously been associated with type 2 diabetes and with height variation. A separate prostate cancer risk allele near JAZF1 showed no association with SLE.
quotes: The promoter region of JAZF1 (juxtaposed with another zinc finger gene 1) is a third newly confirmed SLE locus (rs849142, P = 1.54 × 10−9).
Of note, this same variant was previously associated with risk of type 2 diabetes and with height variation.

findings.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) identified an SLE risk locus defined by a nonsynonymous allele, R454Q (rs11755393; P = 2.22 x 10(-8)), in UHRF1BP1, a putative binding partner of UHRF1. The risk allele lies in a region of extended linkage disequilibrium that includes several genes, including SNRPC. SNRPC is part of an RNA processing complex often targeted by SLE autoantibodies.
quotes: A fourth newly identified SLE risk locus is defined by a nonsynonymous allele (R454Q) of UHRF1BP1 (ICBP90 binding protein 1; rs11755393, P = 2.22 × 10−8).

The UHRF1BP1 risk allele is in a region of extended LD that encompasses multiple genes, including SNRPC (small nuclear ribonucleoprotein polypeptide C), which is part of a RNA processing complex often targeted by SLE autoantibodies.

findings.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) identified IL10 as an SLE susceptibility locus (rs3024505; P = 3.95 x 10(-8); OR 1.19). This SNP is the same one previously found to contribute to the risk of ulcerative colitis and type 1 diabetes, which the authors suggested may indicate shared pathophysiology in the IL10 pathway.
quotes: The fifth newly identified SLE locus is IL10 (interleukin-10; rs3024505, P = 3.95 × 10−8; Fig. 2).

The variant associated with SLE is identical to a SNP recently identified as contributing to risk of ulcerative colitis and type 1 diabetes, suggesting the possibility of shared pathophysiology in the IL10 pathway across these disorders.

findings.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) tested 25 SNPs from 23 previously reported SLE loci and found further evidence of association for 21 of them. Nine loci reached genome-wide significance in the combined dataset: HLA-DRB1 (DR3), IRF5, TNFAIP3, BLK, STAT4, ITGAM, PTPN22, PHRF1 (KIAA1542) and TNFSF4. At the IRAK1-MECP2 locus, SNPs near IRAK1 showed the strongest association. No association was seen for LYN, SCUBE1, TLR5 or LY9.
quotes: We found further evidence of association for 21 of the variants (P < 0.05), including 9 loci that reached genome-wide significance (P < 5 × 10−8) in the current combined dataset.
Among the loci with genome-wide significant results were HLA-DRB1 (HLA*DR3 or DRB1*0301), IRF5, TNFAIP3, BLK, STAT4, ITGAM, PTPN22, PHRF1 (also called KIAA1542) and TNFSF4 (also called OX40L).
For four previously implicated variants (LYN, SCUBE1, TLR5 and LY9), no evidence of association was observed in the combined dataset.

findings.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) identified 21 additional candidate SLE loci with P < 1 x 10(-5). These included IRF8, TAOK3 (missense allele rs428073, N47S), LYST and IL12RB2.
quotes: Using a significance threshold of P < 1 × 10−5 in the combined replication sample, we identified 21 additional SLE candidate risk loci (Table 2 and Supplementary Table 2).
TAOK3 (TAO kinase 3), a kinase expressed in lymphocytes, and the disease-associated variant is a missense allele (rs428073, N47S)

findings.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) tested 42 variants from 35 loci previously reported as risk alleles for other autoimmune diseases. Five loci showed suggestive association with SLE: IFIH1, CFB, CLEC16A, IL12B and SH2B3. These included a missense allele of IFIH1 (rs1990760; P = 3.3 x 10(-7)) previously associated with type 1 diabetes and Graves disease, and a missense allele R32Q of CFB (rs641153). The CFB allele was protective and remained significant after conditioning on HLA DR2 and DR3.
quotes: A candidate screen of alleles previously associated with other autoimmune diseases suggested five loci (P < 1 x 10(-3)) that may contribute to SLE: IFIH1, CFB, CLEC16A, IL12B and SH2B3.
We observed a highly significant association to SLE of a missense allele of IFIH1 (rs1990760, P = 3.3 × 10−7) that has previously been associated with type 1 diabetes and Graves’ disease.

This missense allele in CFB is not in significant LD with other HLA region variants associated with SLE (DR2/DR3) and remained significant (P < 0.05) after conditional logistic regression analyses that incorporated DR2 and DR3.

findings.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) found no evidence for non-additive interactions among the 26 confirmed SLE risk alleles. HLA-DRB1 (DR3), IRF5 and STAT4 each accounted for more than 1% of the genetic variance. Together, the 26 loci explained an estimated 8% of the total genetic susceptibility to SLE.
quotes: we observed no evidence for non-additive interactions
HLA-DRB1 (HLA*DR3), IRF5 and STAT4 were each estimated to account for over 1% of the genetic variance, whereas the remaining loci each accounted for less than 1% of the variance.
Together, the 26 SLE risk loci explain an estimated 8% of the total genetic susceptibility to SLE.

relevance_reason: A GWAS of SLE in a Chinese Han population that found 9 new susceptibility loci and confirmed 7 previously reported loci.

findings.statement: Han et al. (2009) performed a genome-wide association study of SLE in a Chinese Han population. They genotyped 1,047 cases and 1,205 controls with Illumina Human610-Quad BeadChips and replicated 78 SNPs in two additional cohorts (3,152 cases and 7,050 controls). They identified 9 new susceptibility loci, at ETS1, IKZF1, RASGRP3, SLC15A4, TNIP1, 7q11.23, 10q11.22, 11q23.3, and 16p11.2, with combined P values from 1.77 x 10(-25) to 2.77 x 10(-8).
quotes: genotyping 1,047 cases and 1,205 controls using Illumina Human610-Quad BeadChips and replicating 78 SNPs in two additional cohorts (3,152 cases and 7,050 controls)
We identified nine new susceptibility loci (ETS1, IKZF1, RASGRP3, SLC15A4, TNIP1, 7q11.23, 10q11.22, 11q23.3 and 16p11.2; 1.77 x 10(-25) < or = P(combined) < or = 2.77 x 10(-8))

findings.statement: In the same Chinese Han study, Han et al. (2009) confirmed previously reported SLE susceptibility loci at BLK, IRF5, STAT4, TNFAIP3, TNFSF4, 6q21, and 22q11.21, with combined P values from 5.17 x 10(-42) to 5.18 x 10(-12).
quotes: confirmed seven previously reported loci (BLK, IRF5, STAT4, TNFAIP3, TNFSF4, 6q21 and 22q11.21; 5.17 x 10(-42) < or = P(combined) < or = 5.18 x 10(-12))

findings.statement: Han et al. (2009) compared their results with previous GWAS findings. They concluded that the comparison highlighted genetic heterogeneity in SLE susceptibility between Chinese Han and European populations.
quotes: Comparison with previous GWAS findings highlighted the genetic heterogeneity of SLE susceptibility between Chinese Han and European populations.

relevance_reason: Association study that identifies an IL18 SNP (rs360719) as a susceptibility variant for SLE, with functional evidence on expression and transcription-factor binding.

findings.statement: Sánchez et al. (2009) genotyped 9 SNPs in the IL18 gene in Spanish SLE cases and controls. Two SNPs stayed significant after fine mapping. The SNP that survived correction for multiple testing, rs360719, was then genotyped in replication cohorts from Italy and Argentina. Its C allele remained associated with SLE across the sets and in the meta-analysis (pooled OR = 1.37, 95% CI 1.21-1.54, combined P = 3.8 x 10(-7)).
quotes: we have genotyped nine SNPs in an independent set of Spanish cases and controls
The SNP (rs360719) surviving correction for multiple tests was genotyped in two replication cohorts from Italy and Argentina.
After the analysis, a significance with rs360719 C-allele remained across the sets and after the meta-analysis (Pooled OR = 1.37, 95% CI 1.21-1.54, combined P = 3.8E-07, Pc = 1.16E-06).

findings.statement: Sánchez et al. (2009) used quantitative real-time PCR to measure IL18 mRNA in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). IL18 mRNA levels were significantly higher in people carrying the rs360719 C risk allele. Electrophoretic mobility shift assays showed that this allele creates a binding site for the transcription factor OCT-1. The authors suggested that rs360719 may help determine SLE susceptibility and may be a key factor in IL18 expression.
quotes: We found a significant increase in the relative expression of IL18 mRNA in individuals carrying the rs360719 C-risk allele; in addition we show that the polymorphism creates a binding site for the transcriptional factor OCT-1.
These findings suggest that the novel IL18 rs360719 variant may play an important role in determining the susceptibility to SLE and it could be a key factor in the expression of the IL18 gene.

relevance_reason: Biomarker study showing elevated serum alpha-defensin (HNP-1) levels in SLE patients that correlated with disease activity; this adds biochemical and pathogenesis context to the SLE entry.

findings.statement: Sthoeger et al. (2009) found that the mean serum level of alpha-defensin human neutrophil peptide-1 (HNP-1) in SLE patients (11.07 +/- 13.92 ng/microl) was significantly higher than in healthy controls (0.12 +/- 0.07 ng/microl). Sixty percent of patients had very high serum levels, and 50% showed increased alpha-defensin gene expression in polymorphonuclear cells. High alpha-defensin levels correlated with disease activity but not with neutrophil count. In contrast, beta-defensin-2 (hBD-2) could not be detected by ELISA, and its mRNA levels were low and similar to those in controls.
quotes: the mean alpha-defensin level in the sera of all SLE patients (11.07 +/- 13.92 ng/microl) was significantly higher than that of controls (0.12 +/- 0.07 ng/microl)

Moreover, 60% of patients demonstrated very high serum levels (18.5 +/- 13.36 ng/microl) and 50% showed elevated gene expression in polymorphonuclear cells. High alpha-defensin levels correlated with disease activity, but not with neutrophil count.
hBD-2 could not be detected by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and its mRNA levels were low in SLE patients and similar to those found in controls.

findings.statement: Sthoeger et al. (2009) concluded that activation and degranulation of neutrophils led to alpha-defensin secretion in SLE patients. Because alpha-defensins have immunomodulatory effects, the authors suggested that their secretion may activate the adaptive immune system and lead to a systemic response.
quotes: Thus, activation and degranulation of neutrophils led to alpha-defensin secretion in SLE patients. Given the immunomodulatory role of alpha-defensins, it is possible that their secretion may activate the adaptive immune system leading to a systemic response.

relevance_reason: Association study that identified three independent TNFAIP3-region SNPs associated with SLE in Europeans, plus functional study of the F127C coding variant. This is susceptibility evidence for the SLE entry.

findings.statement: Musone et al. (2008) used genome-wide association data from 1,239 SLE cases and 1,629 controls of European ancestry to analyze the TNFAIP3 region on chromosome 6. They found 21 SNPs with allelic P of 0.005 or less. The strongest association was with rs13192841 (P = 5.4 x 10(-8); OR 1.4). Conditional analysis identified three independent signals in different LD blocks: rs13192841, rs2230926 and rs6922466.
quotes: In total, 1,239 SLE cases and 1,629 controls were included in this analysis.
rs13192841 had the smallest P value, 5.4 × 10−8 (OR 1.4, 95% CI = 1.2–1.6), and rs2230926 had the highest odds ratio (OR), 2.0 (95% CI = 1.4–3.0, P = 3.0 × 10−4).
The final three SNPs are in different LD blocks; each pairwise r2 is <0.01 (Fig. 1).

findings.statement: In multivariate logistic regression, Musone et al. (2008) found that the minor alleles of the noncoding SNPs rs13192841 (OR 0.72, P = 7.9 x 10(-6)) and rs6922466 (OR 0.76, P = 0.00039) were protective. The minor allele of rs2230926 was associated with increased SLE risk (OR 1.88, P = 0.0016). Analyses stratified by ancestry gave consistent results. The authors concluded that, although some of the rs2230926 signal may reflect substructure within the European population, a signal remained after controlling for it.
quotes: This shows protective effects of the rs13192841 minor allele with an OR of 0.72 (95% CI = 0.62–0.83, P = 7.9 × 10−6) and the rs6922466 minor allele with an OR of 0.76 (95% CI = 0.65–0.88, P = 0.00039).
In contrast, the minor allele of rs2230926 was associated with an increased risk of SLE with an OR of 1.88 (95% CI = 1.27–2.79, P = 0.0016).
although some signal from rs2230926 may be due to intra-European population substructure, there is strong evidence that a signal remains even after controlling for substructure.

findings.statement: Musone et al. (2008) reported that the coding SNP rs2230926 in TNFAIP3 causes a phe127-to-cys (F127C) change in A20. The risk cys127 protein was as stable as the phe127 protein. However, it was modestly but consistently less effective at inhibiting TNF-induced NF-kappa-B activity, which the authors suggested makes it a hypomorphic A20 protein.
quotes: The coding SNP, rs2230926, is a nonsynonymous variant resulting in a phenylalanine-to-cysteine change at residue 127 of the A20 protein.
Notably, the Cys127 A20 protein is modestly, but consistently, less effective at inhibiting TNF-induced NF-κB activity when similar amounts of the two proteins are expressed
it is likely that a hypomorphic A20 protein may contribute to multiple facets of excessive inflammation and auto-immunity in humans bearing this polymorphism.

findings.statement: Musone et al. (2008) suggested that TNFAIP3 polymorphisms may reduce the expression or anti-inflammatory activity of A20, which restricts NF-kappa-B signaling, and so predispose to SLE. They concluded that TNFAIP3 may be an important determinant of multiple autoimmune diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: These polymorphisms may cause reduced expression or activity of the anti-inflammatory activity of A20, predisposing individuals to develop SLE.
Hence, TNFAIP3 may be an important determinant for multiple autoimmune diseases.

relevance_reason: Genome-wide association study with trio replication. It identifies TNFAIP3 on 6q23 as an SLE susceptibility locus and also reports association at STAT4 and BLK.

findings.statement: Graham et al. (2008) performed a genome-wide association study of 311,238 SNPs in 431 unrelated SLE cases and 2,155 controls. Three regions reached genome-wide significance: HLA, IRF5/TNPO3, and a new SLE locus on chromosome 6q23 within the TNFAIP3 gene. The TNFAIP3 variant rs5029939 had a GWAS P value of 2.55 x 10(-8) and an odds ratio of 2.28. The association replicated in 740 independent trios (P = 2.47 x 10(-5)), giving a meta-analysis P value of 2.89 x 10(-12).
quotes: we tested association of 311,238 successfully genotyped SNPs in 431 unrelated SLE cases and 2155 controls

Three regions met a pre-specified threshold for genome-wide significance (P<5×10−8): the previously defined HLA, IRF5/TNPO3 regions and a novel SLE locus at chromosome 6q23 within the TNFAIP3 gene (Figure 1A).
Association with rs5029939 in TNFAIP3 replicated in the trios (trio P value=2.47×10−5), which together with the GWAS data produced a convincing meta-analysis P value = 2.89 ×10−12 (Table 1).

findings.statement: Graham et al. (2008) found that, in both the GWAS and the trio datasets, variants in STAT4 (rs3821236; meta-analysis P = 8.49 x 10(-11)) and BLK (rs2618476; meta-analysis P = 1.7 x 10(-8)) were associated with SLE at genome-wide significance. An ITGAM variant (rs11150610; meta-analysis P = 1.72 x 10(-6)) also showed replicated association.
quotes: Variants in the region of STAT4 and BLK also demonstrated association with SLE in both the GWAS and trio datasets and together produced meta-analysis P values exceeding genome-wide significance (rs3821236 in STAT4, meta P value=8.49×10−11 and rs2618476 in BLK, meta P value = 1.7×10−8) (Table 1).
In our study, a variant in ITGAM also demonstrated strong and convincing evidence for replication (rs11150610, meta P value = 1.72×10−6)

findings.statement: Graham et al. (2008) genotyped 8 SNPs across the TNFAIP3 region in 991 SLE trio families. The minor allele of rs6920220, which lies about 185 kb upstream of TNFAIP3 and is associated with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) risk, was also associated with SLE (P = 8.92 x 10(-5)). The RA-protective variant rs10499194 showed no association with SLE (P = 0.72).
quotes: We found the minor allele of rs6920220 that contributes to RA risk was also associated with susceptibility to SLE (P value = 8.92×10−5); however, no evidence for association was seen for the rs10499194 RA protective variant (P value = 0.72)
we genotyped a panel of eight SNPs that tag the RA and SLE alleles in our complete set of trio families (N=991)

findings.statement: Graham et al. (2008) used haplotype and conditional logistic regression analyses to show 2 apparently independent SLE association signals near TNFAIP3. One signal was marked by the minor allele of rs6920220. The other was a risk haplotype that directly spans TNFAIP3 and is marked by the minor alleles of rs10499197 and rs7749323. The authors could not exclude the possibility that a single variant with multiple risk alleles underlies the signal.
quotes: These results suggest that two independent variants in the region of TNFAIP3 contribute to SLE risk, although we are unable to exclude the possibility that a single variant with multiple risk alleles
3) a risk haplotype for SLE marked by a haplotype comprised of the minor alleles of rs10499197 and rs7749323 that directly spans TNFAIP3.

findings.statement: Graham et al. (2008) found that the association at the TNFAIP3 exon 3 missense SNP rs2230926 could be fully explained by the association at rs10499197 and rs7749323. Haplotype 5, which carries the minor allele of rs2230926, was not associated with SLE. The authors suggested that an untyped variant (or variants) on the risk haplotype is responsible for the association.
quotes: Haplotype 5 carries the minor allele of rs2230926 but is not associated with SLE
Taken together these results suggest an untyped variant(s) carried on the haplotype tagged by the minor alleles of rs10499197 and rs7749323 is responsible for this SLE association effect.

relevance_reason: Reports a protective association between the PTPN22 R263Q loss-of-function variant and SLE, with functional and structural studies.

findings.statement: Orrú et al. (2009) found that the Q263 allele of an R263Q missense substitution in the PTPN22 gene was associated with protection against systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: the Q263 variant conferred protection against human systemic lupus erythematosus, reinforcing the proposal that inhibition of LYP activity could be beneficial in human autoimmunity

findings.statement: Orrú et al. (2009) showed that the R263Q substitution in the catalytic domain of the lymphoid tyrosine phosphatase LYP, encoded by PTPN22, reduced phosphatase activity, and high-resolution structural analysis revealed the molecular basis for this loss of function. This contrasts with the gain-of-function R620W polymorphism, which is a risk factor for autoimmunity. The authors suggested that inhibiting LYP activity could be beneficial in human autoimmunity.
quotes: another missense substitution (R263Q) within the catalytic domain of LYP leads to reduced phosphatase activity
High-resolution structural analysis revealed the molecular basis for this loss of function.
A gain-of-function R620W polymorphism in the PTPN22 gene, encoding the lymphoid tyrosine phosphatase LYP, has recently emerged as an important risk factor for human autoimmunity.

relevance_reason: Replicates the link between low FCGR3B copy number and SLE in Caucasians and adds functional evidence for a mechanism (less FcγRIIIb, less immune complex uptake), including a family with FcγRIIIb deficiency whose proband had SLE.

findings.statement: Willcocks et al. (2008) confirmed an association between low FCGR3B copy number and SLE in a UK Caucasian population. They measured copy number by quantitative PCR in 171 patients and 176 ethnically matched controls (P = 0.027). They found no such association in a Hong Kong Chinese cohort of 159 cases and 150 controls, and none when the 57 patients with lupus nephritis were analyzed separately.
quotes: In total, 171 samples from Caucasian patients with SLE were compared with 176 ethnically matched control samples. We found lower CN was significantly associated with SLE in Caucasians (P = 0.027;
but such an association was not seen in a Chinese SLE cohort from Hong Kong, comprising 159 cases and 150 controls
This lack of association held true when the patients with lupus nephritis (n = 57) were analyzed independently

findings.statement: Willcocks et al. (2008) identified a woman with SLE whose neutrophils had no FCGR3 mRNA and no surface FcγRIIIb. Her monocytes had normal FCGR3 mRNA levels. Her son, daughter and one brother each carried one FCGR3B-null allele, showing Mendelian inheritance of the null allele. PCR showed that the deletion removed FCGR3B, HSPA7 and FCGR2C but spared FCGR3A and FCGR2B. CD59 was still expressed on neutrophils, which excluded a general defect in GPI anchoring.
quotes: we identified an individual with SLE who had no FCGR3 mRNA in neutrophils, but normal levels of FCGR3 mRNA in monocytes
the proband (A), her son, daughter, and brother with a single FCGR3B-null allele (B–D), and her husband and other brother (E and F) with two copies of FCGR3B
Further PCR analysis demonstrated that the genetic defect spared FCGR3A and FCGR2B and included HSPA7 and the FCGR2C

variants.as_reported: FCGR3B-null allele (deletion including FCGR3B, HSPA7 and FCGR2C)

findings.statement: In the FcγRIIIb-deficient family, Willcocks et al. (2008) found that FCGR3B copy number correlated with neutrophil adherence to IgG-coated surfaces under flow, immune complex binding and uptake, and serum levels of soluble FcγRIIIb. Superoxide production in response to stimuli thought to be Fc receptor–independent was not affected by copy number.
quotes: we analyzed the adherence of neutrophils flowed over surfaces coated with IgG, and demonstrated that adherence was proportional to FCGR3B CN
Immune complex adherence to, and uptake by, neutrophils also increased with increasing CN

Superoxide anion production in response to several stimuli thought to be FcR independent, such as formyl-Met-Leu-Phe (fMLP), granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), and PMA, was not affected by FCGR3B CN

findings.statement: In 33 healthy individuals, Willcocks et al. (2008) found that FCGR3B copy number was associated with neutrophil FcγRIIIb expression, immune complex uptake and soluble FcγRIIIb levels. Individuals with high copy number showed 4 times the rate of neutrophil adherence to IgG-coated surfaces seen in those with low copy number. The authors suggested that low FCGR3B copy number predisposes to SLE through impaired neutrophil trafficking to inflammatory lesions and reduced immune complex clearance.
quotes: with high CN individuals having four times the rate of adherence of those with low FCGR3B CN

Our data would suggest that the mechanism underlying this association is a failure of neutrophil trafficking to inflammatory lesions and reduced ability to ingest immune complexes once there, thereby reducing immune complex clearance and predisposing to SLE.

findings.statement: Willcocks et al. (2008) found that, unlike SLE, ANCA-associated systemic vasculitis was associated with high FCGR3B copy number (P = 10(-8)) in 556 patients from 3 UK cohorts compared with 286 controls. When tested directly on the same plate, patients with SLE had a significantly lower FCGR3B/CD36 ratio than patients with vasculitis (P = 0.0028).
quotes: AASV was associated with high CN when cases from all cohorts were compared with controls (P = 10−8
Patients with SLE showed a significantly lower mean FCGR3B/CD36 ratio than patients with AASV (P = 0.0028; Fig. 5 D).

relevance_reason: A case-control association study linking an ITPR3 promoter SNP and an NKX2.5 SNP to SLE susceptibility in Japanese people. It adds susceptibility-locus evidence to the SLE entry.

findings.statement: Oishi et al. (2008) carried out a case-control association study in Japanese people using genome-wide gene-based SNPs. They found that an SNP (rs3748079) in the promoter region of the ITPR3 gene on chromosome 6p21 was significantly associated with SLE in two independent Japanese case-control samples (P = 1.78 x 10(-8); odds ratio, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.51-2.35).
quotes: Here we report that an SNP (rs3748079) located in a promoter region of the inositol 1,4,5-triphosphate receptor type 3 (ITPR3) gene on chromosome 6p21 was significantly associated with SLE in two independent Japanese case-control samples [P=0.0000000178 with odds ratio of 1.88, 95% confidence interval (CI) of 1.51-2.35].

findings.statement: Oishi et al. (2008) found that NKX2.5 bound the promoter region containing the ITPR3 SNP rs3748079, and that this binding was specific to the non-susceptible T allele.
quotes: We found the binding of NKX2.5 specific to the non-susceptible T allele in the region including this SNP.

findings.statement: Oishi et al. (2008) found that an SNP in NKX2.5 was also associated with SLE in Japanese people (P = 0.0037; odds ratio, 1.74; 95% CI, 1.19-2.55). Individuals with risk genotypes at both the ITPR3 and NKX2.5 loci had a higher risk of SLE (odds ratio, 5.77). The authors concluded that genetic and functional interactions between ITPR3 and NKX2.5 play a crucial role in SLE pathogenesis.
quotes: Furthermore, an SNP in NKX2.5 also revealed an association with SLE (P=0.0037 with odds ratio of 1.74, 95% CI of 1.19-2.55).
Individuals with risk genotype of both ITPR3 and NKX2.5 loci have higher risk for SLE (odds ratio=5.77).

findings.statement: Oishi et al. (2008) found that the ITPR3 SNP rs3748079 was also associated with rheumatoid arthritis (P = 0.0084; odds ratio, 1.23) and with Graves disease (P = 0.00036; odds ratio, 1.57) in Japanese people.
quotes: This particular SNP also revealed associations with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) (P=0.0084 with odds ratio of 1.23, 95% CI of 1.05-1.43) and with Graves' disease (GD) (P=0.00036 with odds ratio of 1.57, 95% CI of 1.22-2.02).

relevance_reason: Association study that identifies ITGAM rs1143679 as an SLE susceptibility variant in individuals of European and African descent.

findings.statement: Nath et al. (2008) identified and replicated an association between SLE risk and ITGAM (CD11b) on 16p11.2 in 3,818 individuals of European descent. The strongest association was at a nonsynonymous SNP, rs1143679 (P = 1.7 x 10(-17), odds ratio = 1.78).
quotes: We identified and replicated an association between ITGAM (CD11b) at 16p11.2 and risk of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in 3,818 individuals of European descent.
The strongest association was at a nonsynonymous SNP, rs1143679 (P = 1.7 x 10(-17), odds ratio = 1.78).

findings.statement: Nath et al. (2008) replicated the association between ITGAM rs1143679 and SLE in two independent samples of individuals of African descent (P = 0.0002 and 0.003). The overall meta-analysis gave P = 6.9 x 10(-22).
quotes: We further replicated this association in two independent samples of individuals of African descent (P = 0.0002 and 0.003; overall meta-analysis P = 6.9 x 10(-22)).

findings.statement: Nath et al. (2008) concluded that the genetic association between ITGAM and SLE implicates the alpha(M)beta2-integrin adhesion pathway in the development of the disease.
quotes: The genetic association between ITGAM and SLE implicates the alpha(M)beta2-integrin adhesion pathway in disease development.

relevance_reason: Genome-wide association study identifying BANK1 as an SLE susceptibility gene, with functional variants.

findings.statement: In a genome-wide association scan using 85,042 SNPs, Kozyrev et al. (2008) identified an association between SLE and a nonsynonymous substitution in the BANK1 gene (rs10516487, R61H). The association was replicated in 4 independent case-control sets (combined P = 3.7 x 10(-10); OR = 1.38).
quotes: In a genome-wide scan using 85,042 SNPs, we identified an association between SLE and a nonsynonymous substitution (rs10516487, R61H) in the B-cell scaffold protein with ankyrin repeats gene, BANK1.
We replicated the association in four independent case-control sets (combined P = 3.7 x 10(-10); OR = 1.38).

findings.statement: Kozyrev et al. (2008) found 2 BANK1 isoforms, full-length and an alternatively spliced transcript lacking exon 2 (Delta2) that encodes a protein without a putative IP3R-binding domain; the transcripts were differentially expressed depending on a branch point-site SNP, rs17266594, in strong linkage disequilibrium with rs10516487. A third associated variant, rs3733197 (A383T), was found in the ankyrin domain. The authors suggested that disease-associated variants could contribute to sustained B cell-receptor signaling and B-cell hyperactivity.
quotes: We analyzed BANK1 cDNA and found two isoforms, one full-length and the other alternatively spliced and lacking exon 2 (Delta2), encoding a protein without a putative IP3R-binding domain.

The transcripts were differentially expressed depending on a branch point-site SNP, rs17266594, in strong linkage disequilibrium (LD) with rs10516487. A third associated variant was found in the ankyrin domain (rs3733197, A383T).
The disease-associated variants could contribute to sustained B cell-receptor signaling and B-cell hyperactivity characteristic of this disease.

relevance_reason: A genome-wide association study of SLE in women of European ancestry, with replication. It identified new susceptibility loci (ITGAM, KIAA1542, PXK and 1q25.1) and confirmed known ones (HLA, IRF5, STAT4, FCGR2A, PTPN22).

findings.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) ran a genome-wide association scan with 317,501 SNPs in 720 women of European ancestry with SLE and 2,337 controls. They then genotyped consistently associated SNPs in 2 independent replication sets totaling 1,846 affected women and 1,825 controls. Besides the HLA region and IRF5, they found replicated association at 4 new regions: 16p11.2 (ITGAM), 11p15.5 (KIAA1542), 3p14.3 (PXK) and 1q25.1 (rs10798269).
quotes: We performed a genome-wide association scan using 317,501 SNPs in 720 women of European ancestry with SLE and in 2,337 controls, and we genotyped consistently associated SNPs in two additional independent sample sets totaling 1,846 affected women and 1,825 controls.

we found evidence of association with replication (1.1 x 10(-7) < P(overall) < 1.6 x 10(-23); odds ratio = 0.82-1.62) in four regions: 16p11.2 (ITGAM), 11p15.5 (KIAA1542), 3p14.3 (PXK) and 1q25.1 (rs10798269).

findings.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) found 3 SNPs in or very near ITGAM on 16p11.2 that were associated with SLE. The associated SNPs were in low linkage disequilibrium with each other. When the authors combined their samples with those of an independent group that had also found the ITGAM association, 7,380 independent samples from women of European ancestry gave P = 2.02 x 10(-26) and OR = 1.65 at rs9888739, and P = 3.7 x 10(-16) and OR = 1.42 at rs1143678.
quotes: Outside the HLA region, we found three SNPs associated with SLE in or very near ITGAM on 16p11.2 (Table 1).
The associated SNPs in ITGAM were in low LD; ITGAM haplotypes did not explain additional variation beyond the individual SNPs.

The 7,380 independent samples from women of European ancestry used in the two studies produced a combined joint P = 2.02 × 10−26 and OR = 1.65 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.45–1.88) at rs9888739 and P = 3.7 × 10−16 and OR = 1.42 (95% CI: 1.27–1.61) at rs1143678.

findings.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) found that SNP rs4963128 in KIAA1542 at 11p15.5 was associated with SLE (joint OR = 0.78; P = 3.0 x 10(-10)). This SNP lies 23 kb telomeric to IRF7, a gene important in interferon-alpha production, and had r2 = 0.94 with rs709266 in IRF7.
quotes: SNP rs4963128 is in KIAA1542 at 11p15.5 (joint OR = 0.78; P = 3.0 × 10−10), a genomic region homologous to a gene encoding an elongation factor.
In addition, rs4963128 is 23 kb telomeric to IRF7, a gene that is important in interferon-α production, and had an r2 = 0.94 with rs709266 in IRF7.

findings.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) found strong evidence of association between SLE and SNP rs6445975 in PXK at 3p14.3 (P = 7.1 x 10(-9); OR = 1.25). PXK encodes a serine-threonine kinase containing a Phox homology domain.
quotes: Second, SNP rs6445975 at position 58345217 in PXK showed strong evidence for association (P = 7.1 × 10−9; OR = 1.25).
PXK at 3p14.3 encodes a Phox homology domain–containing serine-threonine kinase that has five known human splice variants

findings.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) found that rs10798269 on 1q25.1, which lies outside any recognized gene, was associated with SLE (OR = 0.82; P = 1.11 x 10(-7)). This marker lies within the 1q23-q25 SLE linkage interval.
quotes: Third, rs10798269, which lies outside any recognized gene, was also associated with SLE (Table 1; OR = 0.82 and P = 1.11 × 10−7). Notably, this marker is within the 1q23–q25 SLE linkage interval.

findings.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) found that the strongest association with SLE was in the HLA region at 6p21.3. In a 7.05-Mb region, 93 SNPs had P < 10(-6) in the joint analysis. The most significant SNPs, rs3131379 and rs1270942, reached P < 10(-50). Logistic regression identified 2 partially independent effects in the HLA region.
quotes: The most significant association was in the HLA region at 6p21.3. In this 7.05-Mb region, 93 SNPs had P < 10−6 in the joint analysis and P < 0.05 in each sample set (1, 2, 3 and 4)
The most significantly associated SNPs achieve P < 10−50 at chromosome 6 positions 31829012 (rs3131379) and 32026839 (rs1270942).
Logistic regression analysis of the HLA region identified two partially independent effects

findings.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) found association between SLE and 3 markers spanning 149 kb in the IRF5 and TNPO3 region on 7q32. Their analysis strongly suggested that this association was driven by a haplotype of the previously reported IRF5 SNPs rs752637 and rs729302.
quotes: Our analysis strongly suggests that the associations with the IRF5 and TNPO3 region in this study are driven by a haplotype of rs752637 and rs729302 (data not shown).

findings.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) tested 20 previously reported associations with SLE or other autoimmune diseases in their genome-wide association data. They replicated the associations in PTPN22, FCGR2A and STAT4.
quotes: We also evaluated 20 previously reported associations with SLE or other autoimmune diseases in the SLEGEN GWA data set (Sets 1 and 2) (Table 4). Our data replicated associations in PTPN22 (ref.), FCGR2A and STAT4 (ref.).

findings.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) dropped the requirement for replication in every sample set and found additional possible non-HLA associations. These included markers in genomic regions containing XKR6, LYN, ATG5, ICA1, BLK and SCUBE1.
quotes: The associations we identified included markers in genomic regions containing XKR6, LYN, ATG5, ICA1, BLK and SCUBE1 (Table 3).

findings.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) used stepwise logistic regression and found independent contributions from 2 HLA effects and 1 effect in each of 5 other regions. Considered jointly, these SNPs predicted SLE with a C statistic of 0.67 and explained about 15% of the sibling risk ratio of 29. The authors found no evidence of statistical interaction among the associated SNPs.
quotes: We detected two separate and independent effects in the HLA region and one additional independent effect in each of five of the six remaining genomic regions from Table 1. Considered jointly, these SNPs are predictive of SLE (C statistic = 0.67).
Alternatively considered, the SNPs listed in Table 2 jointly explained ~15% of the sibling risk ratio of 29.
Computing all pairwise interactions via logistic regression models did not provide any evidence of a statistical interaction among the associated SNPs, either within or between genes (P > 0.01).

relevance_reason: Genome-wide association study that identified and replicated two new SLE susceptibility loci, C8orf13-BLK (8p23.1) and ITGAM-ITGAX (16p11.2).

findings.statement: Hom et al. (2008) genotyped more than 500,000 SNPs in 1,311 patients with SLE and 1,783 controls, all North Americans of European descent, plus genotypes from 1,557 more controls taken from public repositories. They replicated the top loci in 793 patients and 857 controls from Sweden. Variation upstream of the transcription start sites of BLK and C8orf13 on chromosome 8p23.1 was associated with SLE in both the US and Swedish series (rs13277113; odds ratio, 1.39; P = 1 x 10(-10)).
quotes: We genotyped more than 500,000 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in DNA samples from 1311 case subjects with SLE and 1783 control subjects; all subjects were North Americans of European descent.
Replication of the top loci was performed in 793 case subjects and 857 control subjects from Sweden.

Genetic variation in the region upstream from the transcription initiation site of the gene encoding B lymphoid tyrosine kinase (BLK) and C8orf13 (chromosome 8p23.1) was associated with disease risk in both the U.S. and Swedish case-control series (rs13277113; odds ratio, 1.39; P=1x10(-10))
findings.population: North American of European descent; Swedish

findings.statement: Hom et al. (2008) found that the SLE risk allele in the BLK/C8orf13 promoter region was associated with altered mRNA levels in B-cell lines: lower BLK expression and higher C8orf13 expression.
quotes: and also with altered levels of messenger RNA in B-cell lines
a promoter-region allele associated with reduced expression of BLK and increased expression of C8orf13

findings.statement: In the combined US and Swedish sample, Hom et al. (2008) found that variants on chromosome 16p11.22 near ITGAM (CD11b) and ITGAX were associated with SLE (rs11574637; odds ratio, 1.33; P = 3 x 10(-11)).
quotes: variants on chromosome 16p11.22, near the genes encoding integrin alpha M (ITGAM, or CD11b) and integrin alpha X (ITGAX), were associated with SLE in the combined sample (rs11574637; odds ratio, 1.33; P=3x10(-11))
findings.population: North American of European descent; Swedish

relevance_reason: Reports global DNA hypomethylation in CD4+ T cells from SLE patients and DNMT expression studies; this is pathogenesis and biochemical evidence for SLE.

findings.statement: Balada et al. (2008) measured the deoxymethylcytosine (dmC) content of DNA from purified CD4+ T cells by ELISA in 29 SLE patients and 30 healthy controls. Patients had significantly lower CD4+ T-cell DNA dmC content than controls (0.802 +/- 0.134 vs 0.901 +/- 0.133; P = 0.007), which fits with global DNA hypomethylation in SLE.
quotes: The DNA deoxymethylcytosine (dmC) content of purified CD4(+) T cells from 29 SLE patients and 30 healthy controls was measured by means of an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).
SLE patients had a significantly lower CD4(+) T-cell DNA dmC content than controls (0.802 +/- 0.134 versus 0.901 +/- 0.133) (P = 0.007).

findings.statement: Balada et al. (2008) used real-time RT-PCR to measure DNMT1, DNMT3A and DNMT3B transcript levels in CD4+ T cells and found no difference between SLE patients and controls. However, low complement together with lymphopenia, high anti-dsDNA titers, or a SLEDAI score above 5 was associated with increased expression of at least one of the three methyltransferases. The authors suggested that patients with active disease might be responding indirectly to an underlying DNA hypomethylation by raising methyltransferase mRNA levels.
quotes: No differences in transcript levels were observed for DNMT1, DNMT3A and DNMT3B between patients and controls.

The simultaneous association of low complement counts with lymphopenia, high titres of anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA), or an SLE disease activity index (SLEDAI) of > 5, resulted in the increase of at least one of the three DNA methyltransferases.
It is possible that patients were reacting indirectly to an underlying DNA hypomethylation status by increasing the mRNA levels of DNA methyltransferases when the disease was being definitely active.

relevance_reason: Association study that identifies TNFSF4 upstream haplotype as an SLE susceptibility locus (SLE susceptibility locus entry), with functional expression data.

findings.statement: Cunninghame Graham et al. (2008) genotyped 36 SNPs across TNFSF4 and 4 across TNFRSF4 in 416 UK European Caucasian SLE parental-affected trios and found, by TDT and haplotype-TDT analysis, association of the upstream region of TNFSF4 (gene-wide permuted P = 0.0020), with no association of TNFRSF4. A single overtransmitted upstream risk haplotype (haplotype 4), tagged by minor alleles of rs10912580, rs12039904, rs2205960 and rs1234317, was found in the UK (P = 0.0104) and replicated in 263 Minnesota trios (P = 3.00 x 10(-4)); an undertransmitted protective haplotype (haplotype 3) was tagged by the rare A allele of rs844644.
quotes: Haplotype-TDT analysis within the upstream region confirmed that there is a single overtransmitted GCTAATCATTTGA haplotype (4) in both the UK (Pu = 0.0104) and Minnesota datasets (Pu = 3.00 × 10−4; Table 1).
This overtransmitted haplotype was tagged by multiple overtransmitted rare alleles (SNPs rs10912580, rs12039904, rs2205960 and rs1234317).

Transmission-disequilibrium test (TDT) analysis of both individual SNPs and haplotypes across TNFRSF4 showed that none of the SNPs (Pu > 0.05) and none of the haplotypes reached significance (Pu > 0.05; data not shown).

findings.statement: In a joint analysis of 778 UK and Minnesota trios, Cunninghame Graham et al. (2008) found the overtransmitted haplotype 4 (T/U 1.61) and undertransmitted haplotype 3 (T/U 0.73) remained significant after permutation (P < 1 x 10(-5)). Association was replicated in an independent case-control set of 424 UK SLE cases and 642 British 1958 Birth Cohort controls (rs2205960 OR 1.28; rs844644 OR 0.710, P = 6.83 x 10(-5)); combining all data, the strongest associations were rs12039904 (P = 1.91 x 10(-6)) and rs844644 (P = 6.08 x 10(-7)).
quotes: There are significant associations from four SNPs, including two haplotype-tagging variants, one of which tags the overtransmitted haplotype (rs2205960 Pu = 7.00 × 10−3, odds ratio (OR) = 1.28, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.07–1.53) and the other of which tags the undertransmitted haplotype (rs844644 Pu = 6.83 × 10−5, OR = 0.710, 95% CI = 0.597–0.840).

The two variants with the strongest associations were the overtransmitted haplotype-tagging variant, rs12039904 (P = 1.91 × 10−6), and rs844644, which tags the under-transmitted haplotype (P = 6.08 × 10−7).

findings.statement: Conditional logistic regression by Cunninghame Graham et al. (2008) showed that the effect of each individual SNP disappeared when conditioned on haplotype background, supporting the hypothesis that no single genotyped variant was responsible for the upstream association, with the exception of rs844644 (P = 0.015). The T allele of rs1234317, which uniquely tags the risk haplotype, was predicted to destroy a binding site for the transcriptional repressor E4BP4.
quotes: supports the hypothesis that no single genotyped variant is responsible for the association in the upstream region of TNFSF4 (Supplementary Table 6 online). The exception is rs844644, which showed a moderate P value (P = 0.015) by conditional analysis.

the T allele of rs1234317, which uniquely tags the overtransmitted haplotype, is predicted by the Genomatix SNP analysis web tool to destroy the DNA binding site for the transcriptional repressor E4BP4

findings.statement: Cunninghame Graham et al. (2008) found in UK SLE families that TNFSF4 risk-haplotype tagging SNPs did not influence the lupus phenotype toward antiphospholipid syndrome, Sjogren syndrome, or lupus nephritis subtypes.
quotes: All the two-sample t-tests for all possible SNP-phenotype combinations exceeded 0.2, indicating that the disease susceptibility variants in TNFSF4 did not influence the lupus phenotype toward any of the three subtypes tested.

findings.statement: Cunninghame Graham et al. (2008) showed that activated lymphoblastoid cell lines homozygous for the overtransmitted TNFSF4 upstream haplotype had more TNFSF4-positive cells (P = 0.02) and a 6.7-fold increase in TNFSF4 transcript (P = 0.008) compared with lines homozygous for the undertransmitted haplotype; activated peripheral blood lymphocytes from 8 SLE probands showed consistent increased surface TNFSF4 with the risk haplotype. They hypothesized that increased TNFSF4 expression predisposes to SLE by augmenting T cell-APC interaction via TNFRSF4 co-stimulation.
quotes: Quantification of TNFSF4 mRNA levels by qRT-PCR showed that the LCL-over cells had a 6.7-fold (P 0.008) increase in the level of TNFSF4 transcript compared to the LCL-under cells (Fig. 2c).
This difference in expression was consistent in eight individuals (P = 0.02; Fig. 2f).

We hypothesize that increased expression of TNFSF4 predisposes to SLE either by quantitatively augmenting T cell-APC interaction or by influencing the functional consequences of T cell activation via TNFRSF4.

relevance_reason: Case-control association study that found a TNXB SNP associated with SLE susceptibility in a Japanese population.

findings.statement: Kamatani et al. (2008) ran a case-control association study using genome-wide gene-based SNP markers in 178 Japanese SLE patients and 899 controls. They found a significant association between SLE and SNP rs3130342, located in the 5-prime flanking region of the TNXB gene (P = 0.000000930; OR 3.11, 95% CI 1.89-5.28). The association was replicated in an independent set of 203 cases and 294 controls (P = 0.0440; OR 1.52, 95% CI 1.01-2.78). The authors concluded that TNXB is a candidate SLE susceptibility gene in the Japanese population.
quotes: An SNP, rs3130342, in a 5' flanking region of the TNXB gene revealed a significant association with SLE [P = 0.000000930, odds ratio (OR) 3.11, with 95% confidence interval (95%CI) of 1.89-5.28] in a Japanese population.
This association was replicated independently with 203 cases and 294 controls (P = 0.0440, OR 1.52, with 95%CI of 1.01-2.78).
Our findings strongly imply that the TNXB gene is a candidate gene susceptible to SLE in the Japanese population.

findings.statement: Kamatani et al. (2008) found that the association of copy number variation (CNV) of the C4 gene, which lies next to TNXB, with SLE was weaker than the association of TNXB SNP rs3130342. They suggested that the C4 CNV association probably reflected linkage disequilibrium with this SNP. Stratified analysis showed that the rs3130342 association was independent of the HLA-DRB1*1501 allele.
quotes: our analysis on this CNV revealed that the association of CNV of the C4 gene was weaker than the SNP in the TNXB gene and likely to reflect the linkage disequilibrium between C4 CNV and this particular SNP.
Stratified analysis also revealed that the association of SNP rs3130342 with SLE was independent of the HLA-DRB1*1501 allele that has been shown to be associated with SLE.

relevance_reason: This paper reports a STAT4 intron 3 haplotype (rs7574865) that is significantly associated with susceptibility to systemic lupus erythematosus.

findings.statement: Remmers et al. (2007) tested SNPs in candidate genes in the previously linked chromosome 2q region. They then tested implicated STAT4 SNPs in 1,039 patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and 1,248 controls from 3 SLE case series. The haplotype marked by rs7574865 in intron 3 of STAT4 was strongly associated with lupus. It was present on 31% of chromosomes from patients and 22% from controls (P = 1.87 x 10(-9); odds ratio 1.55).
quotes: in a total of 1039 case patients and 1248 controls from three series of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus

The haplotype marked by rs7574865 was strongly associated with lupus, being present on 31% of chromosomes of case patients and 22% of those of controls (P=1.87x10(-9); odds ratio for having the risk allele in chromosomes of patients vs. those of controls, 1.55).

findings.statement: Remmers et al. (2007) found that being homozygous for the STAT4 risk allele, compared with not carrying it, was associated with more than double the risk of lupus. The same comparison showed a 60% increased risk of rheumatoid arthritis. The authors suggested that SLE and rheumatoid arthritis share a pathway.
quotes: Homozygosity of the risk allele, as compared with absence of the allele, was associated with a more than doubled risk for lupus and a 60% increased risk for rheumatoid arthritis.
A haplotype of STAT4 is associated with increased risk for both rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus, suggesting a shared pathway for these illnesses.

relevance_reason: Reports heterozygous TREX1 mutations in SLE patients, absent from controls, with functional data, which implicates TREX1 in SLE.

findings.statement: Lee-Kirsch et al. (2007) found monoallelic frameshift or missense mutations, plus one 3-prime UTR variant, in the TREX1 gene in 9 of 417 individuals with systemic lupus erythematosus. None of these variants were found in 1,712 controls (P = 4.1 x 10(-7)). The authors concluded that TREX1 is implicated in the pathogenesis of SLE.
quotes: we report monoallelic frameshift or missense mutations and one 3' UTR variant of TREX1 present in 9/417 individuals with systemic lupus erythematosus but absent in 1,712 controls (P = 4.1 x 10(-7))
Our findings implicate TREX1 in the pathogenesis of SLE.

findings.statement: Lee-Kirsch et al. (2007) showed that 2 mutant TREX1 alleles found in SLE patients changed the subcellular targeting of the protein. They noted that TREX1 works together with the SET complex in granzyme A-mediated apoptosis.
quotes: We demonstrate that two mutant TREX1 alleles alter subcellular targeting.
TREX1 acts in concert with the SET complex in granzyme A-mediated apoptosis

relevance_reason: Case-control association study showing that low FCGR3B copy number, and complete FCGR3B deficiency, is associated with susceptibility to SLE in UK cohorts. This is evidence for a susceptibility locus.

findings.statement: Fanciulli et al. (2007) confirmed and strengthened an association between low FCGR3B copy number and SLE with glomerulonephritis (P = 1.4 x 10(-8)) in 161 UK SLE patients with glomerulonephritis compared with 312 controls from the UK 1958 birth cohort. Individuals with fewer than 2 copies of FCGR3B had a significantly higher risk of glomerulonephritis than those with 2 copies (OR = 2.43, P = 1 x 10(-3)).
quotes: the previously reported association (P = 1 × 10-3) was confirmed and strengthened (P = 1.4 × 10-8, 95% c.i. = 0 to 2.9 × 10-5; Fig. 1a) in a larger sample comprising 161 SLE patients with glomerulonephritis from the UK and in 312 independent controls from the UK 1958 birth cohort
individuals with fewer than two copies had a significantly higher risk of glomerulonephritis (odds ratio (OR) = 2.43, P = 1 × 10-3, Table 1)

findings.statement: Fanciulli et al. (2007) found a strong association between FCGR3B copy number and SLE without known renal involvement in 375 unrelated UK cases (P = 1.4 x 10(-5)), with increased risk of SLE in individuals with fewer than 2 FCGR3B copies (OR = 2.21, P = 3 x 10(-4)). Across all 536 SLE cases, the P value of association was 2.7 x 10(-8). Among SLE patients, fewer than 2 copies did not significantly increase the risk of glomerulonephritis (OR = 1.09, P = 0.660).
quotes: We found a new, strong association (P = 1.4 × 10-5; 95% c.i. = 0 to 2.9 × 10-5; Fig. 1b and Table 1) and an increased risk for development of SLE in individuals with fewer than two copies of FCGR3B (OR = 2.21, P = 3 × 10-4, Table 1).
When we considered all SLE cases together (n = 536), regardless of renal involvement, the P value of association was 2.7 × 10-8 (95% c.i. = 0 to 2.9 × 10-5).

However, we did not observe any significantly higher risk of acquiring glomerulonephritis in individuals with SLE who possessed fewer than two copies of FCGR3B (OR = 1.09; 95% c.i. = 0.73-1.62, P = 0.660).

findings.statement: Fanciulli et al. (2007) observed zero copies of FCGR3B, indicating complete FCGR3B deficiency, in 25 of 1,279 (2%) individuals with autoimmunity, including 7 SLE patients with glomerulonephritis and 14 with SLE without nephritis. Only 1 of 862 controls (0.1%) had zero copies. The authors suggested that complete FCGR3B deficiency confers a very high risk of autoimmunity, particularly SLE.
quotes: We observed zero copies of FCGR3B in 25 out of 1,279 (2%) individuals with autoimmunity (7 SLE patients with glomerulonephritis, 14 with SLE, one with MPA, 1 with Wegener’s granulomatosis and 2 with Graves’ disease) but in only 1 of 862 controls (0.1%).
This suggests that complete FCGR3B deficiency confers a very high risk of autoimmunity, particularly for SLE.

findings.statement: Fanciulli et al. (2007) also found association of low FCGR3B copy number with Wegener granulomatosis in UK (P = 3 x 10(-3)) and French (P = 1.1 x 10(-4)) cohorts, and with microscopic polyangiitis (P = 2.9 x 10(-4)). They found no association with the organ-specific diseases Graves disease (P = 0.65) or Addison disease (P = 0.057). This suggested different roles for FCGR3B copy number variation in systemic and organ-specific autoimmunity.
quotes: we found association between FCGR3B copy number and susceptibility to Wegener’s granulomatosis (Birmingham cohort, P = 3 × 10-3 and 95% c.i. = 2.5 × 10-3 to 3.1 × 10-3; Paris cohort, P = 1.1 × 10-4
We did not see any significant association between FCGR3B copy number and either Graves’ disease (in a large cohort that included 429 cases and 190 controls; P = 0.65
suggesting a different role for FCGR3B CNV in development of systemic and organ-specific autoimmunity

findings.statement: Fanciulli et al. (2007) noted that FCGR3B is expressed by neutrophils and eosinophils and is important in tethering neutrophils to immune complexes and in clearing immune complexes. They hypothesized that in SLE, reduced clearance of immune complexes predisposes to disease in the glomeruli and at other sites.
quotes: FCGR3B is expressed by neutrophils and eosinophils and is important in tethering of neutrophils to immune complexes and in clearance of immune complexes.
We hypothesize that in individuals with SLE, reduced clearance of immune complexes predisposes to disease in glomeruli and at other sites.

relevance_reason: Case-control and family-based association study showing that C4 gene copy-number variation affects how likely people are to develop SLE.

findings.statement: Yang et al. (2007) studied C4 gene copy-number variation in 1,241 European Americans, including patients with SLE, their first-degree relatives, and unrelated healthy subjects, using definitive genotyping and phenotyping techniques. Compared with healthy subjects, patients with SLE had total C4 and C4A gene copy numbers shifted to the lower side. Having only 2 copies of total C4 significantly raised SLE risk (patients 9.3% vs unrelated controls 1.5%; OR = 6.514; P = 0.00002). Having 5 or more copies lowered the risk (5.79% vs 12%; OR = 0.466; P = 0.016).
quotes: We investigated the C4 gene CNV in 1,241 European Americans, including patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), their first-degree relatives, and unrelated healthy subjects, by definitive genotyping and phenotyping techniques.
In comparison with healthy subjects, patients with SLE clearly had the GCN of total C4 and C4A shifting to the lower side.

The risk of SLE disease susceptibility significantly increased among subjects with only two copies of total C4 (patients 9.3%; unrelated controls 1.5%; odds ratio [OR] = 6.514; P=.00002) but decreased in those with > or =5 copies of C4 (patients 5.79%; controls 12%; OR=0.466; P=.016).

findings.statement: Yang et al. (2007) found that having zero copies of C4A (OR = 5.267; P = 0.001) or one copy of C4A (OR = 1.613; P = 0.022) was a risk factor for SLE. Having 3 or more copies of C4A appeared to be protective (OR = 0.574; P = 0.012).
quotes: Both zero copies (OR=5.267; P=.001) and one copy (OR=1.613; P=.022) of C4A were risk factors for SLE, whereas > or =3 copies of C4A appeared to be protective (OR=0.574; P=.012).

findings.statement: Among European Americans, Yang et al. (2007) found that gene copy number ranged from 2 to 6 for total C4, 0 to 5 for C4A, and 0 to 4 for C4B. Four copies of total C4, 2 of C4A, and 2 of C4B were the most common counts, but each made up only one-half to three-quarters of the study populations. Long C4 genes correlated with C4A (R = 0.695) and short C4 genes correlated with C4B (R = 0.437).
quotes: The gene copy number (GCN) varied from 2 to 6 for total C4, from 0 to 5 for C4A, and from 0 to 4 for C4B.
Four copies of total C4, two copies of C4A, and two copies of C4B were the most common GCN counts, but each constituted only between one-half and three-quarters of the study populations.
Long C4 genes were strongly correlated with C4A (R=0.695; P<.0001). Short C4 genes were correlated with C4B (R=0.437; P<.0001).

findings.statement: Using family-based association tests, Yang et al. (2007) suggested that a specific haplotype carrying a single short C4B gene was more likely to be passed to patients with SLE. This haplotype was in tight linkage disequilibrium with the -308A allele of TNFA.
quotes: Family-based association tests suggested that a specific haplotype with a single short C4B in tight linkage disequilibrium with the -308A allele of TNFA was more likely to be transmitted to patients with SLE.

relevance_reason: Reports linkage of SLE to 1q32.2 and association of a CR2 haplotype with SLE susceptibility, with functional data on the 5'UTR SNP.

findings.statement: In a targeted genome scan of 1q21-43 in 126 lupus multiplex families containing 151 affected sib pairs, Wu et al. (2007) found evidence of linkage of SLE at 1q32.2 (nonparametric linkage score 2.52, P = 0.006).
quotes: We found evidence of linkage at 1q32.2 in a targeted genome scan of 1q21-43 in 126 lupus multiplex families containing 151 affected sibpairs (nonparametric linkage score 2.52, P = 0.006).

findings.statement: Wu et al. (2007) analyzed 1,416 individuals from 258 Caucasian and 142 Chinese lupus simplex families and found that a common 3-SNP haplotype of the CR2 gene (rs3813946, rs1048971, rs17615) was associated with SLE susceptibility (P = 0.00001), conferring a 1.54-fold increased risk of disease. They concluded that CR2, a positional candidate at 1q32.2 and also a candidate in the murine Sle1c locus, is a likely SLE susceptibility gene.
quotes: we analyzed 1,416 individuals from 258 Caucasian and 142 Chinese lupus simplex families and demonstrated that a common three-single-nucleotide polymorphism CR2 haplotype (rs3813946, rs1048971, rs17615) was associated with lupus susceptibility (P = 0.00001) with a 1.54-fold increased risk for the development of disease.
Our findings reveal that CR2 is a likely susceptibility gene for human lupus at 1q32.2

findings.statement: Wu et al. (2007) found that SNP1 (rs3813946), located in the 5-prime untranslated region of CR2, altered transcriptional activity, suggesting a potential mechanism by which CR2 could contribute to the development of lupus.
quotes: Single-nucleotide polymorphism 1 (rs3813946), located in the 5' untranslated region of the CR2 gene, altered transcriptional activity, suggesting a potential mechanism by which CR2 could contribute to the development of lupus.

relevance_reason: Pathogenesis study showing that anti-NMDAR/anti-DNA autoantibodies from SLE patients cause hippocampal neuronal damage and memory impairment in mice and are present in the brains of patients with neuropsychiatric lupus.

findings.statement: Kowal et al. (2006) found that serum from lupus patients that reacted with both DNA and the NMDA receptor (NMDAR) caused cognitive impairment in mice. The serum was given intravenously, and the mice also received lipopolysaccharide to break down the blood-brain barrier. The mice showed hippocampal neuron damage on histopathology and hippocampus-dependent memory impairment on behavioral testing.
quotes: serum with reactivity to DNA and NMDAR extracted from lupus patients elicited cognitive impairment in mice receiving the serum intravenously and given lipopolysaccharide to compromise the BBB integrity
Brain histopathology showed hippocampal neuron damage, and behavioral testing revealed hippocampus-dependent memory impairment.

findings.statement: Kowal et al. (2006) eluted IgG from the brain of a lupus patient. This IgG bound DNA and NMDAR and caused neuronal apoptosis when injected into mouse brains. In the brains of 4 more patients with neuropsychiatric lupus, endogenous IgG colocalized with anti-NMDAR antibodies. The authors concluded that lupus patients have circulating anti-NMDAR antibodies that can cause neuronal damage and memory deficits if they cross the blood-brain barrier, and that these antibodies are present in patients' brains.
quotes: we eluted IgG from a patient's brain. The IgG bound DNA and NMDAR and caused neuronal apoptosis when injected into mouse brains.
We examined four more brains of patients with neuropsychiatric lupus and found that they displayed endogenous IgG colocalizing with anti-NMDAR Abs.
lupus patients have circulating anti-NMDAR Abs capable of causing neuronal damage and memory deficit, if they breach the BBB, and that the Abs exist within patients' brains

relevance_reason: Replicates association of IRF5 rs2004640 T allele/haplotype with SLE susceptibility and characterizes functional splicing and expression effects.

findings.statement: Graham et al. (2006) replicated association of the IRF5 rs2004640 T allele with SLE in 4 independent case-control cohorts (P = 4.4 x 10(-16)) and by family-based transmission disequilibrium test analysis (P = 0.0006).
quotes: Here we convincingly replicate association of the IFN regulatory factor 5 (IRF5) rs2004640 T allele with SLE in four independent case-control cohorts (P = 4.4 x 10(-16)) and by family-based transmission disequilibrium test analysis (P = 0.0006).

findings.statement: Graham et al. (2006) found that the IRF5 rs2004640 T allele creates a 5-prime donor splice site in an alternate exon 1 (exon 1B), allowing expression of several unique IRF5 isoforms. They also identified an independent cis-acting variant, linked to the exon 1B splice site, associated with elevated IRF5 expression; haplotypes carrying the elevated-expression variant but lacking the exon 1B donor site did not confer SLE risk. They concluded that a common IRF5 haplotype driving elevated expression of multiple unique isoforms is an important genetic risk factor for SLE, establishing a causal role for type I IFN pathway genes in human autoimmunity.
quotes: The rs2004640 T allele creates a 5' donor splice site in an alternate exon 1 of IRF5, allowing expression of several unique IRF5 isoforms.

We also identify an independent cis-acting variant associated with elevated expression of IRF5 and linked to the exon 1B splice site. Haplotypes carrying the variant associated with elevated expression and lacking the exon 1B donor site do not confer risk of SLE.
Thus, a common IRF5 haplotype driving elevated expression of multiple unique isoforms of IRF5 is an important genetic risk factor for SLE

relevance_reason: Reports association of low FCGR3B copy number with glomerulonephritis in human SLE, plus a rat model of Fcgr3 copy number variation and glomerulonephritis.

findings.statement: Aitman et al. (2006) found that, in humans, low copy number of FCGR3B, an orthologue of rat Fcgr3, was associated with glomerulonephritis in systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: In humans, low copy number of FCGR3B, an orthologue of rat Fcgr3, was associated with glomerulonephritis in the autoimmune disease systemic lupus erythematosus.

findings.statement: Aitman et al. (2006) used positional cloning in Wistar Kyoto rats to identify loss of a newly described rat-specific Fcgr3 paralogue, Fcgr3-related sequence (Fcgr3-rs), as a determinant of macrophage overactivity and immunologically mediated glomerulonephritis. They concluded that gene copy number polymorphism predisposes to immunologically mediated renal disease in two mammalian species.
quotes: Positional cloning identified loss of the newly described, rat-specific Fcgr3 paralogue, Fcgr3-related sequence (Fcgr3-rs), as a determinant of macrophage overactivity and glomerulonephritis in Wistar Kyoto rats.
Here we show that copy number variation of the orthologous rat and human Fcgr3 genes is a determinant of susceptibility to immunologically mediated glomerulonephritis.

relevance_reason: A meta-analysis of studies linking the TNF-alpha -308 A/G promoter polymorphism to SLE susceptibility. It adds association evidence and ethnic stratification.

findings.statement: Lee et al. (2006) performed a meta-analysis of 21 studies of the TNF-alpha promoter -308 A/G functional polymorphism and SLE. Overall, the A/A genotype was associated with SLE (OR 3.2, 95% CI 2.0-5.3, P less than 0.001), as were the A/A plus A/G genotypes (OR 2.0, CI 1.3-3.1, P less than 0.001). The authors concluded that the -308 A/G polymorphism may confer susceptibility to SLE, especially in European-derived populations.
quotes: We have identified 21 studies of this polymorphism and SLE using MEDLINE search.
The overall odds ratio (OR) of the A/A genotype was 3.2 (95% CI=2.0-5.3, P<0.001).
The overall OR for the risk genotypes (A/A and A/G) was 2.0 (CI=1.3-3.1, P<0.001).

findings.statement: In ethnic stratification, Lee et al. (2006) found that the TNF -308 A/A genotype was associated with SLE in European-derived populations (OR 4.0, CI 2.5-6.4, P less than 0.001) but not in Asian-derived populations (OR 1.3, P = 0.76). The A allele was associated with SLE in Europeans (OR 2.1, CI 1.6-2.7, P less than 0.001). It was not associated in Asian (OR 1.4, P = 0.2) or African (OR 1.2, P = 0.59) populations.
quotes: Stratification by ethnicity indicated that the A/A genotype was associated with SLE in European-derived population (OR=4.0, CI=2.5-6.4, P<0.001). No association was detected in Asian-derived population (OR, 1.3, CI=0.3-6.3, P=0.76).
a significant association was found in European population (OR=2.1, CI=1.6-2.7, P<0.001), but not in Asian (OR=1.4, CI=0.8-2.3, P=0.2) or African (OR=1.2, CI=0.6-2.5, P=0.59) populations

relevance_reason: Genome scan meta-analysis of SLE linkage studies identifying susceptibility loci; mapping evidence for SLE.
