findings.statement: Lee and Nath (2005) performed a genome search meta-analysis (GSMA) of 12 genome scan results from 9 independent studies, comprising 605 families with 1,355 SLE-affected individuals of Caucasian, African American, and Hispanic self-reported ethnicity. Two genomic locations, 6p22.3-6p21.1 (containing the HLA region) and 16p12.3-16q12.2, met genome-wide significance (p less than 0.000417), with clustering of significant adjacent bins on chromosomes 6 and 16.
quotes: Twelve genome scan results generated from nine independent studies have been used for the present GSMA. All together, the data consists of 605 families with 1,355 SLE affected individuals from three self-reported ethnicities; Caucasian, African-American, and Hispanic.
The present study identified two genomic locations at 6p22.3-6p21.1 and 16p12.3-16q12.2 that met genome-wide significance (p<0.000417). The identified region at 6p22.3-6p21.1 contains the HLA region.
Clustering of significant adjacent bins was observed for chromosomes 6 and 16.

findings.statement: Lee and Nath (2005) found 12 additional bins with two pointwise p values less than 0.05, suggesting they likely contain SLE susceptibility loci, including 2 novel regions at 4q32.1-4q34.3 and 13q13.2-13q22.2.
quotes: Additionally, there are 12 other bins with two point-wise p-values (Psumrnk and Pord) <0.05, suggesting that these bin regions are highly likely to contain SLE susceptibility loci. Among them, present GSMA also identified two novel regions at 4q32.1-4q34.3 and 13q13.2-13q22.2.

findings.statement: In a separate analysis restricted to Caucasian populations, Lee and Nath (2005) found the strongest evidence for linkage at 6p21.1-6q15 (Psumrnk = 0.00021), and suggested that a novel region at 3q22.1-3q25.33 (Psumrnk = 0.01376) may represent an ethnicity-specific SLE linkage.
quotes: However, separate analysis using only Caucasian populations identified the strongest evidence for linkage at chromosome 6p21.1-6q15 (Psumrnk=0.00021).
One interesting novel region suggests that 3q22.1-3q25.33 (Psumrnk=0.01376) may be an ethnicity-specific SLE linkage.

relevance_reason: Linkage study mapping an SLE susceptibility locus to 13q32 in African American multiplex families with affected males; also reports clinical subphenotype (renal disease) in such families.

findings.statement: Xing et al. (2005) replicated, in a combined sample of 372 individuals from 159 families plus 392 individuals from 181 new families, the observation that SLE females with affected male relatives have a higher prevalence of renal disease than SLE females without affected male relatives, supporting the hypothesis that multiplex SLE families with at least one affected male ('male families') form a distinct subpopulation.
quotes: Previously, our group showed that SLE females with affected male relatives have higher prevalence of renal disease than SLE females with no affected male relatives in a sample of 372 individuals from 159 families.

By adding 392 individuals from 181 new families, we replicated this finding in the largest collection of families with affected males, confirming our hypothesis that multiplex SLE families with at least one affected male member ("male families") comprise a distinct subpopulation of SLE multiplex families.

findings.statement: Xing et al. (2005) performed a genome-wide scan in 64 SLE multiplex families with affected male members and found the largest signal (lod = 3.08) at 13q32 in 18 African American male families using affected-relative-pair model-free linkage; IBD sharing suggested dominant inheritance, and multipoint model-based analysis gave a lod score of 3.13 (disease allele frequency 0.0004, penetrance 0.5). Fine mapping in these and 3 additional African American male families localized the locus to a region tightly linked to D13S892, confirming previously reported linkage of SLE to 13q32; the authors suggested the susceptibility gene is specific to African Americans with a form of SLE in which males are at high risk.
quotes: We studied 64 male families by a genome-wide scan for SLE and found the largest signal (lod=3.08) at 13q32 in 18 African American male families using an affected-relative-pair model-free linkage method.

Multipoint model-based linkage analysis generated a lod score of 3.13 in the same chromosomal region with a low-disease allele frequency of 0.0004 and a disease penetrance of 0.5 for the 18 African American male families.
We performed fine mapping in these and three additional African American male families and the SLE predisposing locus was localized to a region tightly linked to the marker D13S892.

relevance_reason: Functional study showing that the SLE-associated FCGR2B T232 polymorphism causes loss of function, which adds evidence about the disease mechanism.

findings.statement: Floto et al. (2005) showed that a recently described SLE-associated FcgammaRIIb polymorphism, FcgammaRIIb T232, which encodes a single amino acid substitution in the transmembrane domain, is functionally impaired. FcgammaRIIb T232 could not inhibit activatory receptors because it was excluded from sphingolipid rafts. The authors stated that this results in unopposed proinflammatory signaling, which is thought to promote SLE.
quotes: We show that a recently described SLE-associated polymorphism of FcgammaRIIb (FcgammaRIIbT(232)), encoding a single transmembrane amino acid substitution, is functionally impaired.
FcgammaRIIbT(232) is unable to inhibit activatory receptors because it is excluded from sphingolipid rafts, resulting in the unopposed proinflammatory signaling thought to promote SLE.

relevance_reason: Animal model study showing PI3Kgamma inhibition reduces glomerulonephritis and extends lifespan in MRL-lpr lupus mice; relevant to SLE animal model/therapeutic section.

findings.statement: Barber et al. (2005) examined the use of inhibitors of phosphoinositide 3-kinase gamma (PI3Kgamma), a lipid kinase that regulates inflammation, in the MRL-lpr mouse model of SLE. Treatment reduced glomerulonephritis and prolonged lifespan, suggesting that PI3Kgamma may be a useful target in the treatment of chronic inflammation.
quotes: Here we examine the use of inhibitors of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) gamma, a lipid kinase that regulates inflammation, in the MRL-lpr mouse model of SLE.
Treatment reduced glomerulonephritis and prolonged lifespan, suggesting that P13Kgamma may be a useful target in the treatment of chronic inflammation.

relevance_reason: Reports an association between an FCGR2B promoter polymorphism and SLE, with functional evidence. This is susceptibility evidence for SLE.

findings.statement: Blank et al. (2005) identified a G-C substitution at position -343 relative to the transcription start site in the FCGR2B promoter (rs3219018). In European Americans, being homozygous for the C allele (-343 C/C) was associated with SLE (OR = 11.1, P = 0.003).
quotes: Here we report the identification of a polymorphism in the human FCGR2B promoter (dbSNP no. rs3219018) that is associated in homozygosity with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) phenotype in European-Americans (OR=11.1, P=0.003).

findings.statement: Blank et al. (2005) found that the -343 G-C substitution was associated with lower transcription from the FCGR2B promoter and reduced binding of the AP1 transcription complex to the variant promoter sequence. Activated B cells from SLE patients homozygous for -343 C/C had significantly reduced surface expression of FcgammaRIIb. The authors suggested that deregulated FCGR2B expression in -343 C/C homozygotes may play a role in the pathogenesis of SLE.
quotes: The G-C substitution correlated with decreased transcription of the FCGR2B promoter, and resulted in decreased binding of the AP1 transcription complex to the mutant promoter sequence.
The surface expression of FcgammaRIIb receptors was significantly reduced in activated B cells from (-343 C/C) SLE patients.
These findings suggest that genetic defects may lead to deregulated expression of the FCGR2B gene in -343 C/C homozygous subjects, and may play a role in the pathogenesis of human SLE.

relevance_reason: Meta-analysis of CTLA-4 polymorphisms as SLE susceptibility factors; supports a susceptibility locus association.

findings.statement: In a meta-analysis of 14 independent studies (to July 2004) testing association between CTLA4 polymorphisms (exon-1 +49, promoter -318 and -1722, and a 3-prime UTR dinucleotide repeat) and SLE, Lee et al. (2005) found that the CTLA4 exon-1 +49 polymorphism was significantly associated with SLE susceptibility; the overall odds ratio for the +49 GG genotype was 1.287 (95% CI 1.031-1.562, P = 0.011). The authors concluded that the +49 (A/G) polymorphism influences the risk of developing SLE, especially in Asians.
quotes: A total of 14 independent studies (to July 2004) testing association between one or more CTLA-4 polymorphisms and SLE were used in this analysis.
The overall risk, measured by odds ratio (OR), for exon-1 +49 GG genotype is 1.287 [95% confidence interval (CI)=1.031-1.562, P=0.011].
this meta-analysis supports the CTLA-4 exon-1 +49 (A/G) polymorphism influencing the risk for developing SLE, especially in Asians.

findings.statement: Lee et al. (2005) found on ethnic stratification that the CTLA4 exon-1 +49 GG genotype was associated with SLE in Asians (OR 1.293, 95% CI 1.031-1.620, P = 0.026), with a similar but nonsignificant effect in European-derived populations (OR 1.268, P = 0.230). The +49 G risk allele was associated in Asians (OR 1.246, 95% CI 1.057-1.469, P = 0.009) but showed no allelic association in Europeans (OR 0.978, P = 0.780).
quotes: Stratification by ethnicity indicates the exon-1 +49 GG genotype is associated with SLE, at least in Asians (OR=1.293, 95% CI=1.031-1.620, P=0.026).
European-derived populations have an effect of similar magnitude (OR=1.268, 95% CI=0.860-1.870, P=0.230), though not significant.
The OR for the exon-1 +49 risk allele (G) in Asians is 1.246 (95% CI=1.057-1.469, P=0.009), while Europeans have no evidence of allelic association (OR=0.978, 95% CI=0.833-1.148, P=0.780).

relevance_reason: Mouse model study showing that restoring FcgRIIB expression on B cells prevents lupus-like autoimmunity in lupus-prone mouse strains; relevant animal model/pathogenesis evidence for SLE.

findings.statement: McGaha et al. (2005) showed that partially restoring levels of the inhibitory Fc receptor FcgRIIB on B cells in lupus-prone mouse strains was enough to restore tolerance and prevent autoimmunity. They concluded that FcgRIIB regulates a common B cell checkpoint in genetically diverse lupus-prone strains, and that modest changes in its expression can lead to either tolerance or autoimmunity. They suggested that increasing FcgRIIB levels on B cells may be an effective way to treat autoimmune diseases.
quotes: we demonstrate that the partial restoration of inhibitory Fc receptor (FcgRIIB) levels on B cells in lupus-prone mouse strains is sufficient to restore tolerance and prevent autoimmunity
FcgRIIB regulates a common B cell checkpoint in genetically diverse lupus-prone mouse strains, and modest changes in its expression can result in either tolerance or autoimmunity
Therefore, increasing FcgammaRIIB levels on B cells may be an effective way to treat autoimmune diseases.

relevance_reason: Functional/pathogenesis study of NK T cell apoptosis in SLE patients involving CD226 and survivin deficiency; no germline variants.

findings.statement: Tao et al. (2005) found that NK T cells from patients with active SLE were highly sensitive to anti-CD95-induced apoptosis compared with those from normal subjects and inactive SLE patients, and that CD226 expression and expression of the antiapoptotic protein survivin were deficient in NK T cells from active SLE patients. CD226 preactivation significantly upregulated survivin expression and activation and rescued active SLE NK T cells from anti-CD95-induced apoptosis.
quotes: NK T cells from active SLE patients are highly sensitive to anti-CD95-induced apoptosis compared with those from normal subjects and inactive SLE patients. CD226 expression is deficient on NK T cells from active SLE patients.
CD226 preactivation significantly up-regulates survivin expression and activation, which can rescue active SLE NK T cells from anti-CD95-induced apoptosis.

findings.statement: In transfected COS7 cells, Tao et al. (2005) showed that anti-CD95-mediated death signals were inhibited by activation of the CD226 pathway through stabilization of caspase-8 and caspase-3 and through activation of survivin. They concluded that deficient expression of CD226 and survivin in NK T cells from active SLE is a molecular basis of the high apoptotic sensitivity of these cells, offering a potential explanation for reduced NK T cell numbers in SLE.
quotes: In transfected COS7 cells, we confirm that anti-CD95-mediated death signals are inhibited by activation of the CD226 pathway through stabilization of caspase-8 and caspase-3 and through activation of survivin.
We therefore conclude that deficient expression of CD226 and survivin in NK T cells from active SLE is a molecular base of high sensitivity of the cells to anti-CD95-induced apoptosis.

relevance_reason: Family-based linkage and association study in Nordic patients reporting that TYK2 and IRF5 SNPs are associated with SLE susceptibility.

findings.statement: Sigurdsson et al. (2005) tested 44 SNPs in 13 type I interferon pathway genes for joint linkage and association with SLE. The study included 679 Swedish, Finnish and Icelandic patients with SLE, 798 unaffected family members and 438 unrelated controls. SNPs in the TYK2 and IRF5 genes gave strong signals in the joint analysis of linkage and association (unadjusted P less than 10(-7)).
quotes: We analyzed 44 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 13 genes from the type I IFN pathway in 679 Swedish, Finnish, and Icelandic patients with SLE, in 798 unaffected family members, and in 438 unrelated control individuals for joint linkage and association with SLE.

In two of the genes--the tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) and IFN regulatory factor 5 (IRF5) genes--we identified SNPs that displayed strong signals in joint analysis of linkage and association (unadjusted P<10(-7)) with SLE.

findings.statement: Sigurdsson et al. (2005) noted that TYK2 binds to the type I interferon receptor complex and that IRF5 regulates type I interferon gene expression. They concluded that their association findings support an SLE disease mechanism involving key components of the type I interferon system.
quotes: TYK2 binds to the type I IFN receptor complex and IRF5 is a regulator of type I IFN gene expression. Thus, our results support a disease mechanism in SLE that involves key components of the type I IFN system.

relevance_reason: This case report describes chondrodysplasia punctata in two brothers whose mother had lupus erythematosus. It belongs in the SLE entry as an associated finding (maternal SLE affecting the fetus), not as a description of SLE itself.

findings.statement: Kozlowski et al. (2004) reported 2 brothers from Cape Town with chondrodysplasia punctata, diagnosed clinically and radiographically. The older brother was born in 1991 and the younger, more severely affected brother in 2000. Their mother had longstanding disseminated lupus erythematosus and epilepsy and was treated with chloroquine and other drugs during both pregnancies. The parents were not consanguineous and the family history was unremarkable.
quotes: Chondrodysplasia punctata (CDP) was diagnosed clinically and radiographically in a male child born in Cape Town in 1991. His only sibling, a brother born in 2000 was similarly but more severely affected.
The boys' mother had longstanding disseminated lupus erythematosus and epilepsy, for which she had been treated with chloraquine and other therapeutic agents during both pregnancies.
The parents were non-consanguineous, and the family history was unremarkable.

findings.statement: Kozlowski et al. (2004) noted that 7 earlier cases of chondrodysplasia punctata linked to maternal lupus erythematosus had been reported. They concluded that maternal lupus erythematosus must be regarded as another cause of chondrodysplasia punctata.
quotes: In addition to these affected brothers, seven previous instances of the association of CDP and maternal lupus erythematosus (MLE) have been reported.
On this basis, MLE must be regarded as yet another causative factor in CDP.

relevance_reason: Association study of DNASE1 polymorphisms in Korean SLE patients; found an association with autoantibody production and did not replicate the reported exon 2 mutation.

findings.statement: Shin et al. (2004) identified 16 SNPs in DNase I (DNASE1) by direct sequencing and genotyped 6 of them in 350 Korean SLE patients and 330 controls. None was significantly associated with risk of SLE. However, the nonsynonymous exon 8 SNP +2373A>G (Gln244Arg) was significantly associated with production of anti-RNP and anti-dsDNA antibodies among SLE patients. Arg/Arg homozygosity was more frequent in patients with anti-RNP antibody than in those without it (31.3% vs 14.4%; P = 0.0006, OR = 2.86).
quotes: Although no significant associations with the risk of SLE were found, logistic regression analyses revealed that one non-synonymous SNPs in exon 8, +2373A>G(Gln244Arg), was significantly associated with an increased risk of the production of anti-RNP and anti-dsDNA antibodies among SLE patients.
The frequency of the homozygous minor allele (Arg/Arg) was much higher in patients who had the anti-RNP antibody (31.3%) than in patients who did not have this antibody (14.4%) (P=0.0006, OR=2.86).

findings.statement: Shin et al. (2004) did not find the DNASE1 exon 2 A/T mutation, previously reported in 2 Japanese SLE patients, in any of 350 Korean SLE patients or 330 controls. Taken together with earlier reports, they concluded that this result strongly suggests the mutation is absent from Caucasian, African, and Asian populations.
quotes: the A/T mutation in exon 2 of DNase reported in two Japanese SLE patients was not present in SLE patients (n=350) or controls (n=330) in our Korean population, which combined with the results of previous reports strongly suggests that the mutation is not present in three major ethnic groups: Caucasian, African and Asian.

relevance_reason: Case-control association study implicating the PTPN22 R620W polymorphism as a susceptibility factor for SLE.

findings.statement: Kyogoku et al. (2004) genotyped 525 independent North American white individuals with SLE and 1,961 white controls for the PTPN22 R620W polymorphism. The SNP was associated with SLE (genotypic P = 0.00009), with minor T allele frequencies of 12.67% in cases and 8.64% in controls. One copy of the T allele (W620) increased SLE risk (OR = 1.37; 95% CI 1.07-1.75), and two copies more than doubled this risk (OR = 4.37; 95% CI 1.98-9.65).
quotes: We genotyped 525 independent North American white individuals with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) for the PTPN22 R620W polymorphism and compared the results with data generated from 1,961 white control individuals.
The R620W SNP was associated with SLE (genotypic P=.00009), with estimated minor (T) allele frequencies of 12.67% in SLE cases and 8.64% in controls.

A single copy of the T allele (W620) increases risk of SLE (odds ratio [OR]=1.37; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.75), and two copies of the allele more than double this risk (OR=4.37; 95% CI 1.98-9.65).

findings.statement: Kyogoku et al. (2004) concluded that, together with association of the same PTPN22 SNP with type 1 diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis, their data provided compelling evidence that PTPN22 plays a fundamental role in regulating the immune system and the development of autoimmunity.
quotes: Together with recent evidence showing association of this SNP with type 1 diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis, these data provide compelling evidence that PTPN22 plays a fundamental role in regulating the immune system and the development of autoimmunity.

relevance_reason: Case-control association study linking an FCGR2B promoter haplotype to SLE susceptibility, plus a functional promoter study.

findings.statement: Su et al. (2004) identified 10 novel SNPs in the promoter region of the FCGR2B gene, which defined two functionally distinct haplotypes in the proximal promoter. In a case-control study of 600 Caucasians, the less frequent FCGR2B promoter haplotype was significantly associated with SLE (odds ratio = 1.65; p = 0.0054). This haplotype was not in linkage disequilibrium with previously identified FCGR2A and FCGR3A polymorphisms, and the association remained after adjustment for them (odds ratio = 1.72; p = 0.0083).
quotes: We have identified 10 novel single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the promoter region of human FCGR2B gene and characterized two functionally distinct haplotypes in its proximal promoter.
Our case-control study in 600 Caucasians indicates a significant association of the less frequent FCGR2B promoter haplotype with the SLE phenotype (odds ratio = 1.65; p = 0.0054).

The FCGR2B haplotype has no linkage disequilibrium with previously identified FCGR2A and FCGR3A polymorphisms, and after adjustment for FCGR2A and FCGR3A, FCGR2B showed a persistent association with SLE (odds ratio = 1.72; p = 0.0083).

findings.statement: In luciferase reporter assays, Su et al. (2004) found that the less frequent FCGR2B promoter haplotype increased reporter gene expression in B lymphoid and myeloid cell lines under both constitutive and stimulated conditions. The authors suggested that an expression variant of FCGR2B is a risk factor for human lupus and implicated FCGR2B in disease pathogenesis.
quotes: In luciferase reporter assays, the less frequent promoter haplotype leads to increased expression of the reporter gene in both B lymphoid and myeloid cell lines under constitutive and stimulated conditions.
These results suggest that an expression variant of FCGR2B is a risk factor for human lupus and implicate FCGR2B in disease pathogenesis.

relevance_reason: Association study and meta-analysis that adds evidence for CTLA4 as an SLE susceptibility gene.

findings.statement: Barreto et al. (2004) tested whether SLE was associated with 2 CTLA4 polymorphisms: an SNP at position +49 of exon 1 and a dinucleotide repeat in the 3-prime UTR. The 3-prime UTR repeat was significantly associated with SLE. One allele conferred susceptibility and another conferred protection. The authors said the associated alleles did not support an allele size-dependent effect of the repeat. Instead, they suggested that the repeat is in linkage disequilibrium with a true causative locus.
quotes: The 3'UTR repeat showed a significant association with SLE, with one allele conferring susceptibility and another conferring protection to the disease.

The associated alleles do not support previous suggestions of an allele size-dependent effect of the 3' UTR polymorphism in autoimmunity development and instead suggest that it is in linkage disequilibrium with a true causative locus.

variants.as_reported: dinucleotide repeat in the 3' untranslated region (3'UTR)

findings.statement: Barreto et al. (2004) found no association between SLE and the CTLA4 exon 1 +49 SNP in their own population. Earlier studies had disagreed on this SNP, so they ran a meta-analysis of 7 published studies plus their own. In the meta-analysis, carriers of the G allele had a significantly increased risk of SLE and carriers of the A allele had a significantly decreased risk.
quotes: No association of the exon 1 SNP with SLE was found in our population.

we performed a meta-analysis including seven previously published studies and the present one. Significantly increased and decreased risks for SLE were found for carriers of the G allele and the A allele, respectively.

variants.as_reported: single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in position +49 of exon 1

relevance_reason: Mouse model: PS1+/- PS2-/- mice develop an SLE-like autoimmune disease; animal model evidence for the SLE entry.

findings.statement: Tournoy et al. (2004) found that mice heterozygous for Ps1 deficiency and homozygous for Ps2 deficiency (PS1+/-PS2-/-), which had considerably lowered PS1 protein, reduced gamma-secretase activity, and impaired beta-catenin downregulation, were normal up to about 6 months of age, when most developed an autoimmune disease with dermatitis, glomerulonephritis, keratitis, and vasculitis resembling human systemic lupus erythematosus. The mice showed B-cell dominated infiltrates, hypergammaglobulinemia with immune complex deposits in several tissues, high-titer nuclear autoantibodies, and an increased CD4+/CD8+ ratio. PS1+/-PS2+/- mice remained healthy, which the authors suggested pointed to a sharply defined minimum of presenilin function.
quotes: Their phenotype is normal up to approximately 6 months, when the majority of the mice develop an autoimmune disease characterized by dermatitis, glomerulonephritis, keratitis and vasculitis, as seen in human systemic lupus erythematosus.
Besides B-cell dominated infiltrates, we observe a hypergammaglobulinemia with immune complex deposits in several tissues, high-titer nuclear autoantibodies and an increased CD4+/CD8+ ratio.
As PS1+/-PS2+/- mice remain healthy, this points towards a sharply defined minimum of PS function.

phenotypes.text: benign skin hyperplasia resembling seborrheic keratosis

relevance_reason: Functional study of SLE pathogenesis showing that lupus T cells upregulate COX-2 (PTGS2) to resist anergy and apoptosis. It also notes that the gene lies in a lupus-susceptibility region on chromosome 1.

findings.statement: Xu et al. (2004) used gene microarray profiling, checked by functional and biochemical studies, to show that activated T cells from SLE patients resisted anergy and apoptosis by strongly upregulating and sustaining COX-2 expression. Inhibiting COX-2 made these anergy-resistant lupus T cells undergo apoptosis by increasing Fas signaling and sharply lowering the survival molecule c-FLIP. The authors noted that the gene encoding COX-2 lies in a lupus-susceptibility region on chromosome 1.
quotes: we establish here that activated T cells of lupus patients resist anergy and apoptosis by markedly upregulating and sustaining cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) expression

Inhibition of COX-2 caused apoptosis of the anergy-resistant lupus T cells by augmenting Fas signaling and markedly decreasing the survival molecule c-FLIP (cellular homolog of viral FLICE inhibitory protein).
Notably, the gene encoding COX-2 is located in a lupus-susceptibility region on chromosome 1.

findings.statement: Xu et al. (2004) used COX-2 inhibitors and Cox-2-deficient mice to confirm that the COX-2/FLIP antiapoptosis program was used selectively by anergy-resistant lupus T cells and not by cancer cells or other autoimmune T cells. Only some COX-2 inhibitors suppressed the production of pathogenic anti-DNA autoantibodies by causing autoimmune T-cell apoptosis, and this effect did not depend on PGE2.
quotes: Studies with COX-2 inhibitors and Cox-2-deficient mice confirmed that this COX-2/FLIP antiapoptosis program is used selectively by anergy-resistant lupus T cells, and not by cancer cells or other autoimmune T cells.

We also found that only some COX-2 inhibitors were able to suppress the production of pathogenic autoantibodies to DNA by causing autoimmune T-cell apoptosis, an effect that was independent of prostaglandin E(2) (PGE(2)).

relevance_reason: Identifies Ltk as a candidate susceptibility gene in the NZB lupus mouse model and reports an association of a similar gain-of-function LTK polymorphism with human SLE.

findings.statement: Li et al. (2004) carried out genome-wide scans for susceptibility genes for aberrant activation of self-reactive CD5+ B1 cells in SLE-prone New Zealand Black (NZB) mice and (NZB x NZW)F1 mice. They identified Ltk, which encodes leukocyte tyrosine kinase, as a possible candidate gene. Sequence and functional analyses showed that NZB mice carry a gain-of-function polymorphism in the LTK kinase domain near YXXM, the binding motif for the p85 subunit of PI3K.
quotes: Our genome-wide scans to search for susceptibility genes for aberrant activation of B1 cells in these mice showed evidence that the gene, Ltk, encoding leukocyte tyrosine kinase (LTK), is a possible candidate.

Sequence and functional analyses of the gene revealed that NZB has a gain-of-function polymorphism in the LTK kinase domain near YXXM, a binding motif of the p85 subunit of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K).

findings.statement: Li et al. (2004) found that SLE patients carried an LTK polymorphism of the same gain-of-function type as the one in NZB mice. Its frequency was significantly higher in patients than in healthy controls.
quotes: SLE patients also had this type of Ltk polymorphism with a significantly higher frequency compared with the healthy controls.

findings.statement: Li et al. (2004) suggested that these polymorphic LTK proteins up-regulate the PI3K pathway. They proposed that this may be one genetic component of susceptibility to abnormal proliferation of self-reactive B cells in SLE.
quotes: Our findings suggest that these polymorphic LTKs cause up-regulation of the PI3K pathway and possibly form one genetic component of susceptibility to abnormal proliferation of self-reactive B cells in SLE.

relevance_reason: Family-based association study linking a CRP 3-prime SNP (CRP 4) to SLE susceptibility and lower basal CRP levels; this is evidence about a susceptibility locus for SLE.

findings.statement: Russell et al. (2004) studied the CRP and APCS genes on 1q23.2 in 586 UK simplex SLE families (2 cohorts). Patients with SLE were more likely to inherit the minor A allele of CRP 4 (rs1205, G>A), a SNP in the 3-prime flanking/untranslated region of CRP. Transmission testing showed this (TRANSMIT P = 0.006 in 498 European-Caucasian families; P = 0.003 in all 586 families; P = 0.0008 in 394 trios).
quotes: We demonstrated using both haplotype analysis and single marker inheritance that the less common A allele of the single nucleotide polymorphism CRP 4 in the 3′ region of the CRP gene is associated with the development of SLE.

This association was strengthened when all 586 families (independent of ethnicity) were analysed (TRANSMIT P = 0.003). When trios only were studied the association with CRP 4 was stronger (143 transmissions compared with 92 non-transmissions P = 0.0008) in all 394 trios.
CRP 4 | 1205 | 1846 | 725333 | 3′ flanking/untranslated region | G>A | 0.33 | 0.14a | 0.32

findings.statement: Russell et al. (2004) found that the rare allele of CRP 4 was also linked with antinuclear autoantibody (ANA) production. In the combined cohorts, the rare allele was over-transmitted to ANA-positive individuals (P = 0.002). There was no association with renal lupus or with other autoantibodies.
quotes: CRP 4 was also associated/linked with the presence of antinuclear autoantibodies (ANA) in probands and seropositive siblings (χ2 = 4.13, P = 0.04).
again there was a significant over-transmission of the rare allele of CRP 4 to ANA positive individuals (median of 25 TRANSMIT iterations χ2 = 12, P = 0.002).
Stratification for renal involvement in the probands (128 families in cohort 1) was negative for association/linkage between renal lupus and any pentraxin polymorphism.

findings.statement: Russell et al. (2004) found that basal serum CRP levels were independently influenced by CRP 4 (P = 0.003) and by CRP 2 (rs1800947, a synonymous G>C change at codon 188; P = 0.01), and this held in both SLE patients and siblings. CRP haplotypes 2 and 5, which carry the CRP 4 minor allele, were associated with lower basal CRP. The authors suggested that reduced basal CRP expression predisposes to SLE, possibly by impairing clearance of cellular debris.
quotes: These analyses indicated correlation with CRP 4 genotype (P = 0.003) and an independent effect from CRP 2 (P = 0.01).
inheritance of minor alleles at both SNPs predicted a CRP level of 0.9 mg/l, whereas inheritance of the common alleles at both SNP predicted a value of 3.4 mg/l.
On the basis of these findings we suggest that reduced basal CRP expression predisposes to the development of SLE.

relevance_reason: Case report of identical triplets concordant for childhood-onset SLE, supporting a genetic contribution to SLE.

findings.statement: Kamat et al. (2003) reported the first case of identical triplets who all developed systemic lupus erythematosus, diagnosed in reverse birth order at ages 8, 9, and 11 years. Although genetically identical, each sibling showed different clinical signs and symptoms, but all 3 had skin rash, fatigue, and biopsy-proven glomerulonephritis at different ages. Laboratory findings were similar, with positive antinuclear, anti-native DNA, and anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies and low complement levels.
quotes: We present herein the first case report of identical triplets who developed systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The children were diagnosed as having SLE in reverse birth order at ages 8, 9, and 11 years.

Although genetically identical, each sibling manifested different clinical signs and symptoms; however, all 3 children did manifest skin rash, fatigue, and biopsy-proven glomerulonephritis at different ages.
Findings of laboratory studies were similar, including positivity for antinuclear antibodies, anti-native DNA, and anti-double-stranded DNA, as well as low levels of complement.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It shows the paper is a family study of systemic lupus erythematosus, which matters for the inheritance section, but no data can be extracted.

findings.statement: LEONHARDT (1964) reported family studies in systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: FAMILY STUDIES IN SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS.

relevance_reason: Only the title was available. It shows a family study of antinuclear antibodies in relatives of patients with SLE, which bears on familial aggregation of the disorder. No results are available.

findings.statement: POLLAK (1964) studied antinuclear antibodies in family members of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: ANTINUCLEAR ANTIBODIES IN FAMILIES OF PATIENTS WITH SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS.

relevance_reason: Mouse model study mapping anxiety-like behavior in SLE-prone NZB/NZW F1 mice to an IFN-alpha-containing region on chromosome 4, with mechanism studies; supports the SLE animal model section.

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2003) carried out genome-wide scans in SLE-prone New Zealand Black (NZB) x New Zealand White (NZW) F1 (B/W F1) mice. They found that a region on NZB chromosome 4 that includes interferon-alpha (IFN-alpha) was significantly linked to anxiety-like behavior. Mice carrying heterozygous NZB/NZW alleles of this susceptibility region on the NZW background also showed anxiety-like behavior, which confirmed the linkage.
quotes: we carried out genome-wide scans, and found that the region including interferon-alpha (IFN-alpha) on NZB chromosome 4 is significantly linked to the anxiety-like behavior seen in SLE-prone New Zealand Black (NZB) x New Zealand White (NZW) F(1) (B/W F(1)) mice
This finding was confirmed by anxiety-like performances of mice with heterozygous NZB/NZW alleles in the susceptibility region onto the NZW background.

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2003) found that neuronal IFN-alpha and corticotropin-releasing hormone levels were higher in B/W F1 mice than in NZW mice. Blocking the mu-1 opioid receptor or corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor 1 partially overcame the anxiety-like behavior of B/W F1 mice. Pretreatment with a mu-1 opioid receptor antagonist abolished the anxiety-like behavior seen in IFN-alpha-treated NZW mice. The authors suggested that a genetically determined endogenous excess of IFN-alpha in the brain may form one aspect of the anxiety-like behavior seen in SLE-prone mice.
quotes: In B/W F(1) mice, neuronal IFN-alpha levels were elevated, and blockade of the micro (1) opioid receptor or corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor 1, possible downstream effectors for IFN-alpha in the brain partially overcame the anxiety-like behavior seen in the B/W F(1) mice.
Furthermore, pretreatment of micro (1) opioid receptor antagonist abolished anxiety-like behaviour seen in IFN-alpha-treated NZW mice.
Our data suggest that a genetically determined endogenous excess amount of IFN-alpha in the brain may form one aspect of anxiety-like behavior seen in SLE-prone mice.

relevance_reason: Gene expression profiling study identifying an IFN-inducible signature in SLE PBMCs that is associated with severe disease; it adds pathogenesis evidence relevant to the SLE entry.

findings.statement: Baechler et al. (2003) used global gene expression profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells and identified distinct patterns of gene expression that distinguished most SLE patients from healthy controls. About half of the patients showed dysregulated expression of genes in the interferon (IFN) pathway. The authors suggested that these results gave insight into the genetic pathways underlying SLE.
quotes: We used global gene expression profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells to identify distinct patterns of gene expression that distinguish most SLE patients from healthy controls.
Strikingly, about half of the patients studied showed dysregulated expression of genes in the IFN pathway.

findings.statement: Baechler et al. (2003) found that the IFN gene expression signature marked more severe SLE involving the kidneys, hematopoietic cells, and/or the central nervous system. They suggested that it identified a subgroup of patients who might benefit from therapies targeting the IFN pathway.
quotes: this IFN gene expression "signature" served as a marker for more severe disease involving the kidneys, hematopoetic cells, and/or the central nervous system.
identify a subgroup of patients who may benefit from therapies targeting the IFN pathway.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormality of blood and blood-forming tissues

relevance_reason: Case-control admixture study showing that SLE risk is associated with west African genetic ancestry in Trinidad. It supports a genetic basis for the ethnic difference in SLE risk.

findings.statement: Molokhia et al. (2003) studied 124 SLE cases and 219 matched controls living in Trinidad. They restricted the admixture analysis to 52 cases and 107 controls who reported no Indian or Chinese ancestry, and typed these individuals with 26 SNPs and 5 insertion/deletion polymorphisms that differ strongly in frequency between west African, European, and Native American populations. Mean west African admixture was 0.81 in cases and 0.74 in controls (P = 0.01). The risk ratio for SLE per unit change in admixture was 32.5 (95% CI 2.0-518), and adjusting for socioeconomic status changed it only slightly (28.4, 95% CI 1.7-485).
quotes: 124 cases of SLE and 219 matched controls resident in Trinidad were studied. Analysis of admixture was restricted to 52 cases and 107 controls who reported no Indian or Chinese ancestry.

Mean west African admixture (M) was 0.81 in cases and 0.74 in controls (P=0.01). The risk ratio for SLE associated with unit change in M was estimated as 32.5 with a 95% confidence interval (CI) of 2.0-518.
Adjustment for measures of socioeconomic status (household amenities in childhood and years of education) altered this risk ratio only slightly (adjusted risk ratio: 28.4, 95% CI 1.7-485).

findings.statement: Molokhia et al. (2003) concluded that their results support an additive genetic model for the ethnic difference in SLE risk between west Africans and Europeans. They favored this over an environmental explanation or an 'overdominant' model, and stated that this lays a basis for localizing the responsible genes by admixture mapping.
quotes: These results support an additive genetic model for the ethnic difference in risk of SLE between west Africans and Europeans, rather than an environmental explanation or an "overdominant" model in which risk is higher in heterozygous than in homozygous individuals.

relevance_reason: Mouse model study showing that an agonistic anti-CD137 antibody blocks lupus-like autoimmune disease in Fas-deficient MRL/lpr mice; relevant to animal models and treatment of SLE.

findings.statement: Sun et al. (2002) found that treating Fas-deficient MRL/lpr mice with an agonistic monoclonal antibody to CD137 (2A) blocked lymphadenopathy and spontaneous autoimmune disease and led to prolonged survival. The 2A treatment quickly increased IFN-gamma production and depleted autoreactive B cells and abnormal double-negative T cells. The authors suggested this happened through increased apoptosis by Fas- and TNF receptor-independent mechanisms. They concluded that agonistic antibodies against costimulatory molecules might be used to delete autoreactive lymphocytes and block autoimmune disease progression.
quotes: Here we report that treatment with an agonistic monoclonal antibody to CD137 (2A) blocks lymphadenopathy and spontaneous autoimmune diseases in Fas-deficient MRL/lpr mice, ultimately leading to their prolonged survival.

Notably, 2A treatment rapidly augments IFN-gamma production, and induces the depletion of autoreactive B cells and abnormal double-negative T cells, possibly by increasing their apoptosis through Fas- and TNF receptor-independent mechanisms.

relevance_reason: This paper reports that an intronic regulatory SNP in PDCD1, which lies within the SLEB2 susceptibility locus, is associated with susceptibility to SLE in Europeans and Mexicans.

findings.statement: Within the SLEB2 susceptibility locus, which they had previously identified in Nordic multi-case families, Prokunina et al. (2002) studied 2,510 individuals for SNPs they identified in PDCD1. The individuals came from 5 independent sets of families and also included unrelated individuals with SLE. One intronic SNP in PDCD1 was associated with SLE in Europeans: it was found in 12% of affected individuals versus 5% of controls (P = 0.00001, relative risk = 2.6). It was also associated with SLE in Mexicans, where it was found in 7% of affected individuals versus 2% of controls (P = 0.0009, relative risk = 3.5).
quotes: Here, we analyzed 2,510 individuals, including members of five independent sets of families as well as unrelated individuals affected with SLE, for single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that we identified in PDCD1.

We show that one intronic SNP in PDCD1 is associated with development of SLE in Europeans (found in 12% of affected individuals versus 5% of controls; P = 0.00001, r.r. (relative risk) = 2.6) and Mexicans (found in 7% of affected individuals versus 2% of controls; P = 0.0009, r.r. = 3.5).

findings.statement: Prokunina et al. (2002) found that the SLE-associated allele of the intronic PDCD1 SNP alters a binding site for the transcription factor RUNX1 (AML1) in an intronic enhancer. They suggested that this is a mechanism by which the SNP could contribute to the development of SLE.
quotes: The associated allele of this SNP alters a binding site for the runt-related transcription factor 1 (RUNX1, also called AML1) located in an intronic enhancer, suggesting a mechanism through which it can contribute to the development of SLE in humans.

findings.statement: Prokunina et al. (2002) noted that they had previously reported a susceptibility locus, SLEB2, in Nordic multi-case SLE families. They regarded PDCD1 as the strongest candidate gene within that locus.
quotes: We previously reported a susceptibility locus (SLEB2) for Nordic multi-case families. Within this locus, the programmed cell death 1 gene (PDCD1, also called PD-1) was considered the strongest candidate for association with the disease.

findings.statement: Prokunina et al. (2002) stated that SLE is a complex autoimmune disease that affects 0.05% of the Western population, mostly women.
quotes: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE, OMIM 152700) is a complex autoimmune disease that affects 0.05% of the Western population, predominantly women.

relevance_reason: Linkage study in multiplex SLE pedigrees stratified by thrombocytopenia, identifying susceptibility loci at 1q22-23 and 11p13 and clinical associations.

findings.statement: Scofield et al. (2003) selected 38 of 184 SLE-multiplex pedigrees that contained an SLE patient with thrombocytopenia (platelets less than 100,000/microL) and established linkage at 1q22-23 (maximum lod = 3.71) in these 38 pedigrees and at 11p13 (maximum lod = 5.72) in the 13 African American pedigrees among them.
quotes: We selected the 38 pedigrees that had an SLE patient with thrombocytopenia (platelets, < 10 x 10(9)/L [< 100,000/microL]) from a collection of 184 pedigrees multiplex for SLE.
Linkages were established at 1q22-23 (maximum logarithm of odds [lod(max)] = 3.71) in the 38 pedigrees and at 11p13 (lod(max) = 5.72) in the 13 African American pedigrees.

findings.statement: Scofield et al. (2003) found that in SLE multiplex pedigrees, thrombocytopenia was associated with nephritis, serositis, neuropsychiatric involvement, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, anti-double-stranded DNA, and antiphospholipid antibody, and that SLE was more severe in families with a thrombocytopenic SLE patient whether or not thrombocytopenia in an individual patient was considered. They concluded that thrombocytopenia is a component of a severe familial form of SLE.
quotes: Nephritis, serositis, neuropsychiatric involvement, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, anti-double-stranded DNA, and antiphospholipid antibody were associated with thrombocytopenia.
Other results show that SLE is more severe in the families with a thrombocytopenic SLE patient, whether or not thrombocytopenia in an individual patient is considered.

relevance_reason: Linkage study in 87 multicase SLE families mapping a major susceptibility locus to 1q31; also tested a CD45 mutation.

findings.statement: Johanneson et al. (2002) genotyped 87 multicase SLE families from European (Iceland, Sweden, England, Norway, Italy, and Greece) and recently admixed (Mexico, Colombia, and the United States) populations for 62 microsatellite markers on chromosome 1. Parametric two-point linkage analysis found 6 regions (1p36, 1p21, 1q23, 1q25, 1q31, and 1q43) with lod scores of 1.50 or higher, all previously described, with contributions differing by population of origin.
quotes: A set of 87 multicase families with systemic lupus erythemathosus (SLE) from European (Iceland, Sweden, England, Norway, Italy, and Greece) and recently admixed (Mexico, Colombia, and the United States) populations were genotyped and analyzed for 62 microsatellite markers on chromosome 1.

By parametric two-point linkage analysis, six regions (1p36, 1p21, 1q23, 1q25, 1q31, and 1q43) were identified that have LOD scores of Z>or=1.50, with different contributions, depending on the population of origin of the families (European or admixed American).
findings.population: European (Iceland, Sweden, England, Norway, Italy, Greece); admixed American (Mexico, Colombia, United States)

findings.statement: Johanneson et al. (2002) found a significant 3-point lod score of 3.79 at 1q31, contributed by families from all populations with several markers under the same parametric model, and concluded that this locus contains a major susceptibility gene important to SLE in general populations.
quotes: The locus at 1q31 showed a significant three-point LOD score of Z=3.79 and was contributed by families from all populations, with several markers and under the same parametric model.
We conclude that the locus at 1q31 contains a major susceptibility gene, important to SLE in general populations.

findings.statement: Johanneson et al. (2002) found that analysis of a known mutation in the CD45 gene did not support a role for this mutation in SLE.
quotes: Analysis of a known mutation in the CD45 gene did not support the role that this mutation plays in disease.

relevance_reason: This is a review of SLE genetics. It summarizes familial aggregation, candidate-gene associations and linkage loci that have significant support and are replicated.

findings.statement: Kelly et al. (2002) noted that SLE shows familial aggregation, with lambda(s) estimates of 10 to 20 and a monozygotic twin concordance rate above 20.
quotes: With lambda(s) estimates of 10 to 20 and other evidence of familial aggregation, as well as a monozygotic twin concordance rate >20, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) would appear to be a very promising phenotype using modern genetic approaches.

findings.statement: Kelly et al. (2002) reviewed completed linkage studies of pedigrees multiplex for SLE. These studies identified 60 susceptibility loci. Seven of them met or exceeded the threshold for significant linkage (LOD at least 3.3 or P at most 0.00005): 1q22-23, 1q41, 2q37, 4p16, 6p21-11, 16q13 and 17p13. Linkage at 1q41, 4p16 and 6p21 had been independently confirmed. For 1q22-23 and 2q37 there was additional suggestive evidence.
quotes: The completed genetic linkage studies performed on various collections of pedigrees multiplex for SLE have identified 60 susceptibility loci with varying degrees of evidence for linkage in man.
Seven of these meet or exceed the threshold for significant linkage (LOD > or = 3.3 or P < or = 0.00005) at 1q22-23, 1q41, 2q37, 4p16, 6p21-11, 16q13 and 17p13.

Evidence that these linkages can be reproduced range from outright independent confirmation (1q41, 4p16 and 6p21) to additional suggestive evidence in the genomic region of the purported linkage (1q22-23 and 2q37).

findings.statement: Kelly et al. (2002) observed that the SLE linkages usually dominate in one ethnicity or another. They suggested that the responsible polymorphisms will also vary by ethnicity.
quotes: In addition, these linkages usually dominate in one ethnicity or another, suggesting that the responsible polymorphisms, once identified, will also vary by ethnicity.

findings.statement: Kelly et al. (2002) noted that SLE has known genetic associations at numerous candidate loci, including various HLA alleles, complement component genes and Fc-gamma receptors. Murine lupus models had provided additional candidate genes and potential syntenic linkages.
quotes: Indeed, genetic associations are already known at numerous candidate loci including various HLA alleles, complement component genes, Fcgamma receptors, and others, and murine genetic studies of lupus models have provided additional candidate genes and potential syntenic linkages to evaluate in man.

relevance_reason: Linkage study identifying SLE susceptibility loci (SLEN1, SLEN2, SLEN3) in pedigrees stratified by renal disease; mapping evidence for SLE.

findings.statement: Quintero-Del-Rio et al. (2002) evaluated genome scan data from more than 300 microsatellite markers in 75 SLE pedigrees with at least 1 SLE patient meeting the ACR renal criterion. Parametric analysis gave a maximum screening lod score of 3.16 at 10q22.3 in European American pedigrees, and multipoint sib-pair regression analysis gave P = 0.0000008 at 10q22.3 in European Americans; this locus was designated SLEN1 and had not been previously described.
quotes: First, we evaluated genome scan data from >300 microsatellite markers in the 75 pedigrees that had at least one SLE affected with the SLE renal criterion.
A maximum-likelihood parametric model approach produced a maximum screening LOD score of 3.16 at 10q22.3 in the European-American (EA) pedigrees.
A multipoint sib-pair regression analysis produced P = 0.0000008 in EA at 10q22.3 (SLEN1)

phenotypes.text: systemic lupus erythematosus with renal disease

findings.statement: In the same 75 pedigrees, Quintero-Del-Rio et al. (2002) found a maximum screening lod score of 2.58 at 11p15.6 in African American pedigrees, and sib-pair regression analysis gave P = 0.000001 at 2q34-35 in African Americans (SLEN2). The 2q34-35 locus had not been previously described.
quotes: The African-American (AA) pedigrees obtained a maximum screening LOD score of 2.58 at 11p15.6.
P = 0.000001 in AA at 2q34-35 (SLEN2)

findings.statement: Quintero-Del-Rio et al. (2002) studied 35 pedigrees with 2 or more SLE patients with renal disease and found a lod score of 3.34 at 11p15.6 in African American pedigrees (SLEN3). Sib-pair analysis in these pedigrees also showed P = 0.00003 at 4q13.1 in European Americans, and P = 0.00003 at 11p13 and P = 0.00007 at 3q23 in African Americans. The authors concluded that multiple genetic linkages are related to the renal criterion in SLE.
quotes: A second stratification strategy explored the renal criterion in 35 pedigrees with two or more SLE patients with renal disease and produced a LOD score of 3.34 at 11p15.6 in AA (SLEN3).
Sib-pair analysis in these 35 pedigrees revealed P = 0.00003 at 4q13.1 in EA, P = 0.00003 at 11p13 and 0.00007 at 3q23 in AA.
Thus, multiple genetic linkages are related to the renal criterion in SLE.

findings.statement: Quintero-Del-Rio et al. (2002) noted that renal disease occurs in 40 to 75% of SLE patients and contributes significantly to morbidity and mortality.
quotes: Renal disease occurs in 40-75% of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients and significantly contributes to morbidity and mortality.

relevance_reason: Family-based association and haplotype mapping study identifying HLA class II DRB1/DQB1 risk haplotypes for SLE.

findings.statement: Graham et al. (2002) genotyped a dense map of polymorphic microsatellites across the HLA region in a large collection of SLE families and identified 3 distinct haplotypes spanning the class II region that showed transmission distortion. DRB1 and DQB1 typing of founders showed that these haplotypes carried DRB1*1501/DQB1*0602, DRB1*0801/DQB1*0402, and DRB1*0301/DQB1*0201, respectively. The authors concluded that HLA class II haplotypes containing DRB1 and DQB1 alleles are strong risk factors for human SLE.
quotes: Using a dense map of polymorphic microsatellites across the HLA region in a large collection of families with SLE, we identified three distinct haplotypes that encompassed the class II region and exhibited transmission distortion.
DRB1 and DQB1 typing of founders showed that the three haplotypes contained DRB1*1501/ DQB1*0602, DRB1*0801/ DQB1*0402, and DRB1*0301/DQB1*0201 alleles, respectively.
We conclude that HLA class II haplotypes containing DRB1 and DQB1 alleles are strong risk factors for human SLE.

findings.statement: By visualizing ancestral recombinants, Graham et al. (2002) narrowed the SLE-associated haplotypes containing DRB1*1501 and DRB1*0801 to a region of about 500 kb.
quotes: By visualizing ancestral recombinants, we narrowed the disease-associated haplotypes containing DRB1*1501 and DRB1*0801 to an approximately 500-kb region.

relevance_reason: Case-control association study identifying FCGR2B I232T and FCGR3A-176F/F as susceptibility factors for SLE in Japanese patients.

findings.statement: Kyogoku et al. (2002) screened FCGR2B for variants by direct sequencing and PCR-SSCP of cDNA and identified a SNP, c.695T>C, causing a nonsynonymous ile232-to-thr (I232T) substitution in the transmembrane domain. In 193 Japanese patients with SLE and 303 healthy controls, the frequency of the 232T/T genotype was significantly increased in patients, and the authors concluded that FCGR2B I232T is associated with susceptibility to SLE in the Japanese.
quotes: We detected a single-nucleotide polymorphism in FCGR2B, (c.695T>C), coding for a nonsynonymous substitution, Ile232Thr (I232T), within the transmembrane domain. The frequency of the 232T/T genotype was significantly increased in SLE patients compared with healthy individuals.
Association with SLE was analyzed in 193 Japanese patients with SLE and 303 healthy individuals.
These results demonstrate the association of a new polymorphism of FCGR2B (I232T) with susceptibility to SLE in the Japanese.

findings.statement: Kyogoku et al. (2002) genotyped the same 193 Japanese SLE patients and 303 controls for FCGR2A-131R/H, FCGR3A-176V/F, and FCGR3B-NA1/2 polymorphisms and found significant association of FCGR3A-176F/F with SLE. Two-locus analyses suggested that both FCGR2B and FCGR3A may contribute to SLE susceptibility, whereas the previously reported FCGR3B association was considered secondary, deriving from strong linkage disequilibrium with FCGR2B.
quotes: When the same patients and controls were also genotyped for FCGR2A-131R/H, FCGR3A-176V/F, and FCGR3B-NA1/2 polymorphisms, FCGR3A-176F/F showed significant association.

Two-locus analyses suggested that both FCGR2B and FCGR3A may contribute to SLE susceptibility, while the previously reported association of FCGR3B was considered to be secondary and derived from strong linkage disequilibrium with FCGR2B.

relevance_reason: Functional study of how autoreactive B cells are activated. It shows that chromatin-IgG immune complexes activate rheumatoid factor B cells by engaging both the antigen receptor and TLR9. This bears on how systemic autoimmune disease, including antinuclear autoantibody production, develops.

findings.statement: Leadbetter et al. (2002) showed that rheumatoid factor (RF)-positive B cells were effectively activated by IgG2a-chromatin immune complexes. Activation required the antigen receptor and a member of the MyD88-dependent Toll-like receptor (TLR) family to be engaged together, and inhibitor studies implicated TLR9. The authors concluded that this links innate and adaptive immunity in the development of systemic autoimmune disease. They also said it explains why so many autoantibodies react with nucleic acid-protein particles.
quotes: Here we show that effective activation of RF+ B cells is mediated by IgG2a-chromatin immune complexes and requires the synergistic engagement of the antigen receptor and a member of the MyD88-dependent Toll-like receptor (TLR) family. Inhibitor studies implicate TLR9.

These data establish a critical link between the innate and adaptive immune systems in the development of systemic autoimmune disease and explain the preponderance of autoantibodies reactive with nucleic acid-protein particles.

relevance_reason: Family-based clinical study showing that renal disease in SLE clusters in multiplex families with affected males, suggesting a familial (genetic) contribution to phenotype.

findings.statement: Stein et al. (2002) analyzed 372 affected individuals from 160 multiplex SLE pedigrees, 25 of which contained at least 1 affected male relative. Renal disease was significantly more frequent in female family members with an affected male relative than in those without (68% vs 43%; P = 0.002), a trend that persisted after stratification by race and was most pronounced in European Americans.
quotes: A total of 372 affected individuals from 160 multiplex SLE pedigrees were analyzed. Twenty-five of these pedigrees contained at least 1 affected male relative.

The presence of renal disease was significantly increased in female family members with an affected male relative when compared with those with no affected male relative (68% and 43%, respectively; P = 0.002).
This trend remained after stratifying by race and was most pronounced in European Americans.

findings.statement: Stein et al. (2002) concluded that the increased prevalence of renal disease previously reported in men with SLE is largely a familial rather than a sex-based difference, at least in multiplex SLE families. A familial basis for differences in hematologic and immunologic manifestations was also suggested, whereas arthritis and dermatologic features appeared most influenced by sex.
quotes: Our results demonstrate that the increased prevalence of renal disease previously reported in men with SLE is, in large part, a familial rather than sex-based difference, at least in multiplex SLE families.
A familial basis for differences in hematologic and immunologic manifestations was also suggested, while arthritis and dermatologic features appeared to be most influenced by sex.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormality of blood and blood-forming tissues

relevance_reason: Functional/pathogenesis study showing that IFN-alpha in SLE serum drives monocyte-to-dendritic cell differentiation, proposed as a mechanism of autoimmunity in SLE.

findings.statement: Blanco et al. (2001) found that blood monocytes from SLE patients functioned as antigen-presenting cells in vitro, and that SLE patient serum induced normal monocytes to differentiate into dendritic cells (DCs). These DCs could capture antigens from dying cells and present them to CD4-positive T cells.
quotes: monocytes from SLE patients' blood were found to function as antigen-presenting cells, in vitro
serum from SLE patients induced normal monocytes to differentiate into DCs. These DCs could capture antigens from dying cells and present them to CD4-positive T cells.

findings.statement: Blanco et al. (2001) showed that the capacity of SLE patient serum to induce DC differentiation correlated with disease activity and depended on interferon-alpha (IFN-alpha). They proposed that unabated induction of DCs by IFN-alpha may drive the autoimmune response in SLE.
quotes: The capacity of SLE patients' serum to induce DC differentiation correlated with disease activity and depended on the actions of interferon-alpha (IFN-alpha).
Thus, unabated induction of DCs by IFN-alpha may drive the autoimmune response in SLE.

relevance_reason: Functional/pathogenesis study showing that a subset of anti-dsDNA antibodies in SLE cross-react with the NMDA receptor subunits NR2a/NR2b and cause neuronal apoptosis. This is a possible mechanism for CNS lupus.

findings.statement: DeGiorgio et al. (2001) noted that the pentapeptide Asp/Glu-Trp-Asp/Glu-Tyr-Ser/Gly, which they had previously shown to mimic double-stranded DNA, is also present in the extracellular domain of the murine and human NMDA receptor subunits NR2a and NR2b. They showed that both murine and human anti-DNA antibodies recognize the NR2 receptor, and that anti-DNA antibodies with this cross-reactivity mediate apoptotic death of neurons in vivo and in vitro.
quotes: This sequence is also present in the extracellular domain of murine and human NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate) receptor subunits NR2a and NR2b.
Here we show that the NR2 receptor is recognized by both murine and human anti-DNA antibodies.
Moreover, anti-DNA antibodies with this cross-reactivity mediate apoptotic death of neurons in vivo and in vitro.

findings.statement: DeGiorgio et al. (2001) found that the cerebrospinal fluid of a patient with SLE contained anti-DNA/NR2 cross-reactive antibodies and caused neuronal death through an apoptotic pathway. The authors concluded that lupus antibodies cross-react with DNA and NMDA receptors, get into the cerebrospinal fluid, and may mediate non-thrombotic and non-vasculitic CNS abnormalities.
quotes: Finally, we show that the cerebrospinal fluid of a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus contains these antibodies and also mediates neuronal death via an apoptotic pathway.

These observations indicate that lupus antibodies cross-react with DNA and NMDA receptors, gain access to cerebrospinal fluid and may mediate non-thrombotic and non-vasculitic abnormalities of the central nervous system.

relevance_reason: The paper reports SLE patients carrying a heterozygous nonsense mutation in DNASE1 with low DNASE1 activity. It links the gene directly to the SLE phenotype.

findings.statement: Yasutomo et al. (2001) found a heterozygous nonsense mutation in exon 2 of the DNASE1 gene in 2 patients with systemic lupus erythematosus. The patients had decreased DNASE1 activity and an extremely high IgG titer against nucleosomal antigens. The authors concluded that the data were consistent with the hypothesis that low DNASE1 activity is directly connected to the progression of human SLE.
quotes: Here we describe two patients with a heterozygous nonsense mutation in exon 2 of DNASE1, decreased DNASE1 activity and an extremely high immunoglobulin G titer against nucleosomal antigens.
These data are consistent with the hypothesis that a direct connection exists between low activity of DNASE1 and progression of human SLE.

variants.as_reported: heterozygous nonsense mutation in exon 2 of DNASE1

phenotypes.text: extremely high IgG titer against nucleosomal antigens

findings.statement: Yasutomo et al. (2001) noted that mice deficient in Dnase1 develop an SLE-like syndrome.
quotes: Mice deficient in deoxyribonuclease I (Dnase1) develop an SLE-like syndrome.

relevance_reason: The paper gives a molecular explanation for why T cells from SLE patients make too little IL-2: phosphorylated CREM binds the IL-2 promoter and represses transcription. This is pathogenesis evidence for the disorder.

findings.statement: Solomou et al. (2001) found that nuclear extracts from unstimulated SLE T cells, unlike those from normal T cells, contained increased amounts of phosphorylated cAMP-responsive element modulator (p-CREM), which bound the -180 site of the IL-2 promoter. After stimulation, normal T-cell extracts showed increased binding of phosphorylated CREB (p-CREB) to this site. Stimulated SLE T-cell extracts showed mainly p-CREM binding and less p-CREB binding. In SLE T cells, p-CREM bound the transcriptional coactivators CREB binding protein and p300.
quotes: nuclear extracts from unstimulated SLE T cells, unlike extracts from normal T cells, express increased amounts of phosphorylated cAMP-responsive element modulator (p-CREM) that binds the -180 site of the IL-2 promoter
whereas nuclear extracts from stimulated SLE T cells display primarily p-CREM and decreased p-CREB binding
In SLE T cells, p-CREM bound to the transcriptional coactivators, CREB binding protein and p300.

phenotypes.text: decreased IL-2 production by T cells

findings.statement: Solomou et al. (2001) found that higher p-CREM expression correlated with lower IL-2 production. A reporter gene driven by the IL-2 promoter -180 site was transcribed more strongly in normal T cells but was suppressed in SLE T cells. The authors concluded that transcriptional repression is responsible for the decreased IL-2 production by SLE T cells.
quotes: Increased expression of p-CREM correlated with decreased production of IL-2.
The transcription of a reporter gene driven by the -180 site was enhanced in normal T cells, but was suppressed in SLE T cells.
These experiments demonstrate that transcriptional repression is responsible for the decreased production of IL-2 by SLE T cells.

relevance_reason: Case-control association study linking IL6 3' minisatellite alleles with SLE susceptibility, plus functional data on IL-6 expression.

findings.statement: Linker-Israeli et al. (1999) genotyped the AT-rich minisatellite in the 3-prime flanking region and the 5-prime promoter-enhancer of the IL6 gene in 146 SLE patients and 139 controls. The 3-prime minisatellite allele distribution differed significantly between SLE patients and controls in both Caucasians (P = 0.001) and African Americans (P = 0.006); short alleles (792 bp or less) were seen exclusively in SLE patients, whereas the 828-bp allele was overrepresented in controls. There was no preferential association of SLE with G/C alleles in the 5-prime region.
quotes: The AT-rich minisatellite allele distribution pattern was significantly different in SLE (n = 146) as compared to 139 controls (chi 2(7) = 48.97, P = 0.001, Caucasians; and chi 2(7) = 19.93, P = 0.006, African-Americans).
In either race, short allele sizes (< or = 792 bp) were seen exclusively in SLE patients (P = 0.001), whereas the 828-bp allele was over-represented in controls (P = 0.015 and 0.002).
In contrast, there was no preferential association of SLE with G/C alleles in the 5' region of the IL-6 gene.

variants.as_reported: 3' AT-rich minisatellite short alleles (< or = 792 bp)

findings.statement: Linker-Israeli et al. (1999) found that B lymphoblastoid cells from patients with 1 or 2 SLE-associated IL6 3-prime minisatellite alleles secreted 3- to 4-fold higher IL-6 levels than cells without these alleles, individuals with SLE-associated alleles had about 4-fold higher percentages of IL-6-positive monocytes, and IL-6 mRNA stability was significantly enhanced in lupus patients carrying SLE-associated alleles, suggesting biologic significance of these alleles.
quotes: B lymphoblastoid cells of patients having one or two SLE-associated alleles secreted IL-6 in 3- to 4-fold higher levels than non-allelic cells (P < 0.05)
higher percentages (approximately 4-fold) of IL-6 positive monocytes were observed in individuals having SLE-associated IL-6 alleles
in lupus patients having SLE-associated minisatellite alleles, IL-6 mRNA stability was significantly enhanced

relevance_reason: Reports elevated serum BLyS (TNFSF13B) in SLE patients with functional activity and association with anti-dsDNA antibodies; pathogenesis/biomarker evidence.

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2001) demonstrated significant elevations of B lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS) in sera of patients with SLE. BLyS isolated from SLE patient sera had the same molecular weight as the natural soluble form and stimulated B cell activation in vitro. The authors suggested that BLyS likely plays a critical role in triggering activation of self-antigen-driven autoimmune B cells in human SLE and may provide an effective therapeutic target.
quotes: Here, we demonstrate significant elevations of BLyS in the patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
The BLyS isolated from the sera of SLE patients had the same m.w. as the natural soluble form and was able to stimulate B cell activation in vitro.
likely plays a critical role in triggering activation of self-Ag-driven autoimmune B cells in human SLE. BLyS may provide an effective therapeutic target in systemic autoimmunity.

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2001) found that increased BLyS in SLE patients was partially associated with higher levels of anti-dsDNA antibodies of the IgG, IgM, and IgA classes, but was not associated with disease activity; they suggested BLyS may be a useful marker for early activation of an autoimmune diathesis.
quotes: Increased BLyS in SLE patients was partially associated with higher levels of anti-dsDNA Ab of the IgG, IgM, and IgA classes, but not associated with the disease activity.
Our results suggest that BLyS may be a useful marker for early activation of an autoimmune diathesis

relevance_reason: Genome-wide linkage scan of SLE that found a new linkage region at 4p16-15.2 and a possible epistatic interaction with 5p15.

findings.statement: Gray-McGuire et al. (2000) performed a genome scan of 126 pedigrees multiplex for SLE, including 469 sibling pairs (affected and unaffected) and 175 affected relative pairs. They used revised multipoint Haseman-Elston regression and conditional logistic regression and identified a novel linkage to chromosome 4p16-15.2 (P = 0.0003 and lod = 3.84). They confirmed this linkage in European American families using an independent pedigree collection.
quotes: We present here the results of a genome scan of 126 pedigrees multiplex for SLE, including 469 sibling pairs (affected and unaffected) and 175 affected relative pairs.
we identify a novel linkage to chromosome 4p16-15.2 (P=.0003 and LOD=3.84)
We confirm the evidence of linkage to chromosome 4p16-15.2 in European American families using data from an independent pedigree collection.

findings.statement: Gray-McGuire et al. (2000) presented evidence of an epistatic interaction between chromosome 4p16-15.2 and chromosome 5p15 in their European American SLE families.
quotes: present evidence of an epistatic interaction between chromosome 4p16-15.2 and chromosome 5p15 in our European American families

findings.statement: Gray-McGuire et al. (2000) reported that their data supported the published results of 3 independent studies for 9 regions reported to be linked to SLE. Their data also agreed with earlier published results from a subset of the same data for 3 regions.
quotes: our data support the published results of three independent studies for nine purportedly linked regions and agree with the previously published results from a subset of these data for three regions

relevance_reason: Animal model: Dnase1-deficient mice develop SLE features; also reports reduced serum DNASE1 activity in human SLE patients.

findings.statement: Napirei et al. (2000) generated Dnase1-deficient mice by gene targeting and found that they showed classical symptoms of SLE, namely antinuclear antibodies, deposition of immune complexes in glomeruli, and full-blown glomerulonephritis, in a Dnase1-dose-dependent manner. The authors suggested that lack or reduction of Dnase1 is a critical factor in the initiation of human SLE.
quotes: we have generated Dnase1-deficient mice by gene targeting. We report here that these animals show the classical symptoms of SLE, namely the presence of ANA, the deposition of immune complexes in glomeruli and full-blown glomerulonephritis in a Dnase1-dose-dependent manner.
Our findings suggest that lack or reduction of Dnase1 is a critical factor in the initiation of human SLE.

findings.statement: Napirei et al. (2000) found, in agreement with earlier reports, that serum DNASE1 activities were lower in SLE patients than in normal subjects.
quotes: Moreover, in agreement with earlier reports, we found Dnase1 activities in serum to be lower in SLE patients than in normal subjects.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal circulating enzyme concentration or activity

relevance_reason: Animal model and pathogenesis evidence implicating zTNF4 (BAFF/BLyS) and its receptors TACI and BCMA in SLE, including transgenic mice and treatment with TACI-Ig in NZBWF1 lupus mice.

findings.statement: Gross et al. (2000) found that transgenic mice overexpressing zTNF4 (BLyS, BAFF, TALL-1, THANK), a member of the TNF ligand family, in lymphoid cells developed symptoms characteristic of SLE and had an expanded rare population of splenic B-1a lymphocytes. Circulating zTNF4 was also more abundant in NZBWF1 and MRL-lpr/lpr mice during the onset and progression of SLE.
quotes: Transgenic animals overexpressing zTNF4 in lymphoid cells develop symptoms characteristic of systemic lupus erythaematosus (SLE) and expand a rare population of splenic B-Ia lymphocytes.
circulating zTNF4 is more abundant in NZBWF1 and MRL-lpr/lpr mice during the onset and progression of SLE.

findings.statement: Gross et al. (2000) identified 2 TNF receptor family members, TACI and BCMA, as receptors that bind zTNF4. The authors concluded that zTNF4 and its receptors are involved in the development of SLE.
quotes: We have identified two TNF receptor family members, TACI and BCMA, that bind zTNF4.
These findings demonstrate the involvement of zTNF4 and its receptors in the development of SLE

findings.statement: Gross et al. (2000) showed that treating NZBWF1 lupus-prone mice with a soluble TACI-Ig fusion protein inhibited the development of proteinuria and prolonged survival. They suggested that TACI-Ig was a promising treatment for autoimmune disease in humans.
quotes: Treatment of NZBWF1 mice with soluble TACI-Ig fusion protein inhibits the development of proteinuria and prolongs survival of the animals.
identify TACI-Ig as a promising treatment of autoimmune disease in humans.

relevance_reason: Genome-wide linkage screen in SLE sib-pair families identifying susceptibility loci; supports mapping section.

findings.statement: Gaffney et al. (2000) performed a second complete genome screen in a new cohort of 82 SLE sib-pair families (Minnesota cohort 2). The four best intervals were 7p22 (lod score 2.87), 7q21 (lod score 2.40), 10p13 (lod score 2.24), and 7q36 (lod score 2.15); 8 additional intervals had lod scores of 1.00-1.67.
quotes: We now report the results of a second complete genome screen in a new cohort of 82 SLE sib-pair families.
In the cohort 2 screen, the four best intervals were 7p22 (LOD score 2.87), 7q21 (LOD score 2.40), 10p13 (LOD score 2.24), and 7q36 (LOD score 2.15).

findings.statement: In a combined analysis of Minnesota cohorts 1 and 2 (187 SLE sib-pair families), Gaffney et al. (2000) found significant linkage to markers in 6p11-p21 (D6S426, lod score 4.19) and 16q13 (D16S415, lod score 3.85). Three intervals (2p15, 7q36, and 1q42) had lod scores of 1.92-2.06, and 13 other intervals had lod scores of 1.00-1.78.
quotes: A combined analysis of MN cohorts 1 and 2 (187 sib-pair families) showed that markers in 6p11-p21 (D6S426, LOD score 4.19) and 16q13 (D16S415, LOD score 3.85) met the criteria for significant linkage.
Three intervals (2p15, 7q36, and 1q42) had LOD scores in the range 1.92-2.06, and another 13 intervals had LOD scores in the range of 1.00-1.78 in the combined sample.

relevance_reason: Genome scans in Icelandic and Swedish families with multiple SLE patients identified a new susceptibility locus for SLE at 2q37 (hSLE1).

findings.statement: Lindqvist et al. (2000) performed genome scans in families with multiple SLE patients from Iceland, a geographic and genetic isolate, and from Sweden. In the Icelandic families, 5 regions had lod scores greater than 2.0: 4p15-p13 (Z = 3.20), 9p22 (Z = 2.27), and 19q13 (Z = 2.06), which are homologous to the murine regions containing the lmb2, sle2, and sle3 loci, respectively; 19p13 (D19S247, Z = 2.58); and 2q37 (D2S125, Z = 2.06).
quotes: we performed genome scans in families with multiple SLE patients from Iceland, a geographical and genetic isolate, and from Sweden

In the Icelandic families, five regions showed lod scores greater than 2.0, three of which (4p15-13, Z=3.20; 9p22, Z=2.27; 19q13, Z=2.06) are homologous to the murine regions containing the lmb2, sle2 and sle3 loci, respectively.
The fourth region is located on 19p13 (D19S247, Z=2.58) and the fifth on 2q37 (D2S125, Z=2.06).

findings.statement: In Swedish families with multiple SLE patients, Lindqvist et al. (2000) found only 2 regions with lod scores above 2.0: 2q11 (D2S436, Z = 2.13) and 2q37 (D2S125, Z = 2.18). Combining the Icelandic and Swedish family sets gave a highly significant lod score of 4.24 at D2S125 in favor of linkage to 2q37, which the authors concluded represents a new SLE susceptibility locus (hSLE1).
quotes: Only two regions showed lod scores above 2.0 in the Swedish families: on chromosome 2q11 (D2S436, Z=2. 13) and 2q37 (D2S125, Z=2.18).
The combination of both family sets gave a highly significant lod score at D2S125 of Z=4.24 in favor of linkage for 2q37. This region represents a new locus for SLE.

relevance_reason: Pharmacokinetic study of CYP2D6 involvement in procainamide N-oxidation, relevant to drug-induced lupus; no SLE patients or SLE variants studied.

findings.statement: Lessard et al. (1999) studied 19 healthy individuals (13 CYP2D6 extensive metabolizers and 6 poor metabolizers) given a single 500-mg oral dose of procainamide, alone and with the CYP2D6 inhibitor quinidine. Urinary nitroprocainamide was measurable in 7 of 13 extensive metabolizers but in none of the poor metabolizers, and was undetectable in everyone during quinidine coadministration. The authors suggested that CYP2D6 is involved in the in vivo N-oxidation of procainamide, forming a metabolite potentially involved in procainamide-induced lupus. They noted that further studies were needed to show whether low CYP2D6 activity, whether genetic or caused by drugs, could prevent the drug-induced lupus syndrome.
