quotes: the urinary excretion of nitroprocainamide during period 1 was measurable in 7/13 extensive metabolizers but in none of the poor metabolizers
our results suggest that CYP2D6 is involved in the in-vivo aliphatic amine deethylation and N-oxidation of procainamide at its arylamine function in man
Further studies are needed to demonstrate whether a low CYP2D6 activity, either genetically determined or pharmacologically modulated, could prevent drug-induced lupus erythematosus syndrome

relevance_reason: Mouse model study showing that the lupus susceptibility loci Sle1 and Sle3 interact epistatically in NZM2410-derived congenic mice. It gives animal-model evidence about how lupus develops.

findings.statement: Mohan et al. (1999) studied the lupus nephritis susceptibility loci Sle1 and Sle3 from the NZM2410 mouse strain. Mice congenic for Sle1 alone (B6.NZMc1) lost tolerance to chromatin but did not develop pathogenic autoantibodies or disease. Mice congenic for Sle3 alone (B6.NZMc7) showed low-grade polyclonal B- and T-cell activation, elevated CD4/CD8 ratios, and mildly penetrant glomerulonephritis. In contrast, bicongenic B6.NZMc1|c7 mice carrying both loci had splenomegaly, expanded populations of activated B cells and CD4+ T cells, and a robust, varied IgG autoantibody response. The targets included chromatin components such as double-stranded DNA, intact glomeruli, and basement membrane matrix antigens. The bicongenic mice, especially the females, had highly penetrant glomerulonephritis.
quotes: Our previous work has shown that B6.NZMc1 mice, congenic for Sle1, exhibit loss of tolerance to chromatin but do not develop any pathogenic autoantibodies or disease.

findings.statement: Solomon et al. (1983) purified anti-native DNA antibodies from the serum of a patient with active SLE and used them to raise mouse monoclonal anti-idiotypic antibodies. One of these, 3I (IgG2a kappa), recognized an idiotypic determinant outside the antigen-binding site. In a solid-phase radioimmunoassay, 3I reacted with 8 of 9 sera that contained anti-native DNA activity. The authors suggested that anti-native DNA antibodies from unrelated SLE patients share a common idiotype.
quotes: Using hybridoma technology, we produced several mouse monoclonal antibodies directed against idiotypic determinants on these antinative DNA antibodies.
3I is not directed against the antigen binding site in that native DNA and 3I do not compete for binding to antinative DNA antibodies.

Eight of nine sera containing antinative DNA activity as determined by the Millipore filter assay reacted with 3I in a solid-phase radioimmunoassay. These findings suggest that antinative DNA antibodies from nonrelated patients with systemic lupus erythematosus share a common idiotype.

relevance_reason: Reports an HLA-DR4 association and a sex effect in susceptibility to drug-induced (hydralazine) SLE, and compares these patients with idiopathic SLE. This is relevant context for the heterogeneity and pathogenesis of SLE.

findings.statement: Batchelor et al. (1980) studied 26 patients with SLE induced by the antihypertensive drug hydralazine; 25 of the 26 were slow acetylators. HLA-DR4 frequency was 73% in hydralazine-induced SLE, significantly higher than in 113 healthy controls (33%), 16 slow-acetylator hypertensive patients treated with hydralazine for more than a year without developing SLE (25%), and 20 patients with idiopathic SLE (25%).
quotes: 25 of the 26 patients were slow acetylators.
The frequency of HLA-DR4 (73%) was significantly higher in the group with hydralazine-induced SLE than in the other groups (respectively 33%, 25%, and 25%).

findings.statement: Batchelor et al. (1980) found a 4:1 ratio of women to men among patients with hydralazine-induced SLE. When all slow acetylators treated with hydralazine were analysed together, every woman with DR4 developed SLE, and the only men who did were those with DR2 who were receiving 200 mg hydralazine per day.
quotes: The ratio of women to men affected was 4:1.
all women with DR4 developed hydralazine-induced SLE; the only men to do so were those with DR2 who were receiving 200 mg hydralazine per day.

findings.statement: Batchelor et al. (1980) found that the distribution of HLA-DR antigens in hydralazine-induced SLE differed significantly from that in idiopathic SLE. They concluded that this supports the view that the two syndromes are separate entities.
quotes: the distribution of DR antigens in the hydralazine-SLE patients was significantly different from that in the group with idiopathic SLE. This supports the view that the syndromes are separate entities.

relevance_reason: Epidemiologic study of SLE comparing New York City and Jefferson County, Alabama. Only the title is available, so the extractable content is limited to the study's scope.

findings.statement: Siegel et al. (1970) reported comparative epidemiologic data on systemic lupus erythematosus for New York City and Jefferson County, Alabama, covering 1956 to 1965.
quotes: Epidemiologic studies on systemic lupus erythematosus. Comparative data for New York City and Jefferson County, Alabama, 1956-1965.
findings.population: New York City and Jefferson County, Alabama, USA

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It shows the paper is a family study of thyroid disease and thyroid antibodies in relation to SLE, but no results are given.

findings.statement: Larsen and Godal (1972) studied thyroid diseases and thyroid antibodies in families of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, as part of a series of family studies in SLE.
quotes: Family studies in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). IX. Thyroid diseases and antibodies.

relevance_reason: The title reports a lupus-like illness in mothers of boys with chronic granulomatous disease. This is relevant to SLE as a phenotypic association, but only the title was available.

findings.statement: Schaller (1972) described an illness resembling lupus erythematosus in mothers of boys with chronic granulomatous disease.
quotes: Illness resembling lupus erythematosus in mothers of boys with chronic granulomatous disease.

relevance_reason: The title shows the paper reports familial occurrence of SLE, which supports a genetic contribution. Only the title was available, so no clinical or genetic details could be extracted.

findings.statement: First (1973) reported familial occurrence of systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: Familial systemic lupus erythematosus.

relevance_reason: Only the title was available. It reports lupus erythematosus together with hereditary angioedema in identical twin boys, which is relevant to complement deficiency and familial SLE.

findings.statement: Kohler et al. (1974) reported identical twin boys who had both hereditary angioedema and 'familial' lupus erythematosus.
quotes: Hereditary angioedema and "familial" lupus erythematosus in identical twin boys.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes a hereditary inflammatory vasculitis with persistent nodules, which the authors suggested was probably related to lupus erythematosus. This makes it relevant as context on familial forms related to SLE.

findings.statement: Reed et al. (1972) described a hereditary inflammatory vasculitis with persistent nodules. They regarded it as a new, genetically determined entity probably related to lupus erythematosus.
quotes: Hereditary inflammatory vasculitis with persistent nodules. A genetically-determined new entity probably related to lupus erythematosus.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It points to an epidemiologic study of SLE incidence, prevalence, outcome and first symptoms in the community, and it reports a high prevalence in black women.

findings.statement: Fessel (1974) studied the incidence, prevalence, outcome, and first symptoms of systemic lupus erythematosus in the community and found a high prevalence in black women.
quotes: Systemic lupus erythematosus in the community. Incidence, prevalence, outcome, and first symptoms; the high prevalence in black women.

relevance_reason: Only the title was available. It describes a family study of procainamide-induced systemic lupus erythematosus and raises the question of a pharmacogenetic polymorphism, which is relevant to drug-induced and genetic susceptibility to SLE.

findings.statement: Lappat and Cawein (1968) carried out a family study of procainamide-induced systemic lupus erythematosus. They asked whether a pharmacogenetic polymorphism might underlie susceptibility.
quotes: A familial study of procainamide-induced systemic lupus erythematosus. A question of pharmacogenetic polymorphism.

relevance_reason: The title shows this is a family study of SLE compared with rheumatoid arthritis, which bears on familial occurrence and inheritance of SLE. Only the title was available, so no results can be extracted.

findings.statement: Siegel et al. (1965) carried out a comparative family study of rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: A comparative family study of rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes family studies of SLE probands from central eastern Norway, which bears on familial occurrence and inheritance of SLE, but no data can be extracted.

findings.statement: Larsen (1972) reported family studies in systemic lupus erythematosus based on a group of probands from central eastern Norway.
quotes: Family studies in systemic lupus erythematosus. I. A proband material from central eastern Norway.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It points to a clinical paper on lupus erythematosus panniculitis (lupus profundus), a cutaneous form of lupus erythematosus. That adds clinical context to the SLE entry, but no patient details, genetics or numbers can be extracted.

findings.statement: Tuffanelli (1971) described lupus erythematosus panniculitis (lupus erythematosus profundus), a form of lupus erythematosus that involves the subcutaneous fat.
quotes: Lupus erythematosus panniculitis (profundus).

relevance_reason: Review of murine models of SLE, relevant to the animal model section; only the title was available, so very little can be extracted.

findings.statement: Theofilopoulos and Dixon (1985) reviewed murine models of systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: Murine models of systemic lupus erythematosus.

relevance_reason: Study of familial SLE kindreds showing that healthy relatives share an increased anti-DNA-associated cross-reactive idiotype; adds evidence that the disorder has a familial/genetic basis.

findings.statement: Halpern et al. (1985) used radioimmunoassay to test sera from 27 members of 3 kindreds with familial SLE for a cross-reactive idiotype found on anti-DNA antibodies, detected with the antiidiotype 3I. High-titered reactivity was present in 6 of 8 SLE patients and 15 of 19 family members. The authors concluded that expression of this idiotype was significantly increased in relatives of SLE patients and usually occurred without anti-DNA activity.
quotes: Sera of 27 members of 3 human kindreds with familial systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) were examined for expression of a cross-reactive idiotype present on anti-DNA antibodies of SLE patients.
By radioimmunoassay, serum samples from 6 of 8 SLE patients and 15 of 19 family members had high-titered reactivity with the antiidiotype, 3I.
This study indicates that expression of an idiotype associated with anti-DNA antibodies is significantly increased in relatives of SLE patients and usually occurs in the absence of anti-DNA activity.

findings.statement: In the familial SLE kindreds studied by Halpern et al. (1985), Millipore filter analysis found anti-DNA antibodies in 4 of 8 SLE patients and in 2 of 19 family members without SLE. Under conditions that dissociate immune complexes, anti-DNA antibodies were also found in 2 more patients and 2 more family members. On isoelectric focusing, cationic 3I-reactive bands (pH 7-8.5) correlated with the presence of anti-DNA antibodies, which the authors took to indicate that immunoglobulin charge may help determine specificity for DNA.
quotes: Millipore filter analysis revealed anti-DNA antibodies in sera of 4 of 8 SLE patients and 2 of 19 family members without SLE.
In 2 additional SLE patients and 2 additional family members, anti-DNA antibodies were revealed when sera were analyzed under conditions that dissociate immune complexes.
Cationic bands were found to correlate with the presence of anti-DNA antibodies, indicating that immunoglobulin charge may be a factor in determining specificity for DNA.

relevance_reason: Negative association/linkage study excluding the T cell receptor beta chain locus as an SLE susceptibility gene.

findings.statement: Fronek et al. (1986) examined genomic DNA restriction fragment length polymorphisms (RFLPs) of the T cell receptor beta chain gene in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, their relatives, and normal controls, and found a similar RFLP distribution in all groups. They suggested that the TCR beta chain genes are not coinherited with genes responsible for SLE.
quotes: The restriction fragment length polymorphism distribution was similar in systemic lupus erythematosus patients, their relatives, and normal controls.
Our observations suggest that these genes are not coinherited with genes responsible for systemic lupus erythematosus.

relevance_reason: Case-control study testing whether acetylator phenotype is associated with idiopathic SLE; the result was negative.

findings.statement: Baer et al. (1986) found that the slow acetylator phenotype was about as common in 64 patients with idiopathic SLE (38%) as in 60 healthy volunteers (50%) and 52 non-SLE medical service patients (44%). Slow acetylators were not more frequent in SLE subgroups defined by demographic features or by specific disease manifestations. The authors concluded that their results, like most previously published results, gave no evidence for an association between acetylator phenotype and idiopathic SLE.
quotes: We have observed that the frequency of the slow acetylator phenotype was similar in 64 patients with idiopathic SLE (38%), 60 healthy volunteers (50%), and 52 non-SLE medical service patients (44%).
The slow acetylator phenotype was not more frequent among subgroups of the SLE patients defined by demographic features or specific manifestations of disease.
Our results, as well as a majority of previously published results, do not provide evidence for an association between acetylator phenotype and idiopathic SLE.

relevance_reason: The study looks at lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin antibodies in 3 families with more than one member affected by SLE. It found the same lab abnormalities in healthy spouses, so the authors point to environmental or transmissible factors.

findings.statement: Mackie et al. (1987) studied 3 families in which more than one member had SLE or lupus-like disease. Of the 19 people studied, 11 had SLE or lupus-like disease. In 8 of these 11, the kaolin partial thromboplastin time (KPTT) was prolonged and there was other evidence of lupus anticoagulant. Only 5 of the 11 had high anticardiolipin antibody titers.
quotes: Three families having more than one affected member with SLE or lupus-like disease were investigated
Of the 19 persons, 11 had SLE or lupus-like disease. Eight of these 11 had a prolonged KPTT and other evidence of LA, while only 5/11 had high anticardiolipin titres.

findings.statement: Mackie et al. (1987) found a prolonged KPTT that did not correct on mixing in 4 healthy spouses of affected women and in 3 asymptomatic sibs. None of these 7 people had a history of bleeding or thrombosis, and their clotting factor levels were normal. The authors concluded that these findings would support the idea that transmissible agents or other environmental factors are involved in lupus-like disorders.
quotes: Four healthy spouses of affected females, and three asymptomatic siblings also had prolonged non-correctable KPTTs.
These persons had no bleeding or thrombotic history and normal clotting factor levels.
These findings would support a hypothesis of transmissible agents or other environmental factors being involved in lupus-like disorders.

findings.statement: Mackie et al. (1987) found that anticardiolipin levels were raised in subjects with lupus anticoagulant. However, the length of the KPTT did not correlate closely with the anticardiolipin titer.
quotes: Although anticardiolipin levels are raised in subjects with LA, there was no close correlation between length of KPTT and anticardiolipin titre.

relevance_reason: Statistical analysis of HLA-DR3 and C4 null allele associations with SLE, suggesting C4 null association is primary.

findings.statement: Green et al. (1986) used the empirical logistic method to analyze data, including the relevant genotypes, on the reported associations of SLE with HLA-DR3 and with null (QO) alleles at the C4A and C4B loci. The analysis suggested that the association with C4 null alleles was primary and that the DR3 association was likely secondary to it, which might help locate the HLA-linked disease susceptibility gene.
quotes: The reported associations between HLA antigen DR3 and null (QO) alleles at the C4A and C4B loci and systemic lupus erythematosus are here analysed.
The analysis suggests that the association with null alleles at the C4 loci is primary and the DR3 association is likely to be secondary to this.

relevance_reason: Describes excess lymphocyte low-molecular-weight DNA, which this SLE entry lists as an included title. The paper reports that the trait segregated as autosomal dominant in an SLE family.

findings.statement: Levcovitz et al. (1988) found that every SLE patient they studied had two classes of newly synthesized DNA in sucrose density gradients of PHA-stimulated lymphocytes. One was a large-molecular-weight fraction that comigrated with control DNA. The other was an excess low-molecular-weight DNA (LMW-DNA) fraction not seen in control lymphocytes. The excess LMW-DNA did not depend on disease activity or drug therapy.
quotes: All patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) demonstrated two classes of newly synthesized DNA in sucrose density gradients of PHA (phytohemagglutinin)-stimulated lymphocytes
an excess low-molecular-weight DNA (LMW-DNA) fraction not found in control lymphocytes
Excess LMW-DNA was independent of disease activity or drug therapy.

phenotypes.text: excess low-molecular-weight DNA in stimulated lymphocytes

findings.statement: Levcovitz et al. (1988) studied a four-generation family in which two first cousins had SLE. Excess lymphocyte LMW-DNA was present in both cousins, in their parents (who were siblings), in a common grandparent, in 4 of 9 siblings of one patient, and in 5 of 7 at-risk children. Every unaffected adult relative with the marker had positive antinuclear antibodies (ANAs) except the grandmother. None of the 5 children with excess LMW-DNA had positive ANAs.
quotes: LMW-DNA and serologic abnormalities were studied in a four-generation family in which two first cousins had SLE.
Excess LMW-DNA was found in the cousins with SLE, sibling parents of the SLE patients, a common grandparent, four of nine siblings of one patient, and five of seven at risk children.
All unaffected adult family members with the marker had positive antinuclear antibodies (ANAs) except the grandmother. However, none of the five children with excess LMW-DNA showed positive ANAs.

findings.statement: In the family studied by Levcovitz et al. (1988), excess LMW-DNA occurred in both males and females and was passed from male to male. The authors concluded that excess LMW-DNA in stimulated lymphocytes was inherited as an autosomal dominant trait in this family.
quotes: Both males and females had excess LMW-DNA. Male-male transmission was observed.
The expression of excess LMW-DNA in stimulated lymphocytes is inherited as an autosomal dominant genetic trait in this family.

findings.statement: Levcovitz et al. (1988) concluded that, in children of adults with excess LMW-DNA, the excess LMW-DNA appears before ANAs. They suggested it may be a predisposing factor in the development of the immunologic responses of SLE.
quotes: Excess LMW-DNA precedes the appearance of ANAs when found in children of adults with excess LMW-DNA, and may be a predisposing factor in the development of the immunologic responses of systemic lupus erythematosus.

relevance_reason: Negative linkage study excluding the T cell receptor alpha, beta and gamma genes as SLE susceptibility loci in multiplex families.

findings.statement: Wong et al. (1988) used Southern blot analysis of restriction fragment length polymorphisms (RFLPs) to study the T cell receptor (TcR) alpha, beta and gamma chain genes in 5 families with multiple members affected by SLE, 14 unrelated SLE patients and 14 normal controls. Polymorphic patterns were found with probes for all 3 TcR chains. However, the distribution of RFLP patterns did not differ significantly among patients, relatives and controls, and none of the 3 TcR genes cosegregated with the disease in families with at least 2 affected members. The authors concluded that the TcR alpha, beta and gamma chain genes are not likely to be linked to genes related to SLE.
quotes: genomic DNA restriction fragment length polymorphisms were studied, using the Southern blot technique, in 5 families with multiple members with SLE, 14 unrelated SLE patients, and 14 normal controls
in the families with at least 2 individuals with the disease, each of the 3 TcR chain genes did not cosegregate with the disease
We conclude that TcR alpha, beta, and gamma chain genes are not likely to be linked to genes related to SLE.

relevance_reason: Family study showing immune abnormalities (impaired IL-2 activity, increased Ig-secreting B cells) in healthy relatives of SLE probands, supporting genetic control of SLE-associated immune defects.

findings.statement: Sakane et al. (1989) studied 34 clinically healthy family members of 6 SLE probands using a phytohemagglutinin-induced IL-2 activity assay (T-cell function) and a spontaneous plaque-forming cell assay (B-cell function). Impaired IL-2 activity was found in 15 of 29 blood relatives but in none of 5 nonconsanguineous household members, and was unrelated to household status, leading the authors to conclude that impaired IL-2 activity strongly correlates with a genetic relationship.
quotes: in 34 clinically healthy family members of six SLE probands

Impaired IL-2 activity was found in 15 of the 29 consanguineous relatives. There was no relation between the household relatives and the nonhousehold relatives; none of the five nonconsanguineous household persons had abnormal results.
The findings indicate that the impaired IL-2 activity in relatives appears to strongly correlate with a genetic relationship.

findings.statement: Sakane et al. (1989) found abnormal spontaneous B-cell immunoglobulin secretion (plaque-forming cell assay) in 22 of 29 blood relatives of SLE probands, more commonly in consanguineous household relatives, but also in 4 of 5 nonconsanguineous household members. They concluded that although the evidence favored a genetic basis for the B-cell abnormalities, environmental effects may also contribute to their familial occurrence.
quotes: Results for the B-cell assay were abnormal in 22 of the 29 consanguineous relatives.
four of the five nonconsanguineous household relatives also had abnormal assay results.
Although the evidence favors a genetic basis for the B-cell abnormalities, environmental effects may also contribute to the familial occurrence of these abnormalities.

phenotypes.text: increased peripheral blood B cells actively secreting immunoglobulins

relevance_reason: Describes a subset of SLE patients with an inherited T4 (CD4) epitope-deficient phenotype, with family studies and immunologic findings.

findings.statement: Stohl et al. (1985) described 3 black Jamaican patients with SLE whose T helper/inducer cells lacked the T4 epitope (T4 epitope-deficient phenotype). All 3 patients had lymphadenopathy. The asymptomatic, otherwise healthy T4 epitope-deficient brother of one patient also had lymphadenopathy in the same distribution as his sister with SLE.
quotes: Three black Jamaicans with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) were identified whose T helper/inducer cells lacked the T4 epitope (T4 epitope-deficient phenotype). All three patients had lymphadenopathy as part of their syndromes.
The asymptomatic and otherwise healthy T4 epitope-deficient brother of one of these patients also had lymphadenopathy in a distribution identical to that of his sister with SLE.

findings.statement: Family studies by Stohl et al. (1985) indicated autosomal codominant inheritance of the T4 epitope phenotype, not linked to the HLA locus.
quotes: Family studies pointed to an autosomal codominant mode of inheritance not linked to the HLA locus for the T4 epitope phenotype.

findings.statement: Stohl et al. (1985) found that peripheral blood mononuclear cells from T4 epitope-deficient family members showed impaired B-cell differentiation after pokeweed mitogen stimulation compared with cells from T4 epitope-intermediate relatives. Helper/suppressor T-cell ratios, autoantibodies, mitogen proliferation, and mixed lymphocyte reactions did not correlate with T4 epitope phenotype. The authors suggested that SLE with the T4 epitope-deficient phenotype may be a distinct subset of SLE.
quotes: Cultures of peripheral-blood mononuclear cells revealed impaired B-cell differentiation upon stimulation with pokeweed mitogen in cells originating from the T4 epitope-deficient family members as compared with those originating from their T4 epitope-intermediate relatives.
We suggest that SLE in association with the T4 epitope-deficient phenotype may represent a unique subset of patients with SLE that has distinct clinical and immunologic properties.

relevance_reason: Population-based study of homozygous C4A deficiency frequency and its clinical correlates in SLE patients; adds evidence on C4A deficiency as an SLE susceptibility factor.

findings.statement: Sturfelt et al. (1990) found homozygous C4A deficiency in 16% (13 of 80) of SLE patients. The patients were all diagnosed cases ascertained from a defined population in southern Sweden, which the authors said minimized patient selection bias.
quotes: Homozygous C4A deficiency was found at a prevalence of 16% (13/80 patients) in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
The patients represented all diagnosed cases retrieved from a defined population in Southern Sweden, which minimizes the influence of patient selection.

findings.statement: Sturfelt et al. (1990) found that photosensitivity was more common in SLE patients with C4A deficiency than in other SLE patients (p less than 0.05). Other clinical features were similar between the groups, and the authors found no differences in anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, anti-RNP, anti-SSA, anti-SSB, rheumatoid factor or anticardiolipin antibodies. They noted that the increased photosensitivity partly resembled findings in patients with complete deficiencies of classical pathway components.
quotes: Photosensitivity was more common among C4A-deficient patients than among other SLE patients (p less than 0.05). Otherwise, clinical features were similar in the two groups.
In addition, no differences were found with regard to presence of various autoantibodies (anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, anti-RNP, anti-SSA, anti-SSB, rheumatoid factors and anti-cardiolipin).
The increased photosensitivity of C4A-deficient patients partly resembles the findings in patients with complete deficiencies of classical pathway components.

findings.statement: Sturfelt et al. (1990) found that in SLE patients expressing both C4A and C4B isotypes, plasma C4B/C4A quotients stayed fairly stable regardless of disease activity. The authors said this argued against preferential breakdown of either isotype during complement activation in SLE.
quotes: In patients expressing both C4A and C4B isotypes, C4B/C4A quotients were fairly stable in plasma irrespective of disease activity. This argues against preferential break-down of either isotype during complement activation in the disease.

relevance_reason: Twin study showing high monozygotic concordance for SLE, supporting a genetic component.

findings.statement: Block et al. (1975) studied 12 twin pairs in which one or both twins had SLE (7 definitely monozygotic, 3 definitely dizygotic) and compared them with 17 previously described twin pairs (12 definitely monozygotic). Four of 7 (57%) definitely monozygotic pairs were clinically concordant for SLE by ARA preliminary criteria, and concordance for antinuclear factor and hypergammaglobulinemia was 71% and 87%, respectively, closely agreeing with the 12 previously described monozygotic sets.
quotes: 12 twon pairs (seven definitely monozygotic, three definitely dizygotic) of which one or both twins had SLE, were studied and compared to 17 twin pairs (12 definitely monozygotic) previously described
four of seven (57 per cent) definitely monozygotic pairs were clinically concordant for SLE, satisfying the preliminary criteria of the American Rheumatism Association (ARA)
These data closely agree with those on the 12 definitely monozygotic sets previously described.

findings.statement: Block et al. (1975) found that all 3 dizygotic twin sets in their series were discordant for clinical SLE, although one clinically well twin had marked serologic abnormalities. Comparison with data from other first-degree relatives suggested to the authors a strong genetic component in the pathogenesis of SLE, with nongenetic and environmental factors also contributing to disease expression.
quotes: All three of the dizygotic sets in the present series were discordant for clinical SLE, although one clinically well twin had marked serologic abnormalities.
Comparison of these data with thos from other first degree relatives of out twins clearly suggests a strong genetic component in the pathogenesis of SLE.

relevance_reason: Serologic family study of anti-nucleic acid and lymphocytotoxic antibodies in SLE probands and relatives. It bears on whether SLE is caused by genes, environment or both.

findings.statement: DeHoratius et al. (1975) found anti-RNA antibodies in 82% of 28 SLE probands, 16% of 124 of their family members, and 5% of 76 control family members. Among SLE family members, the antibodies were found only in the 94 close household contacts of the probands, 21% of whom had them. Anti-native DNA antibodies were present in 68% of probands and 6% of close household contacts, compared with 1% in control families; the difference between household contacts and controls was not significant.
quotes: Anti-RNA antibodies were found in 82% of 28 systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) probands and in 16% of 124 of their family members. The incidence in 76 control family members was only 5%.
In the SLE family members, the antibodies were found exclusively in 21% of the 94 close household contacts of the probands.
The incidence of anti-nDNA antibodies in close household contacts of the probands was 6%, which was not significantly different from the 1% incidence found in control families.

findings.statement: DeHoratius et al. (1975) found lymphocytotoxic antibodies in 57% of SLE family members overall and in 68% of close household contacts. In probands, these antibodies correlated with anti-single-stranded RNA (poly A) and anti-nDNA antibodies; in household contacts, they correlated with anti-double-stranded RNA (poly A-poly U) antibodies. Anti-RNA antibodies occurred in consanguineous household contacts but not in nonconsanguineous ones. The authors concluded that this supported the hypothesis that both an environmental agent, possibly a virus, and the genetic response are important in the pathogenesis of SLE.
quotes: Lymphocytotoxic antibodies occurred in 57% of the SLE family members as a whole and in 68% of the close household contacts.
The anti-RNA antibodies were present in consanguineous household contacts but not in nonconsanguineous household contacts.
These findings strengthen the hypothesis that both an environmental agent, possibly a virus, as well as the genetic response are important in the pathogenesis of SLE.

relevance_reason: Clinical study of familial SLE showing evidence for both genetic and environmental influences; relevant to the inheritance and clinical sections of the SLE entry.

findings.statement: Arnett and Shulman (1976) studied 8 families with familial SLE. Combining these with 1 deceased pair and 31 families from the literature gave 8 pairs of identical twins, 1 pair of non-identical twins, 16 sibling combinations and 15 parent-offspring combinations. Of these, 53 cases in 25 families had enough documentation for detailed analysis. The authors compared 23 clinical and laboratory features between affected relatives and against matched non-related SLE controls. They found impressive concordance for disease expression between identical twins and between parents and offspring, but not between siblings or controls. They concluded that this supported genetic influences on how SLE is expressed.
quotes: These families, plus one deceased pair and 31 described in the literature consisted of 8 pairs of identical twins, one pair of non-identical twins, and 16 sibling and 15 parent-offspring combinations.
Impressive concordance for disease expression was found between pairs of identical twins and between parent and offspring. No such concordance was found between siblings and controls.
These findings support genetic influences in the expression of SLE in identical twins and parents and offspring pairs.

findings.statement: Arnett and Shulman (1976) found 4 father-offspring pairs among families with familial SLE. They stated that this made it less likely that SLE is transmitted during the perinatal period.
quotes: The finding of four father-offspring pairs lessens the possibility that SLE is transmitted during the perinatal period.

findings.statement: Arnett and Shulman (1976) found that SLE began in each member of an identical twin pair within an average of 2 years of each other. Between siblings, the average difference in age at onset was 9 years, but the average difference in actual calendar date of onset was only 3 years. For parents and offspring, the corresponding figures were 20 and 8 years. The authors suggested that environmental influences play a role in starting SLE, especially in siblings.
quotes: The onset of SLE in each of identical twins occurred within an average of 2 years.
In siblings, however, while the average difference in age at onset was 9 years, the average difference in time of onset (actual date) was only 3 years.
These data suggest environmental influences in the initiation of SLE, especially in siblings.

findings.statement: Arnett and Shulman (1976) found no real differences in the frequencies of clinical and laboratory features between familial and non-familial SLE. They concluded that familial SLE is probably not a different disease entity from non-familial SLE.
quotes: Comparison of the frequencies of clinical and laboratory attributes in the familial group as opposed to non-familial groups showed no real differences.
Thus, familial SLE is probably not a different disease entity from non-familial SLE.

findings.statement: Arnett and Shulman (1976) studied 27 unaffected first-degree relatives in their 8 families. Two sisters had thyroid disease, persistent leukopenia and a raised sedimentation rate. Their mother had SLE and Hashimoto thyroiditis, and their sibling had SLE. The other 25 relatives were normal clinically, hematologically, biochemically and serologically.
quotes: Studies of 27 unaffected first-degree relatives in our eight families revealed two sisters with thyroid disease, persistent leukopenia and sedimentation rate elevation.
They were daughters of a patient with SLE and Hashimoto's thyroiditis and sisters of a patient with SLE.
The remaining 25 relatives were clinically, hematologically, biochemically, and serologically normal.

phenotypes.text: Hashimoto thyroiditis in mother with SLE

relevance_reason: Mouse model genetic study of lupus nephritis in NZB x NZW F1 hybrids; identifies number of contributing genes and H-2 linkage. Relevant as an animal model for SLE.

findings.statement: Knight and Adams (1978) studied the incidence of early severe lupus nephritis, identified by antemortem determination of renal function, in 230 (NZB x NZW) x NZW backcross mice and 150 (NZB x NZW) x NZB backcross mice. The data indicated that the NZB strain contributes only 1 gene and the NZW strain contributes 2 genes, or clusters of closely linked genes, to the renal disorder of the F1 hybrid; neither parental inbred strain shows the disorder. All 3 genes were concluded to be dominant or codominant, as their effect is expressed in the heterozygous state.
quotes: The data indicate that the NZB strain contributes only one gene and the NZW strain contributes two genes, or clusters of closely linked genes, to the renal disorder of the F1 hybrid.
All three genes must be dominant or codominant, as their effect is expressed in the heterozygous state.
we have studied the incidence of the renal disease in 230 (NZB x NZW) x NZW backcross mice (an earlier study) and, in this study, in 150 (NZB x NZW) x NZB backcross mice

findings.statement: In (NZB x NZW) backcross mice, Knight and Adams (1978) found that 1 of the 2 NZW-derived genes contributing to lupus nephritis was linked to the H-2 (major histocompatibility) complex.
quotes: One of the NZW genes was found to be linked to the H-2 complex.

relevance_reason: The abstract describes familial lupus erythematosus: a mother with discoid lupus whose child developed discoid lupus lesions in infancy. This adds a familial case to the SLE entry, but the paper reports no genetic data.

findings.statement: Brustein et al. (1977) reported familial lupus erythematosus. A woman had discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE), and her child developed DLE lesions at 2 months of age. The original lesions persisted and new lesions kept appearing up to the time of the report, when the child was 28 months old. In a second child, then 11 months old, a probable lupus erythematosus rash developed at 1 week of age.

findings.statement: Serdula and Rhoads (1979) surveyed SLE patients in civilian general hospitals on Oahu, Hawaii, for 1970-1975 and ascertained 168 cases, 107 considered definite. Age-adjusted prevalence rates per 100,000 for definite cases at the end of 1975 were 5.8 in whites, 24.1 in Chinese, 19.9 in Filipinos, 20.4 in part-Hawaiians, and 18.2 in Japanese. Females made up about 90% of definite cases overall, with a heavy female preponderance in each ethnic group.

findings.statement: Miller and Schwartz (1979) found abnormal suppressor-cell activity in 13 clinically healthy first-degree relatives of SLE patients, 12 of whom were women, with no correlation between assay results and lymphocytotoxic antibodies in relatives. They concluded that impaired suppressor-cell function cannot by itself explain SLE pathogenesis, that certain suppressor-cell abnormalities are genetic markers, and proposed that development of SLE requires participation of at least two functionally distinct classes of genes.

relevance_reason: Case report of monozygotic twins discordant for SLE. It suggests a hormonal (ovarian) role in getting the disease, which adds context on nongenetic factors and incomplete concordance.

findings.statement: Yocum et al. (1975) studied a pair of monozygotic twins discordant for SLE. Both twins had biologically false-positive serologic tests for syphilis at an early age, but only one developed SLE. The twins did not differ in their immune responses to tetanus toxoid, keyhole limpet hemocyanin, or DNCB, in delayed sensitivity, or in antibody titers to viruses.
